- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-27
- **kind:** Notification
- **exact title:** Section 42(1) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 - Change in Daily Minimum Cash Reserve Maintenance Requirement
- **reference number:** RBI/2026-27/310 ; R.RET.REC.262/12.01.001/2026-27 ; R.RET.REC.247/12.01.001/2026-27
- **addressed to / applies to:** All Scheduled Banks,
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13759&Mode=0
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/notification/PDFs/310NTFF0FFDF6AF554020849CBE9D36E4E36E.PDF
- **local text file name:** RBI-N13759.txt

```text
(223 kb) | 
Section 42(1) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 - Change in Daily Minimum Cash Reserve Maintenance Requirement | 
 RBI/2026-27/310 
DoR.RET.REC.262/12.01.001/2026-27
 November 27, 2026
 All Scheduled Banks,
 Madam / Sir,
 Section 42(1) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 - Change in Daily Minimum Cash Reserve Maintenance Requirement
 Please refer to our circular DoR.RET.REC.247/12.01.001/2026-27 dated October 09, 2026 on the captioned subject.
 2. On the basis of an assessment of the current and evolving macroeconomic situation and liquidity conditions, it has been decided to reduce the minimum daily maintenance of the cash reserve ratio (CRR) from 99 per cent of the requirement to 90 per cent effective from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026.
 Yours faithfully,
 (J P Sharma)
 Chief General Manager-in-Charge
 | 

 |
```

## [rbi] 2026-11-27 | Thirty First Meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to Review the Flow of Credit to the MSME Sector in Kolkata on November 27, 2026

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-27
- **kind:** Press release
- **exact title:** Thirty First Meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to Review the Flow of Credit to the MSME Sector in Kolkata on November 27, 2026
- **reference number:** Press Release: 2026-2027/1581
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64059
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/PR1581EF13886A07594B4C9D37BD7039DCBA6C.PDF
- **local text file name:** RBI-PR64059.txt

```text
(294 kb) | 
 Date : Nov 27, 2026 | 
Thirty First Meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to Review the Flow of Credit to the MSME Sector in Kolkata on November 27, 2026 | 
 The 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to review the flow of credit to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) was held in Kolkata on November 27, 2026. Shri Swaminathan J, Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of India (RBI), chaired the meeting. Participants included the Additional Secretary and Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, and the Joint Secretary, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance. Managing directors and executive directors of select banks, heads of SIDBI, NABARD, CGTMSE, NCGTC and KVIC, the Chief Executive Officer of the Indian Banks’ Association, and representatives of national, regional and state-level MSME associations also attended.
 Recognising MSMEs’ contribution to India’s economy and development goals, the Deputy Governor urged banks to expedite credit sanctions and reduce reliance on collateral through cash-flow-based lending using ULI and other digital channels. He called for greater use of TReDS for receivables financing and early identification and resolution of stress. He invited industry associations to actively participate in outreach events such as RBI’s town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings to improve awareness and raise their members’ concerns with banks.
 The Committee reviewed working capital and investment credit to MSMEs, lending to first-time borrowers and credit guarantee coverage. It also discussed the higher limit for collateral-free lending to micro and small enterprises, settlement of CPSE invoices through TReDS and key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026.
 (Brij Raj) 
 Chief General Manager
 Press Release: 2026-2027/1581
 | 

 |
```

```text
(222 kb) | 
Implementation of Section 51A of UAPA, 1967: Updates to UNSC’s 1267/ 1989 ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List: Amendment of 81 entries | 
 RBI/2026-27/308
 DoR.AML.REC.260/14.06.001/2026-27
 November 26, 2026
 The Chairpersons/ CEOs of the Commercial Banks, 
Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, Urban Co-operative Banks, 
Rural Co-operative Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Local Area Banks, 
Non-Banking Financial Companies, Asset Reconstruction Companies, 
All India Financial Institutions
 Madam/Dear Sir
 Implementation of Section 51A of UAPA, 1967: Updates to UNSC’s 1267/ 1989 ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List: Amendment of 81 entries
 Please refer to Chapter IX on “Requirements/obligations under International Agreements - Communications from International Agencies” of the Reserve Bank of India - Know Your Customer, Directions, 2025 dated November 28, 2025 (amended time to time) (“Directions”), as applicable, as per which, regulated entity shall ensure that in terms of section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) (UAPA) Act, 1967 and amendments thereto, it does not have any account in the name of individuals / entities appearing in the lists of individuals and entities, suspected of having terrorist links, which are approved by and periodically circulated by the United Nations Security Council (UNSC).
 2. In this connection, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Government of India has informed about the UNSC press release SC/16516, dated November 20, 2026 wherein the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) Committee has amended the entries below on the ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List of individuals and entities subject to the assets freeze, travel ban and arms embargo set out in paragraph 1 of Security Council resolution 2734 (2024) following the 2025 Annual Review conducted in accordance with paragraphs 92-95 of resolution 2734 (2024).

3. Press release dated November 20, 2026, regarding the above can be found at https://press.un.org/en/2026/sc16516.doc.htm

5. In view of the above, regulated entities are advised to take appropriate action in terms of Chapter IX of the aforementioned Directions and strictly follow the procedure as laid down in the UAPA Order dated February 02, 2021 (amended on April 22, 2024) annexed to the Directions.
6. Updated lists of individuals and entities linked to ISIL (Da'esh), Al-Qaida and Taliban are available at:

Further, as per the instructions from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), any request for de-listing received by any bank is to be forwarded electronically to Joint Secretary (CTCR), MHA for consideration. More details are available at the following URL: https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/ombudsperson/application
8. Regulated entities are advised to take note of the aforementioned UNSC communication and ensure meticulous compliance.
Yours faithfully
```

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-23
- **kind:** Draft for comments
- **exact title:** DRAFT: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/bs_viewcontent.aspx?Id=5221
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/Content/PDFs/CBSAFEGUARD23112026CC6EED0FD7774A43B334ACE6A850BCBC.PDF
- **comment deadline (drafts):** December 14, 2026
- **local text file name:** RBI-DRAFT5221.txt
- **note:** Draft released with RBI press release prid=64026; date and comment deadline are from that press release.

```text
Draft - Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 | 
 DoR.MCS.REC.No. /01-01-032/2026-27
 XXXX XX, 2026
 Draft Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026
 The Reserve Bank had issued the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 dated June 24, 2026 on ‘Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’, which, inter alia, strengthened the existing framework for limiting liability of customers in unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs). While the revised framework primarily addresses customer liability in the event of fraudulent EBTs, a need is felt to further strengthen the same from a preventive perspective by providing customers with greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels are used. Accordingly, based on the public feedback received on the Discussion Paper ‘Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds’ dated April 09, 2026, it has been decided to issue directions on customer-induced controls and an additional layer of authentication through a Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM). Further, on a review to bring uniformity in practices adopted by banks and ensure that customers are protected against specific acts of omission or commission on part of the banks, it has been decided to expand the scope of the definition of ‘negligence by a bank’ specified in the aforementioned Amendment Directions.
 Accordingly, these directions are issued to all Commercial Banks (other than Small Finance Banks, Payments Banks, Regional Rural Banks, and Local Area Banks) (hereinafter referred to collectively as “banks” and individually as a “bank”) under the Reserve Bank’s Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025.
 2. In exercise of the powers conferred by section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act,1949, the Reserve Bank, being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in public interest so to do, hereby issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified.
 3. Short Title and Commencement
 (1) These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026.
 (2) These Directions shall come into effect from July 1, 2027, or on such earlier date as a bank may decide to implement, except the provisions contained in clauses (i) to (vi), (ix) and (x) of sub-paragraph 4(20B) specified below which shall come into effect from January 1, 2027.
 4. These Amendment Directions shall substitute the definition of ‘negligence by a bank’ prescribed in the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 as under:
 “4(20B) Negligence by a bank means any act of omission or commission on part of the bank which results in or contributes to the occurrence of a fraudulent electronic banking transaction in a customer account, including the following:
 (i) not implementing instructions related to factors of authentication for EBTs, as prescribed under Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025;
 (ii) not implementing multi factor authentication for creation of new account linkages (addition / modification / deletion of beneficiaries), change in account details or revision to fund transfer limits, as prescribed under paragraph 46 of Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls) Directions, 2026;
 (iii) not sending mandatory alert for an EBT, as prescribed under paragraph 76D of these Directions;
 (iv) not providing 24x7 channels for reporting of fraudulent EBTs or loss of debit / credit card, as prescribed under paragraph 76G of these Directions;
 (v) not acting promptly upon a customer notification regarding fraudulent EBT(s) or loss of debit / credit card, as prescribed under paragraph 76J of these Directions;
 (vi) not blocking the digital payment channel and / or notifying the customer consequent to the maximum number of failed login or authentication attempts, where such failure contributed to the fraudulent EBT, as prescribed under paragraphs 50 and 51 of Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls) Directions, 2026);
 (vii) not providing the facility of mandatory customer-induced controls or not implementing the controls for EBTs as set by the customer, as prescribed under these Directions;
 (viii) not providing Trusted Person Mechanism or failing to implement the directions with respect to the mechanism, as prescribed under these Directions;
 (ix) a system malfunction or security breach at the bank’s end, which facilitates or results in a fraudulent EBT; and
 (x) collusion or connivance of an employee of the bank or any third party engaged by the bank, which facilitates or results in a fraudulent EBT.”
 5. These Amendment Directions shall modify the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the Directions) as under:
 (1) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(9), namely:
 “4(9A) Customer-induced Control means a customer-configurable restriction, limit, lock, safeguard or permission applicable to the customer’s account.”
 (2) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(10.1A), namely:
 “4(10.1B) Digital Payment Channel means any electronic interface, device, network or set of procedures provided by a bank, through which a customer can undertake a digital payment transaction / electronic banking transaction.”
 (3) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(19), namely:
 “4(19A) Merchant shall have the same meaning as defined in the Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA).”
 (4) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(24), namely:
 “4(24.1A) Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI) shall have the same meaning as defined in the Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs).”
 (5) In paragraph 4, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(25A), namely:
 “4(25B) Stop Switch means a facility through which a customer can disable all customer initiated future debits associated with her / his account(s) as per these Directions.”
 (6) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(26A), namely:
 “4(26AA) Trusted Person means a natural person aged 18 years or above, registered by a bank’s customer, to act as an additional factor of authentication as per these Directions.”
 (7) In Chapter IV on ‘Customer Guidance and Protection’ of the Directions, in the section ‘DA. Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’, the following sub-sections and paragraphs shall be inserted after the sub-section ‘DA.2 Alerts for EBTs’, namely:
 “DA.2A. Preventive Safeguards for EBTs
 DA.2A.1 Customer-induced controls for EBTs
 DA.2A.1.1 Customer-induced controls for digital payment channels other than cards
 76FA. A bank shall provide all its customers with the facility to disable one or more digital payment channels linked to their account, and to subsequently re-enable such channel through the physical or digital interfaces of the bank, in accordance with the procedure specified in paragraphs 76FI and 76FJ hereunder.
 76FB. Where a digital payment channel has been disabled by the customer, no customer-initiated debit transaction shall be permitted through that channel until it is re-enabled.
 76FC. In addition, a bank shall provide the following controls to its customers, which may be exercised by them at their option:
 (1) to set or modify a maximum amount limit per transaction, per beneficiary or for the transactions in aggregate in a day that may be undertaken through a digital payment channel, within the overall limits otherwise applicable to that channel;
 Illustration 1: Beneficiary level limit – A customer sets a maximum limit of ₹20,000 per day for payments to a particular beneficiary. Even if the limit for the digital payment channel set by the payment system operator / the bank permits a higher amount, transactions to that particular beneficiary cannot exceed ₹20,000 per day.
 Illustration 2: Transaction amount limit – A customer sets a maximum limit of ₹10,000 per transaction for a particular digital payment channel. Any transaction above ₹10,000 through that digital payment channel would not be permitted.
 Illustration 3: Daily limit – A customer sets an overall daily limit of ₹50,000 for transactions done through a particular digital payment channel, even though the payment systems operator or the bank permits a higher limit. Any transaction above the daily limit would not be permitted through that digital payment channel.
 (2) to set or modify, a maximum limit for the transactions that may be undertaken in a day, through all the available digital payment channels taken together;
 (3) to set a time window during which one or more digital payment channels linked to the customer’s account shall remain disabled; and
 (4) any other control introduced by the bank over and above the controls prescribed at 76FC (1) to 76FC (3) above, which may further strengthen customer options to safeguard their EBTs.
 DA.2A.1.2 Customer-induced controls for cards (Debit, Credit, and Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPI) Card))
 76FD. A bank shall provide to all its cardholders the facility to switch on / off and set / modify transaction limits (within the overall card limit, if any, set by the issuer) for all types of transactions – domestic or international; at Point of Sale (PoS) / ATMs / online transactions / contactless transactions, etc.
 76FE. The card-specific directions are not applicable to Gift PPI cards and Transit PPI Cards.
 DA.2A.1.3 Stop Switch facility in customer accounts
 76FF. A bank shall provide its customers with a Stop Switch facility for immediate disablement of all outward future debits associated with her / his account(s). However, any debits due to ongoing recurring payment mandates and standing instructions, and marking of lien or debits initiated by the bank to recover due charges, loan instalment, etc., shall be excluded from the scope of Stop Switch.
 76FG. Upon activation of the Stop Switch, no customer-initiated debit transaction, creation of new payment mandates, setting up of new standing instructions or registration of UPI on new third-party payment applications shall be permitted in the account.
 76FH. The activation of a customer-induced control or Stop Switch shall however not affect any inward credits into the customer’s account.
 DA.2A.1.4 Re-enablement of digital payment channels or Deactivation of Stop Switch
 76FI. A bank shall provide customers the facility to re-enable digital payment channels or deactivate the Stop Switch to re-enable operations in the customer’s account, subject to customer authentication. A bank shall ensure that any request for re-enablement is subject to, at the minimum, the authentication requirements prescribed under the Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The authentication for such requests shall be at least as stringent as those applied while enabling the corresponding digital payment channel and may be enhanced based on the bank’s risk assessment laid down in its policy.
 76FJ. Based on its risk assessment, a bank shall impose a reasonable cooling period or other risk mitigation measures, before giving effect to such re-enablement requests.
 DA.2A.1.5 Default controls and other aspects
 76FK. A bank shall keep all digital payment channels disabled by default at the time of customer onboarding. Such channels shall be enabled only upon an explicit consent from the customer and after complying with the applicable authentication requirements.
 76FL. Notwithstanding the above,
 (1) in case of cards -
 (i) at the time of their issue, all cards (physical and virtual) shall be enabled for use only at contact-based points of usage (viz. ATMs and Point of Sale (PoS) devices) within India.
 (ii) at the time of their re-issue, the existing card controls shall be mapped to re-issued cards.
 (iii) forex prepaid cards shall be enabled for both contact, and contactless points of usage outside India at the time of their issue / re-issue.
 (2) in case of other digital payment channels, where a bank has enabled a particular channel for a customer at the time of customer onboarding or subsequently, it shall specify a ceiling on the aggregate value of fund transfers that the customer can undertake across the channel over the initial period of 24 hours, based on the bank's risk assessment. After the initial period of 24 hours, the bank may provide for gradual enhancements to the ceiling, based on its channel risk assessment and internal policy. The bank shall allow modification of the initial or enhanced ceiling (if implemented) through the exercise of customer controls provided at paragraph 76FC above and subject to compliance with the applicable authentication requirements. However, such modification shall be allowed only after the initial period of 24 hours has lapsed post activation of the digital payment channel.
 76FM. The facilities for activation, modification and deactivation of customer-induced controls and Stop Switch shall be made available to all customers through the available points of customer interface such as branches, ATMs, internet banking, mobile banking, Interactive Voice Response (IVR), etc.
 76FN. Upon any activation, modification, deactivation or re-activation of any of such facilities, a bank shall immediately notify the customers through the available channels of communication, including but not limited to SMS and e-mail.
 76FO. A bank shall maintain tamper proof audit logs of controls and the Stop Switch initiated by customers to facilitate review and resolution of disputes.
 76FP. A bank shall undertake outreach efforts on an ongoing basis to inform customers regarding availability of the customer-induced controls and Stop Switch facility and attendant aspects such as process to activate or deactivate the same, implications of the activation, etc.
 DA.2A.2 Authentication through Trusted Person Mechanism
 DA.2A.2.1 Applicability
 76FQ. A bank shall put in place a mechanism, called the Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM), to enable customers to register a trusted person to act as an additional factor of transaction authentication. The TPM shall apply to electronic fund transfers initiated through the physical and digital channels available under such customer’s account beyond the threshold set by the customer, except for transactions initiated for:
 (1) payments made through the UPI channel linked to the customer’s account;
 (2) merchant payments, irrespective of the payment channel or instrument used; and
 (3) recurring payments through standing instructions, e-mandates or NACH mandates.
 76FR. A bank shall offer the TPM to all its customers, whose availment shall be entirely voluntary, based on explicit requests of the customer and the trusted person, and are subject to the thresholds put in place by the customer.
 76FS. The TPM shall be available in bank accounts operated by individuals solely or in such joint accounts operated under any of the survivorship clauses.
 DA.2A.2.2 Registration and onboarding of trusted person
 76FT. A bank shall facilitate, through its physical and digital channels, the registration of a trusted person, activation of the TPM, and configuration of related transaction-level thresholds by customers.
 76FU. For registering a trusted person, a bank shall:
 (1) obtain the trusted person’s name, mobile number, email address and copy of at least one Officially Valid Document (OVD);
 (2) verify the identity and eligibility of the trusted person on the basis of the OVD and such other information or documentation as may be reasonably required; and
 (3) verify the mobile number and email address of the trusted person through an appropriate authentication mechanism.
 76FV. The mobile number registered for the trusted person shall be distinct from the mobile number linked to the customer’s account.
 76FW. A bank, while obtaining the consent for TPM registration, shall clearly inform the customer and the trusted person that registration under the mechanism:
 (1) does not confer upon the trusted person the status of a joint account holder, nominee, mandate holder or authorised signatory;
 (2) does not grant the trusted person any right, title or beneficial interest in the account;
 (3) does not authorise the trusted person to independently access or operate the account, initiate any transaction, or otherwise issue instructions in relation to the account;
 (4) does not result in the trusted person incurring any financial liability when she / he approves or rejects a transaction; and
 (5) requires the trusted person to authenticate or reject the transaction within the time window prescribed by the bank and in a manner compliant with paragraph 76FZ ibid.
 76FX. Subsequent to registration of the trusted person, a bank shall send an acknowledgement to the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication, informing them of the successful registration.
 76FY. A bank shall observe a 24 hour cooling period before the TPM is activated for a customer. Upon activation of the TPM, the bank shall promptly notify the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication.
 DA.2A.2.3 Authentication process for transactions under TPM
 76FZ. Any transaction beyond the threshold indicated by the customer will be notified to the trusted person for authentication through the available channels of communication. The notification shall include the amount of transaction, beneficiary details [viz., name, account number, mobile number, etc.,] to which the amount is being transferred and narration (if any) entered by the customer while initiating the transaction. A trusted person shall have a one-hour window from being notified, to give consent to the transaction through the trusted mode as prescribed by the bank for TPM. The transaction shall be executed only upon the trusted person’s consent to the transaction, subject to the bank’s fraud risk controls and other applicable requirements. In case there is a negative response or there is no response from the trusted person within the prescribed time window as above, the transaction shall be rejected.
 76FZA. The consent of the trusted person to authenticate a transaction may be taken either through physical / digital signature or any other form of authentication given in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The bank shall also maintain appropriate logs / records of the same.
 76FZB. A bank shall ensure that the trusted person is not privy to aspects pertaining to the customer’s banking relationship (including but not limited to account balance, fixed deposits, investments, or insurance details) at any stage, including during transaction validation. The role of the trusted person shall be strictly limited to the transaction authentication.
 DA.2A.2.4 Customer controls
 76FZC. A bank shall provide customers with controls to change an existing trusted person, modify the threshold amount or payment channels chosen for the TPM, or opting out of the TPM itself. Exercise of such controls shall be subject to a cooling period of 24 hours and shall be authenticated by the customer. Further, if a customer is assessed to be more vulnerable to falling prey to cyber-enabled financial crimes / frauds, the bank shall resort to additional checks, e.g. requiring a mandatory branch visit or a tele-verification call, etc.
 76FZD. In case of change or removal of a trusted person, a bank shall notify both the customer and the outgoing trusted person through the available communication channels of the change before it takes effect.
 DA.2A.2.5 Implementation and customer awareness
 76FZE. A bank shall give wide publicity to the availability of the TPM and provide guidance to customers regarding its applicability and features. Such communications shall be disseminated in English, Hindi and local language of the region through all available channels of customer outreach available to the bank, such as branches, SMS, email, etc. The bank shall ensure that the communication explicitly delineates the role of the trusted person, benefits and limitations of the TPM, etc.”
 (R Sathish)
 Chief General Manager
 | 

 |
```

```text
Draft - Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 | 
 DoR.MCS.REC.No. /01-01-033/2026-27 
 XXXX XX, 2026
 Draft Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026
 The Reserve Bank had issued the Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 dated June 24, 2026 on ‘Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’ which, inter alia, strengthened the existing framework for limiting liability of customers in unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs). While the revised framework primarily addresses customer liability in the event of fraudulent EBTs, a need is felt to further strengthen the same from a preventive perspective by providing customers with greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels are used. Accordingly, based on the public feedback received on the Discussion Paper ‘Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds’ dated April 09, 2026, it has been decided to issue directions on customer-induced controls and an additional layer of authentication through a Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM). Further, on a review to bring uniformity in practices adopted by banks and ensure that customers are protected against specific acts of omission or commission on part of the banks, it has been decided to expand the scope of the definition of ‘negligence by an SFB’ specified in the aforementioned Amendment Directions.
 Accordingly, these directions are issued to all Small Finance Banks (hereinafter referred to collectively as “SFBs” and individually as an “SFB”) under the Reserve Bank’s Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025.
 2. In exercise of the powers conferred by section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act,1949, the Reserve Bank, being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in public interest so to do, hereby issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified. 
 3. Short Title and Commencement
 (1) These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026.
 (2) These Directions shall come into effect from July 1, 2027, or on such earlier date as an SFB may decide to implement, except the provisions contained in in clauses (i) to (vi), (ix) and (x) of sub-paragraph 4(20C) specified below which shall come into effect from January 1, 2027.
 4. These Amendment Directions shall substitute the definition of ‘negligence by an SFB’ prescribed in the Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 as under:
 “4(20C) Negligence by an SFB means any act of omission or commission on part of the SFB which results in or contributes to the occurrence of a fraudulent electronic banking transaction in a customer account, including the following:
 (i) not implementing instructions related to factors of authentication for EBTs, as prescribed under Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025;
 (ii) not implementing multi factor authentication for creation of new account linkages (addition / modification / deletion of beneficiaries), change in account details or revision to fund transfer limits, as prescribed under paragraph 46 of Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls) Directions, 2026;
 (iii) not sending mandatory alert for an EBT, as prescribed under paragraph 76D of these Directions;
 (iv) not providing 24x7 channels for reporting of fraudulent EBTs or loss of debit / credit card, as prescribed under paragraph 76G of these Directions;
 (v) not acting promptly upon a customer notification regarding fraudulent EBT(s) or loss of debit / credit card, as prescribed under paragraph 76J of these Directions;
 (vi) not blocking the digital payment channel and / or notifying the customer consequent to the maximum number of failed login or authentication attempts, where such failure contributed to the fraudulent EBT, as prescribed under paragraphs 50 and 51 of Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls) Directions, 2026; 
 (vii) not providing the facility of mandatory customer-induced controls or not implementing the controls for EBTs as set by the customer, as prescribed under these Directions;
 (viii) not providing Trusted Person Mechanism or failing to implement the directions with respect to the mechanism, as prescribed under these Directions;
 (ix) a system malfunction or security breach at the SFB’s end, which facilitates or results in a fraudulent EBT; and
 (x) collusion or connivance of an employee of the SFB or any third party engaged by the SFB, which facilitates or results in a fraudulent EBT.”
 5. These Amendment Directions shall modify the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the Directions) as under:
 (1) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(9), namely:
 “4(9A) Customer-induced Control means a customer-configurable restriction, limit, lock, safeguard or permission applicable to the customer’s account.”
 (2) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(10.1A), namely:
 “4(10.1B) Digital Payment Channel means any electronic interface, device, network or set of procedures provided by an SFB, through which a customer can undertake a digital payment transaction / electronic banking transaction.”
 (3) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(19), namely:
 “4(19A) Merchant shall have the same meaning as defined in the Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA).”
 (4) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(24), namely:
 “4(24.1A) Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI) shall have the same meaning as defined in the Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs). ”
 (5) In paragraph 4, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(25A), namely:
 “4(25B) Stop Switch means a facility through which a customer can disable all customer initiated future debits associated with her / his account(s) as per these Directions.”
 (6) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(26A), namely:
 “4(26AA) Trusted Person means a natural person aged 18 years or above, registered by an SFB’s customer, to act as an additional factor of authentication as per these Directions.”
 (7) In Chapter IV on ‘Customer Guidance and Protection’ of the Directions, in the section ‘DA. Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’, the following sub-sections and paragraphs shall be inserted after the sub-section ‘DA.2 Alerts for EBTs’, namely:
 “DA.2A. Preventive Safeguards for EBTs
 DA.2A.1 Customer-induced controls for EBTs
 DA.2A.1.1 Customer-induced controls for digital payment channels other than cards
 76FA. An SFB shall provide all its customers with the facility to disable one or more digital payment channels linked to their account, and to subsequently re-enable such channel through the physical or digital interfaces of the SFB, in accordance with the procedure specified in paragraphs 76FI and 76FJ hereunder.
 76FB. Where a digital payment channel has been disabled by the customer, no customer-initiated debit transaction shall be permitted through that channel until it is re-enabled.
 76FC. In addition, an SFB shall provide the following controls to its customers, which may be exercised by them at their option:
 (1) to set or modify a maximum amount limit per transaction, per beneficiary or for the transactions in aggregate in a day that may be undertaken through a digital payment channel, within the overall limits otherwise applicable to that channel;
 Illustration 1: Beneficiary level limit – A customer sets a maximum limit of ₹20,000 per day for payments to a particular beneficiary. Even if the limit for the digital payment channel set by the payment system operator / the SFB permits a higher amount, transactions to that particular beneficiary cannot exceed ₹20,000 per day.
 Illustration 2: Transaction amount limit – A customer sets a maximum limit of ₹10,000 per transaction for a particular digital payment channel. Any transaction above ₹10,000 through that digital payment channel would not be permitted.
 Illustration 3: Daily limit – A customer sets an overall daily limit of ₹50,000 for transactions done through a particular digital payment channel, even though the payment systems operator or the SFB permits a higher limit. Any transaction above the daily limit would not be permitted through that digital payment channel.
 (2) to set or modify, a maximum limit for the transactions that may be undertaken in a day, through all the available digital payment channels taken together;
 (3) to set a time window during which one or more digital payment channels linked to the customer’s account shall remain disabled; and
 (4) any other control introduced by the SFB over and above the controls prescribed at 76FC (1) to 76FC (3) above, which may further strengthen customer options to safeguard their EBTs.
 DA.2A.1.2 Customer-induced controls for cards (Debit, Credit, and Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPI) Card))
 76FD. An SFB shall provide to all its cardholders the facility to switch on / off and set / modify transaction limits (within the overall card limit, if any, set by the issuer) for all types of transactions – domestic or international; at Point of Sale (PoS) / ATMs / online transactions / contactless transactions, etc.
 76FE. The card-specific directions are not applicable to Gift PPI cards and Transit PPI Cards.
 DA.2A.1.3 Stop Switch facility in customer accounts
 76FF. An SFB shall provide its customers with a Stop Switch facility for immediate disablement of all outward future debits associated with her / his account(s). However, any debits due to ongoing recurring payment mandates and standing instructions, and marking of lien or debits initiated by the SFB to recover due charges, loan instalment, etc., shall be excluded from the scope of Stop Switch.
 76FG. Upon activation of the Stop Switch, no customer-initiated debit transaction, creation of new payment mandates, setting up of new standing instructions or registration of UPI on new third-party payment applications shall be permitted in the account.
 76FH. The activation of a customer-induced control or Stop Switch shall however not affect any inward credits into the customer’s account.
 DA.2A.1.4 Re-enablement of digital payment channels or Deactivation of Stop Switch
 76FI. An SFB shall provide customers the facility to re-enable digital payment channels or deactivate the Stop Switch to re-enable operations in the customer’s account, subject to customer authentication. An SFB shall ensure that any request for re-enablement is subject to, at the minimum, the authentication requirements prescribed under the Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The authentication for such requests shall be at least as stringent as those applied while enabling the corresponding digital payment channel and may be enhanced based on the SFB’s risk assessment laid down in its policy.
 76FJ. Based on its risk assessment, an SFB shall impose a reasonable cooling period or other risk mitigation measures, before giving effect to such re-enablement requests.
 DA.2A.1.5 Default controls and other aspects
 76FK. An SFB shall keep all digital payment channels disabled by default at the time of customer onboarding. Such channels shall be enabled only upon an explicit consent from the customer and after complying with the applicable authentication requirements.
 76FL. Notwithstanding the above,
 (1) in case of cards -
 (i) at the time of their issue, all cards (physical and virtual) shall be enabled for use only at contact-based points of usage (viz. ATMs and Point of Sale (PoS) devices) within India.
 (ii) at the time of their re-issue, the existing card controls shall be mapped to re-issued cards.
 (iii) forex prepaid cards shall be enabled for both contact, and contactless points of usage outside India at the time of their issue / re-issue.
 (2) in case of other digital payment channels, where an SFB has enabled a particular channel for a customer at the time of customer onboarding or subsequently, it shall specify a ceiling on the aggregate value of fund transfers that the customer can undertake across the channel over the initial period of 24 hours, based on the SFB's risk assessment. After the initial period of 24 hours, the SFB may provide for gradual enhancements to the ceiling, based on its channel risk assessment and internal policy. The SFB shall allow modification of the initial or enhanced ceiling (if implemented) through the exercise of customer controls provided at paragraph 76FC above and subject to compliance with the applicable authentication requirements. However, such modification shall be allowed only after the initial period of 24 hours has lapsed post activation of the digital payment channel.
 76FM. The facilities for activation, modification and deactivation of customer-induced controls and Stop Switch shall be made available to all customers through the available points of customer interface such as branches, ATMs, internet banking, mobile banking, Interactive Voice Response (IVR), etc.
 76FN. Upon any activation, modification, deactivation or re-activation of any of such facilities, an SFB shall immediately notify the customers through the available channels of communication, including but not limited to SMS and e-mail.
 76FO. An SFB shall maintain tamper proof audit logs of controls and the Stop Switch initiated by customers to facilitate review and resolution of disputes.
 76FP. An SFB shall undertake ongoing outreach efforts on an ongoing basis to inform customers regarding availability of the customer-induced controls and Stop Switch facility and attendant aspects such as process to activate or deactivate the same, implications of the activation, etc.
 DA.2A.2 Authentication through Trusted Person Mechanism
 DA.2A.2.1 Applicability
 76FQ. An SFB shall put in place a mechanism, called the Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM), to enable customers to register a trusted person to act as an additional factor of transaction authentication. The TPM shall apply to electronic fund transfers initiated through the physical and digital channels available under such customer’s account beyond the threshold set by the customer, except for transactions initiated for:
 (1) payments made through the UPI channel linked to the customer’s account;
 (2) merchant payments, irrespective of the payment channel or instrument used; and
 (3) recurring payments through standing instructions, e-mandates or NACH mandates.
 76FR. An SFB shall offer the TPM to all its customers, whose availment shall be entirely voluntary, based on explicit requests of the customer and the trusted person, and are subject to the thresholds put in place by the customer.
 76FS. The TPM shall be available in bank accounts operated by individuals solely or in such joint accounts operated under any of the survivorship clauses.
 DA.2A.2.2 Registration and onboarding of trusted person
 76FT. An SFB shall facilitate, through its physical and digital channels, the registration of a trusted person, activation of the TPM, and configuration of related transaction-level thresholds by customers.
 76FU. For registering a trusted person, an SFB shall:
 (1) obtain the trusted person’s name, mobile number, email address and copy of at least one Officially Valid Document (OVD);
 (2) verify the identity and eligibility of the trusted person on the basis of the OVD and such other information or documentation as may be reasonably required; and
 (3) verify the mobile number and email address of the trusted person through an appropriate authentication mechanism.
 76FV. The mobile number registered for the trusted person shall be distinct from the mobile number linked to the customer’s account.
 76FW. An SFB, while obtaining the consent for TPM registration, shall clearly inform the customer and the trusted person that registration under the mechanism:
 (1) does not confer upon the trusted person the status of a joint account holder, nominee, mandate holder or authorised signatory;
 (2) does not grant the trusted person any right, title or beneficial interest in the account;
 (3) does not authorise the trusted person to independently access or operate the account, initiate any transaction, or otherwise issue instructions in relation to the account;
 (4) does not result in the trusted person incurring any financial liability when she / he approves or rejects a transaction; and
 (5) requires the trusted person to authenticate or reject the transaction within the time window prescribed by the SFB and in a manner compliant with paragraph 76FZ ibid.
 76FX. Subsequent to registration of the trusted person, an SFB shall send an acknowledgement to the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication, informing them of the successful registration.
 76FY. An SFB shall observe a 24 hour cooling period before the TPM is activated for a customer. Upon activation of the TPM, the SFB shall promptly notify the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication.
 DA.2A.2.3 Authentication process for transactions under TPM
 76FZ. Any transaction beyond the threshold indicated by the customer will be notified to the trusted person for authentication through the available channels of communication. The notification shall include the amount of transaction, beneficiary details [viz., name, account number, mobile number, etc.,] to which the amount is being transferred and narration (if any) entered by the customer while initiating the transaction. A trusted person shall have a one-hour window from being notified, to give consent to the transaction through the trusted mode as prescribed by the SFB for TPM. The transaction shall be executed only upon the trusted person’s consent to the transaction, subject to the SFB’s fraud risk controls and other applicable requirements. In case there is a negative response or there is no response from the trusted person within the prescribed time window as above, the transaction shall be rejected.
 76FZA. The consent of the trusted person to authenticate a transaction may be taken either through physical / digital signature or any other form of authentication given in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The SFB shall also maintain appropriate logs / records of the same.
 76FZB. An SFB shall ensure that the trusted person is not privy to aspects pertaining to the customer’s banking relationship (including but not limited to account balance, fixed deposits, investments, or insurance details) at any stage, including during transaction validation. The role of the trusted person shall be strictly limited to the transaction authentication.
 DA.2A.2.4 Customer controls
 76FZC. An SFB shall provide customers with controls to change an existing trusted person, modify the threshold amount or payment channels chosen for the TPM, or opting out of the TPM itself. Exercise of such controls shall be subject to a cooling period of 24 hours and shall be authenticated by the customer. Further, if a customer is assessed to be more vulnerable to falling prey to cyber-enabled financial crimes / frauds, the SFB shall resort to additional checks, e.g. requiring a mandatory branch visit or a tele-verification call, etc.
 76FZD. In case of change or removal of a trusted person, an SFB shall notify both the customer and the outgoing trusted person through the available communication channels of the change before it takes effect.
 DA.2A.2.5 Implementation and customer awareness
 76FZE. An SFB shall give wide publicity to the availability of the TPM and provide guidance to customers regarding its applicability and features. Such communications shall be disseminated in English, Hindi and local language of the region through all available channels of customer outreach available to the SFB, such as branches, SMS, email, etc. The SFB shall ensure that the communication explicitly delineates the role of the trusted person, benefits and limitations of the TPM, etc.”
 (R Sathish)
 Chief General Manager
 | 

 |
```

```text
Draft - Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 | 
 DoR.MCS.REC.No. /01-01-034/2026-27
 XXXX XX, 2026
 Draft Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026
 The Reserve Bank had issued the Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 dated June 24, 2026 on ‘Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’ which, inter alia, strengthened the existing framework for limiting liability of customers in unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs). While the revised framework primarily addresses customer liability in the event of fraudulent transactions, a need is felt to further strengthen the same from a preventive perspective by providing customers with greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels are used. Accordingly, based on the public feedback received on the Discussion Paper ‘Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds’ dated April 09, 2026, it has been decided to issue directions on customer-induced controls and an additional layer of authentication through a Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM). Further, on a review to bring uniformity in practices adopted by banks and ensure that customers are protected against specific acts of omission or commission on part of the banks, it has been decided to expand the scope of the definition of ‘negligence by a PB’ specified in the aforementioned Amendment Directions.
 Accordingly, these directions are issued to all Payments Banks (hereinafter referred to collectively as “PBs” and individually as a “PB”) under the Reserve Bank’s Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025.
 2. In exercise of the powers conferred by section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act,1949, the Reserve Bank, being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in public interest so to do, hereby issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified.
 3. Short Title and Commencement
 (1) These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026.
 (2) These Directions shall come into effect from July 1, 2027, or on such earlier date as a PB may decide to implement, except the provisions contained in clauses (i) to (vi), (ix) and (x) of sub-paragraph 4(10C) specified below which shall come into effect from January 1, 2027.
 4. These Amendment Directions shall substitute the definition of ‘negligence by a PB’ prescribed in the Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 as under:
 “4(10C) Negligence by a PB means any act of omission or commission on part of the PB which results in or contributes to the occurrence of a fraudulent electronic banking transaction in a customer account, including the following:
 (i) not implementing instructions related to factors of authentication for EBTs, as prescribed under Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025;
 (ii) not implementing multi factor authentication for creation of new account linkages (addition / modification / deletion of beneficiaries), change in account details or revision to fund transfer limits, as prescribed under paragraph 46 of Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls) Directions, 2026;
 (iii) not sending mandatory alert for an EBT, as prescribed under paragraph 33D of these Directions;
 (iv) not providing 24x7 channels for reporting of fraudulent EBTs or loss of debit / credit card, as prescribed under paragraph 33G of these Directions;
 (v) not acting promptly upon a customer notification regarding fraudulent EBT(s) or loss of debit / credit card, as prescribed under paragraph 33J of these Directions;
 (vi) not blocking the digital payment channel and / or notifying the customer consequent to the maximum number of failed login or authentication attempts, where such failure contributed to the fraudulent EBT, as prescribed under paragraphs 50 and 51 of Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks – Digital Payment Security Controls) Directions, 2026;
 (vii) not providing the facility of mandatory customer-induced controls or not implementing the controls for EBTs as set by the customer, as prescribed under these Directions;
 (viii) not providing Trusted Person Mechanism or failing to implement the directions with respect to the mechanism, as prescribed under these Directions;
 (ix) a system malfunction or security breach at the PB’s end, which facilitates or results in a fraudulent EBT; and
 (x) collusion or connivance of an employee of the PB or any third party engaged by the PB, which facilitates or results in a fraudulent EBT.”
 5. These Amendment Directions shall modify the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the Directions) as under:
 (1) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(6), namely:
 “4(6A) Customer-induced Control means a customer-configurable restriction, limit, lock, safeguard or permission applicable to the customer’s account.”
 (2) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(7.1A), namely:
 “4(7.1B) Digital Payment Channel means any electronic interface, device, network or set of procedures provided by a PB, through which a customer can undertake a digital payment transaction / electronic banking transaction.”
 (3) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(10), namely:
 “4(10.1A) Merchant shall have the same meaning as defined in the Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA).”
 (4) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(12), namely:
 "4(12A) Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI) shall have the same meaning as defined in the Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs)."
 (5) In paragraph 4, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(13), namely:
 “4(13.A1A) Stop Switch means a facility through which a customer can disable all customer-initiated future debits associated with her / his account(s) as per these Directions.”
 (6) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(13A), namely:
 “4(13AA) Trusted Person means a natural person aged 18 years or above, registered by a PB’s customer, to act as an additional factor of authentication as per these Directions.”
 (7) In Chapter III on ‘Customer Guidance and Protection’ of the Directions, in the section ‘CA. Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’, the following sub-sections and paragraphs shall be inserted after the sub-section ‘CA.2 Alerts for EBTs’, namely:
 “CA.2A. Preventive Safeguards for EBTs
 CA.2A.1 Customer-induced controls for EBTs
 CA.2A.1.1 Customer-induced controls for digital payment channels other than cards
 33FA. A PB shall provide all its customers with the facility to disable one or more digital payment channels linked to their account, and to subsequently re-enable such channel through the physical or digital interfaces of the PB, in accordance with the procedure specified in paragraphs 33FI and 33FJ hereunder.
 33FB. Where a digital payment channel has been disabled by the customer, no customer-initiated debit transaction shall be permitted through that channel until it is re-enabled.
 33FC. In addition, a PB shall provide the following controls to its customers, which may be exercised by them at their option:
 (1) to set or modify a maximum amount limit per transaction, per beneficiary or for the transactions in aggregate in a day that may be undertaken through a digital payment channel, within the overall limits otherwise applicable to that channel;
 Illustration 1: Beneficiary level limit – A customer sets a maximum limit of ₹20,000 per day for payments to a particular beneficiary. Even if the limit for the digital payment channel set by the payment system operator / the PB permits a higher amount, transactions to that particular beneficiary cannot exceed ₹20,000 per day.
 Illustration 2: Transaction amount limit – A customer sets a maximum limit of ₹10,000 per transaction for a particular digital payment channel. Any transaction above ₹10,000 through that digital payment channel would not be permitted.
 Illustration 3: Daily limit – A customer sets an overall daily limit of ₹50,000 for transactions done through a particular digital payment channel, even though the payment systems operator or the PB permits a higher limit. Any transaction above the daily limit would not be permitted through that digital payment channel.
 (2) to set or modify, a maximum limit for the transactions that may be undertaken in a day, through all the available digital payment channels taken together;
 (3) to set a time window during which one or more digital payment channels linked to the customer’s account shall remain disabled; and
 (4) any other control introduced by the PB over and above the controls prescribed at 33FC (1) to 33FC (3) above, which may further strengthen customer options to safeguard their EBTs.
 CA.2A.1.2 Customer-induced controls for cards (Debit, Credit, and Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPI) Card))
 33FD. A PB shall provide to all its cardholders the facility to switch on / off and set / modify transaction limits (within the overall card limit, if any, set by the issuer) for all types of transactions – domestic or international; at Point of Sale (PoS) / ATMs / online transactions / contactless transactions, etc.
 33FE. The card-specific directions are not applicable to Gift PPI cards and Transit PPI Cards.
 CA.2A.1.3 Stop Switch facility in customer accounts
 33FF. A PB shall provide its customers with a Stop Switch facility for immediate disablement of all outward future debits associated with her / his account(s). However, any debits due to ongoing recurring payment mandates and standing instructions, and marking of lien or debits initiated by the PB to recover due charges, loan instalment, etc., shall be excluded from the scope of Stop Switch.
 33FG. Upon activation of the Stop Switch, no customer-initiated debit transaction, creation of new payment mandates, setting up of new standing instructions or registration of UPI on new third-party payment applications shall be permitted in the account.
 33FH. The activation of a customer-induced control or Stop Switch shall however not affect any inward credits into the customer’s account.
 CA.2A.1.4 Re-enablement of digital payment channels or Deactivation of Stop Switch
 33FI. A PB shall provide customers the facility to re-enable digital payment channels or deactivate the Stop Switch to re-enable operations in the customer’s account, subject to customer authentication. A PB shall ensure that any request for re-enablement is subject to, at the minimum, the authentication requirements prescribed under the Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The authentication for such requests shall be at least as stringent as those applied while enabling the corresponding digital payment channel and may be enhanced based on the PB’s risk assessment laid down in its policy.
 33FJ. Based on its risk assessment, a PB shall impose a reasonable cooling period or other risk mitigation measures, before giving effect to such re-enablement requests.
 CA.2A.1.5 Default controls and other aspects
 33FK. A PB shall keep all digital payment channels disabled by default at the time of customer onboarding. Such channels shall be enabled only upon an explicit consent from the customer and after complying with the applicable authentication requirements.
 33FL. Notwithstanding the above,
 (1) in case of cards -
 (i) at the time of their issue, all cards (physical and virtual) shall be enabled for use only at contact-based points of usage (viz. ATMs and Point of Sale (PoS) devices) within India.
 (ii) at the time of their re-issue, the existing card controls shall be mapped to re-issued cards.
 (iii) forex prepaid cards shall be enabled for both contact, and contactless points of usage outside India at the time of their issue / re-issue.
 (2) in case of other digital payment channels, where a PB has enabled a particular channel for a customer at the time of customer onboarding or subsequently, it shall specify a ceiling on the aggregate value of fund transfers that the customer can undertake across the channel over the initial period of 24 hours, based on the PB's risk assessment. After the initial period of 24 hours, the PB may provide for gradual enhancements to the ceiling, based on its channel risk assessment and internal policy. The PB shall allow modification of the initial or enhanced ceiling (if implemented) through the exercise of customer controls provided at paragraph 33FC above and subject to compliance with the applicable authentication requirements. However, such modification shall be allowed only after the initial period of 24 hours has lapsed post activation of the digital payment channel.
 33FM. The facilities for activation, modification and deactivation of customer-induced controls and Stop Switch shall be made available to all customers through the available points of customer interface such as branches, ATMs, internet banking, mobile banking, Interactive Voice Response (IVR), etc.
 33FN. Upon any activation, modification, deactivation or re-activation of any of such facilities, a PB shall immediately notify the customers through the available channels of communication, including but not limited to SMS and e-mail.
 33FO. A PB shall maintain tamper proof audit logs of controls and the Stop Switch initiated by customers to facilitate review and resolution of disputes.
 33FP. A PB shall undertake ongoing outreach efforts on an ongoing basis to inform customers regarding availability of the customer-induced controls and Stop Switch facility and attendant aspects such as process to activate or deactivate the same, implications of the activation, etc.
 CA.2A.2 Authentication through Trusted Person Mechanism
 CA.2A.2.1 Applicability
 33FQ. A PB shall put in place a mechanism, called the Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM), to enable customers to register a trusted person to act as an additional factor of transaction authentication. The TPM shall apply to electronic fund transfers initiated through the physical and digital channels available under such customer’s account beyond the threshold set by the customer, except for transactions initiated for:
 (1) payments made through the UPI channel linked to the customer’s account;
 (2) merchant payments, irrespective of the payment channel or instrument used; and
 (3) recurring payments through standing instructions, e-mandates or NACH mandates.
 33FR. A PB shall offer the TPM to all its customers, whose availment shall be entirely voluntary, based on explicit requests of the customer and the trusted person, and are subject to the thresholds put in place by the customer.
 33FS. The TPM shall be available in bank accounts operated by individuals solely or in such joint accounts operated under any of the survivorship clauses.
 CA.2A.2.2 Registration and onboarding of trusted person
 33FT. A PB shall facilitate, through its physical and digital channels, the registration of a trusted person, activation of the TPM, and configuration of related transaction-level thresholds by customers.
 33FU. For registering a trusted person, a PB shall:
 (1) obtain the trusted person’s name, mobile number, email address and copy of at least one Officially Valid Document (OVD);
 (2) verify the identity and eligibility of the trusted person on the basis of the OVD and such other information or documentation as may be reasonably required; and
 (3) verify the mobile number and email address of the trusted person through an appropriate authentication mechanism.
 33FV. The mobile number registered for the trusted person shall be distinct from the mobile number linked to the customer’s account.
 33FW. A PB, while obtaining the consent for TPM registration, shall clearly inform the customer and the trusted person that registration under the mechanism:
 (1) does not confer upon the trusted person the status of a joint account holder, nominee, mandate holder or authorised signatory;
 (2) does not grant the trusted person any right, title or beneficial interest in the account;
 (3) does not authorise the trusted person to independently access or operate the account, initiate any transaction, or otherwise issue instructions in relation to the account;
 (4) does not result in the trusted person incurring any financial liability when she / he approves or rejects a transaction; and
 (5) requires the trusted person to authenticate or reject the transaction within the time window prescribed by the PB and in a manner compliant with paragraph 33FZ ibid.
 33FX. Subsequent to registration of the trusted person, a PB shall send an acknowledgement to the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication, informing them of the successful registration.
 33FY. A PB shall observe a 24 hour cooling period before the TPM is activated for a customer. Upon activation of the TPM, the PB shall promptly notify the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication.
 CA.2A.2.3 Authentication process for transactions under TPM
 33FZ. Any transaction beyond the threshold indicated by the customer will be notified to the trusted person for authentication through the available channels of communication. The notification shall include the amount of transaction, beneficiary details [viz., name, account number, mobile number, etc.,] to which the amount is being transferred and narration (if any) entered by the customer while initiating the transaction. A trusted person shall have a one-hour window from being notified, to give consent to the transaction through the trusted mode as prescribed by the PB for TPM. The transaction shall be executed only upon the trusted person’s consent to the transaction, subject to the PB’s fraud risk controls and other applicable requirements. In case there is a negative response or there is no response from the trusted person within the prescribed time window as above, the transaction shall be rejected.
 33FZA. The consent of the trusted person to authenticate a transaction may be taken either through physical / digital signature or any other form of authentication given in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The PB shall also maintain appropriate logs / records of the same.
 33FZB. A PB shall ensure that the trusted person is not privy to aspects pertaining to the customer’s banking relationship (including but not limited to account balance, fixed deposits, investments, or insurance details) at any stage, including during transaction validation. The role of the trusted person shall be strictly limited to the transaction authentication.
 CA.2A.2.4 Customer controls
 33FZC. A PB shall provide customers with controls to change an existing trusted person, modify the threshold amount or payment channels chosen for the TPM, or opting out of the TPM itself. Exercise of such controls shall be subject to a cooling period of 24 hours and shall be authenticated by the customer. Further, if a customer is assessed to be more vulnerable to falling prey to cyber-enabled financial crimes / frauds, the PB shall resort to additional checks, e.g. requiring a mandatory branch visit or a tele-verification call, etc.
 33FZD. In case of change or removal of a trusted person, a PB shall notify both the customer and the outgoing trusted person through the available communication channels of the change before it takes effect.
 CA.2A.2.5 Implementation and customer awareness
 33FZE. A PB shall give wide publicity to the availability of the TPM and provide guidance to customers regarding its applicability and features. Such communications shall be disseminated in English, Hindi and local language of the region through all available channels of customer outreach available to the PB, such as branches, SMS, email, etc. The PB shall ensure that the communication explicitly delineates the role of the trusted person, benefits and limitations of the TPM, etc.”
 (R Sathish)
 Chief General Manager | 

 |
```
