```text
Draft - Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 | 
 DoR.MCS.REC.No. /01-01-035/2026-27
 XXXX XX, 2026
 Draft Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026
 The Reserve Bank had issued the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 dated June 24, 2026 on ‘Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’ which, inter alia, strengthened the existing framework for limiting liability of customers in unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs). While the revised framework primarily addresses customer liability in the event of fraudulent EBTs, a need is felt to further strengthen the same from a preventive perspective by providing customers with greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels are used. Accordingly, based on the public feedback received on the Discussion Paper ‘Exploring safeguards in digital payments to curb frauds’ dated April 09, 2026, it has been decided to issue directions on customer-induced controls and an additional layer of authentication through a Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM). Further, on a review to bring uniformity in practices adopted by banks and ensure that customers are protected against specific acts of omission or commission on part of the banks, it has been decided to expand the scope of the definition of ‘negligence by an LAB’ specified in the aforementioned Amendment Directions.
 Accordingly, these directions are issued to all Local Area Banks (hereinafter referred to collectively as “LABs” and individually as an “LAB”) under the Reserve Bank’s Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025.
 2. In exercise of the powers conferred by section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act,1949, the Reserve Bank, being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in public interest so to do, hereby issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified.
 3. Short Title and Commencement
 (1) These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026.
 (2) These Directions shall come into effect from July 1, 2027, or on such earlier date as an LAB may decide to implement, except the provisions contained in clauses (i) to (iv), (vii) and (viii) of sub-paragraph 4(20C) specified below which shall come into effect from January 1, 2027.
 4. These Amendment Directions shall substitute the definition of ‘negligence by an LAB’ prescribed in the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 as under:
 “4(20C) Negligence by an LAB means any act of omission or commission on part of the LAB which results in or contributes to the occurrence of a fraudulent electronic banking transaction in a customer account, including the following:
 (i) not implementing instructions related to factors of authentication for EBTs, as prescribed under Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025;
 (ii) not sending mandatory alert for an EBT, as prescribed under paragraph 16D of these Directions;
 (iii) not providing 24x7 channels for reporting of fraudulent EBTs or loss of debit / credit card, as prescribed under paragraph 16G of these Directions;
 (iv) not acting promptly upon a customer notification regarding fraudulent EBT(s) or loss of debit / credit card, as prescribed under paragraph 16J of these Directions;
 (v) not providing the facility of mandatory customer-induced controls or not implementing the controls for EBTs as set by the customer, as prescribed under these Directions;
 (vi) not providing Trusted Person Mechanism or failing to implement the directions with respect to the mechanism, as prescribed under these Directions;
 (vii) a system malfunction or security breach at the LAB’s end, which facilitates or results in a fraudulent EBT; and
 (viii) collusion or connivance of an employee of the LAB or any third party engaged by the LAB, which facilitates or results in a fraudulent EBT.”
 5. These Amendment Directions shall modify the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the Directions) as under:
 (1) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(9), namely:
 “4(9A) Customer-induced Control means a customer-configurable restriction, limit, lock, safeguard or permission applicable to the customer’s account.”
 (2) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(10.1A), namely:
 “4(10.1B) Digital Payment Channel means any electronic interface, device, network or set of procedures provided by an LAB, through which a customer can undertake a digital payment transaction / electronic banking transaction.”
 (3) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(19), namely:
 “4(19A) Merchant shall have the same meaning as defined in the Master Direction on Regulation of Payment Aggregator (PA).”
 (4) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(24), namely:
 “4(24.1A) Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI) shall have the same meaning as defined in the Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs).”
 (5) In paragraph 4, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(25A), namely:
 “4(25B) Stop Switch means a facility through which a customer can disable all customer initiated future debits associated with her / his account(s) as per these Directions.”
 (6) In paragraph 4 of the Directions, the following definition shall be inserted after sub-paragraph 4(26A), namely:
 “4(26AA) Trusted Person means a natural person aged 18 years or above, registered by an LAB’s customer, to act as an additional factor of authentication as per these Directions.”
 (7) In Chapter IV on ‘Customer Guidance and Protection’ of the Directions, in the section ‘AA. Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’, the following sub-sections and paragraphs shall be inserted after the sub-section on ‘AA.2 Alerts for EBTs’, namely:
 “AA.2A. Preventive Safeguards for EBTs
 AA.2A.1 Customer-induced controls for EBTs
 AA.2A.1.1 Customer-induced controls for digital payment channels other than cards
 16FA. An LAB shall provide all its customers with the facility to disable one or more digital payment channels linked to their account, and to subsequently re-enable such channel through the physical or digital interfaces of the LAB, in accordance with the procedure specified in paragraphs 16FI and 16FJ hereunder.
 16FB. Where a digital payment channel has been disabled by the customer, no customer-initiated debit transaction shall be permitted through that channel until it is re-enabled.
 16FC. In addition, an LAB shall provide the following controls to its customers, which may be exercised by them at their option:
 (1) to set or modify a maximum amount limit per transaction, per beneficiary or for the transactions in aggregate in a day that may be undertaken through a digital payment channel, within the overall limits otherwise applicable to that channel;
 Illustration 1: Beneficiary level limit – A customer sets a maximum limit of ₹20,000 per day for payments to a particular beneficiary. Even if the limit for the digital payment channel set by the payment system operator / the LAB permits a higher amount, transactions to that particular beneficiary cannot exceed ₹20,000 per day.
 Illustration 2: Transaction amount limit – A customer sets a maximum limit of ₹10,000 per transaction for a particular digital payment channel. Any transaction above ₹10,000 through that digital payment channel would not be permitted.
 Illustration 3: Daily limit – A customer sets an overall daily limit of ₹50,000 for transactions done through a particular digital payment channel, even though the payment systems operator or the LAB permits a higher limit. Any transaction above the daily limit would not be permitted through that digital payment channel.
 (2) to set or modify, a maximum limit for the transactions that may be undertaken in a day, through all the available digital payment channels taken together;
 (3) to set a time window during which one or more digital payment channels linked to the customer’s account shall remain disabled; and
 (4) any other control introduced by the LAB over and above the controls prescribed at 16FC (1) to 16FC (3) above, which may further strengthen customer options to safeguard their EBTs.
 AA.2A.1.2 Customer-induced controls for cards (Debit, Credit, and Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPI) Card))
 16FD. An LAB shall provide to all its cardholders the facility to switch on / off and set / modify transaction limits (within the overall card limit, if any, set by the issuer) for all types of transactions – domestic or international; at Point of Sale (PoS) / ATMs / online transactions / contactless transactions, etc.
 16FE. The card-specific directions are not applicable to Gift PPI cards and Transit PPI Cards.
 AA.2A.1.3 Stop Switch facility in customer accounts
 16FF. An LAB shall provide its customers with a Stop Switch facility for immediate disablement of all outward future debits associated with her / his account(s). However, any debits due to ongoing recurring payment mandates and standing instructions, and marking of lien or debits initiated by the LAB to recover due charges, loan instalment, etc., shall be excluded from the scope of Stop Switch.
 16FG. Upon activation of the Stop Switch, no customer-initiated debit transaction, creation of new payment mandates, setting up of new standing instructions or registration of UPI on new third-party payment applications shall be permitted in the account.
 16FH. The activation of a customer-induced control or Stop Switch shall however not affect any inward credits into the customer’s account.
 AA.2A.1.4 Re-enablement of digital payment channels or Deactivation of Stop Switch
 16FI. An LAB shall provide customers the facility to re-enable digital payment channels or deactivate the Stop Switch to re-enable operations in the customer’s account, subject to customer authentication. An LAB shall ensure that any request for re-enablement is subject to, at the minimum, the authentication requirements prescribed under the Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The authentication for such requests shall be at least as stringent as those applied while enabling the corresponding digital payment channel and may be enhanced based on the LAB’s risk assessment laid down in its policy.
 16FJ. Based on its risk assessment, an LAB shall impose a reasonable cooling period or other risk mitigation measures, before giving effect to such re-enablement requests.
 AA.2A.1.5 Default controls and other aspects
 16FK. An LAB shall keep all digital payment channels disabled by default at the time of customer onboarding. Such channels shall be enabled only upon an explicit consent from the customer and after complying with the applicable authentication requirements.
 16FL. Notwithstanding the above,
 (1) in case of cards -
 (i) at the time of their issue, all cards (physical and virtual) shall be enabled for use only at contact-based points of usage (viz. ATMs and Point of Sale (PoS) devices) within India.
 (ii) at the time of their re-issue, the existing card controls shall be mapped to re-issued cards.
 (iii) forex prepaid cards shall be enabled for both contact, and contactless points of usage outside India at the time of their issue / re-issue.
 (2) in case of other digital payment channels, where an LAB has enabled a particular channel for a customer at the time of customer onboarding or subsequently, it shall specify a ceiling on the aggregate value of fund transfers that the customer can undertake across the channel over the initial period of 24 hours, based on the LAB's risk assessment. After the initial period of 24 hours, the LAB may provide for gradual enhancements to the ceiling, based on its channel risk assessment and internal policy. The LAB shall allow modification of the initial or enhanced ceiling (if implemented) through the exercise of customer controls provided at paragraph 16FC above and subject to compliance with the applicable authentication requirements. However, such modification shall be allowed only after the initial period of 24 hours has lapsed post activation of the digital payment channel.
 16FM. The facilities for activation, modification and deactivation of customer-induced controls and Stop Switch shall be made available to all customers through the available points of customer interface such as branches, ATMs, internet banking, mobile banking, Interactive Voice Response (IVR), etc.
 16FN. Upon any activation, modification, deactivation or re-activation of any of such facilities, an LAB shall immediately notify the customers through the available channels of communication, including but not limited to SMS and e-mail.
 16FO. An LAB shall maintain tamper proof audit logs of controls and the Stop Switch initiated by customers to facilitate review and resolution of disputes.
 16FP. An LAB shall undertake ongoing outreach efforts on an ongoing basis to inform customers regarding availability of the customer-induced controls and Stop Switch facility and attendant aspects such as process to activate or deactivate the same, implications of the activation, etc.
 AA.2A.2 Authentication through Trusted Person Mechanism
 AA.2A.2.1 Applicability
 16FQ. An LAB shall put in place a mechanism, called the Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM), to enable customers to register a trusted person to act as an additional factor of transaction authentication. The TPM shall apply to electronic fund transfers initiated through the physical and digital channels available under such customer’s account beyond the threshold set by the customer, except for transactions initiated for:
 (1) payments made through the UPI channel linked to the customer’s account;
 (2) merchant payments, irrespective of the payment channel or instrument used; and
 (3) recurring payments through standing instructions, e-mandates or NACH mandates.
 16FR. An LAB shall offer the TPM to all its customers, whose availment shall be entirely voluntary, based on explicit requests of the customer and the trusted person, and are subject to the thresholds put in place by the customer.
 16FS. The TPM shall be available in bank accounts operated by individuals solely or in such joint accounts operated under any of the survivorship clauses.
 AA.2A.2.2 Registration and onboarding of trusted person
 16FT. An LAB shall facilitate, through its physical and digital channels, the registration of a trusted person, activation of the TPM, and configuration of related transaction-level thresholds by customers.
 16FU. For registering a trusted person, an LAB shall:
 (1) obtain the trusted person’s name, mobile number, email address and copy of at least one Officially Valid Document (OVD);
 (2) verify the identity and eligibility of the trusted person on the basis of the OVD and such other information or documentation as may be required; and
 (3) verify the mobile number and email address of the trusted person through an appropriate authentication mechanism.
 16FV. The mobile number registered for the trusted person shall be distinct from the mobile number linked to the customer’s account.
 16FW. An LAB, while obtaining the consent for TPM registration, shall clearly inform the customer and the trusted person that registration under the mechanism:
 (1) does not confer upon the trusted person the status of a joint account holder, nominee, mandate holder or authorised signatory;
 (2) does not grant the trusted person any right, title or beneficial interest in the account;
 (3) does not authorise the trusted person to independently access or operate the account, initiate any transaction, or otherwise issue instructions in relation to the account;
 (4) does not result in the trusted person incurring any financial liability when she / he approves or rejects a transaction; and
 (5) requires the trusted person to authenticate or reject the transaction within the time window prescribed by the LAB and in a manner compliant with paragraph 16FZ ibid.
 16FX. Subsequent to registration of the trusted person, an LAB shall send an acknowledgement to the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication, informing them of the successful registration.
 16FY. An LAB shall observe a 24 hour cooling period before the TPM is activated for a customer. Upon activation of the TPM, the LAB shall promptly notify the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication.
 AA.2A.2.3 Authentication process for transactions under TPM
 16FZ. Any transaction beyond the threshold indicated by the customer will be notified to the trusted person for authentication through the available channels of communication. The notification shall include the amount of transaction, beneficiary details [viz., name, account number, mobile number, etc.,] to which the amount is being transferred and narration (if any) entered by the customer while initiating the transaction. A trusted person shall have a one-hour window from being notified, to give consent to the transaction through the trusted mode as prescribed by the LAB for TPM. The transaction shall be executed only upon the trusted person’s consent to the transaction, subject to the LAB’s fraud risk controls and other applicable requirements. In case there is a negative response or there is no response from the trusted person within the prescribed time window as above, the transaction shall be rejected.
 16FZA. The consent of the trusted person to authenticate a transaction may be taken either through physical / digital signature or any other form of authentication given in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The LAB shall also maintain appropriate logs / records of the same.
 16FZB. An LAB shall ensure that the trusted person is not privy to aspects pertaining to the customer’s banking relationship (including but not limited to account balance, fixed deposits, investments, or insurance details) at any stage, including during transaction validation. The role of the trusted person shall be strictly limited to the transaction authentication.
 AA.2A.2.4 Customer controls
 16FZC. An LAB shall provide customers with controls to change an existing trusted person, modify the threshold amount or payment channels chosen for the TPM, or opting out of the TPM itself. Exercise of such controls shall be subject to a cooling period of 24 hours and shall be authenticated by the customer. Further, if a customer is assessed to be more vulnerable to falling prey to cyber-enabled financial crimes / frauds, the LAB shall resort to additional checks, e.g. requiring a mandatory branch visit or a tele-verification call, etc.
 16FZD. In case of change or removal of a trusted person, an LAB shall notify both the customer and the outgoing trusted person through the available communication channels of the change before it takes effect.
 AA.2A.2.5 Implementation and customer awareness
 16FZE. An LAB shall give wide publicity to the availability of the TPM and provide guidance to customers regarding its applicability and features. Such communications shall be disseminated in English, Hindi and local language of the region through all available channels of customer outreach available to the LAB, such as branches, SMS, email, etc. The LAB shall ensure that the communication explicitly delineates the role of the trusted person, benefits and limitations of the TPM, etc.”
 (R Sathish)
 Chief General Manager
 | 

 |
```

```text
 at the time of their issue, all cards (physical and virtual) shall be enabled for use only at contact-based points of usage (viz. ATMs and Point of Sale (PoS) devices) within India.

 at the time of their re-issue, the existing card controls shall be mapped to re-issued cards.

 forex prepaid cards shall be enabled for both contact, and contactless points of usage outside India at the time of their issue / re-issue.

 (2) in case of other digital payment channels, where an RRB has enabled a particular channel for a customer at the time of customer onboarding or subsequently, it shall specify a ceiling on the aggregate value of fund transfers that the customer can undertake across the channel over the initial period of 24 hours, based on the RRB's risk assessment. After the initial period of 24 hours, the RRB may provide for gradual enhancements to the ceiling, based on its channel risk assessment and internal policy. The RRB shall allow modification of the initial or enhanced ceiling (if implemented) through the exercise of customer controls provided at paragraph 128FC above and subject to compliance with the applicable authentication requirements. However, such modification shall be allowed only after the initial period of 24 hours has lapsed post activation of the digital payment channel.
 128FM. The facilities for activation, modification and deactivation of customer-induced controls and Stop Switch shall be made available to all customers through the available points of customer interface such as branches, ATMs, internet banking, mobile banking, Interactive Voice Response (IVR), etc.
 128FN. Upon any activation, modification, deactivation or re-activation of any of such facilities, an RRB shall immediately notify the customers through the available channels of communication, including but not limited to SMS and e-mail.
 128FO. An RRB shall maintain tamper proof audit logs of controls and the Stop Switch initiated by customers to facilitate review and resolution of disputes.
 128FP. An RRB shall undertake ongoing outreach efforts on an ongoing basis to inform customers regarding availability of the customer-induced controls and Stop Switch facility and attendant aspects such as process to activate or deactivate the same, implications of the activation, etc.
 EA.2A.2 Authentication through Trusted Person Mechanism
 EA.2A.2.1 Applicability
 128FQ. An RRB shall put in place a mechanism, called the Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM), to enable customers to register a trusted person to act as an additional factor of transaction authentication. The TPM shall apply to electronic fund transfers initiated through the physical and digital channels available under such customer’s account beyond the threshold set by the customer, except for transactions initiated for:
 payments made through the UPI channel linked to the customer’s account;

 merchant payments, irrespective of the payment channel or instrument used; and

 recurring payments through standing instructions, e-mandates or NACH mandates.

 128FR. An RRB shall offer the TPM to all its customers, whose availment shall be entirely voluntary, based on explicit requests of the customer and the trusted person, and are subject to the thresholds put in place by the customer.
 128FS. The TPM shall be available in bank accounts operated by individuals solely or in such joint accounts operated under any of the survivorship clauses.
 EA.2A.2.2 Registration and onboarding of trusted person
 128FT. An RRB shall facilitate, through its physical and digital channels, the registration of a trusted person, activation of the TPM, and configuration of related transaction-level thresholds by customers.
 128FU. For registering a trusted person, an RRB shall:
 obtain the trusted person’s name, mobile number, email address and copy of at least one Officially Valid Document (OVD);

 verify the identity and eligibility of the trusted person on the basis of the OVD and such other information or documentation as may be reasonably required; and

 verify the mobile number and email address of the trusted person through an appropriate authentication mechanism.

 128FV. The mobile number registered for the trusted person shall be distinct from the mobile number linked to the customer’s account.
 128FW. An RRB, while obtaining the consent for TPM registration, shall clearly inform the customer and the trusted person that registration under the mechanism:
 does not confer upon the trusted person the status of a joint account holder, nominee, mandate holder or authorised signatory;

 does not grant the trusted person any right, title or beneficial interest in the account;

 does not authorise the trusted person to independently access or operate the account, initiate any transaction, or otherwise issue instructions in relation to the account;

 does not result in the trusted person incurring any financial liability when she / he approves or rejects a transaction; and

 requires the trusted person to authenticate or reject the transaction within the time window prescribed by the RRB and in a manner compliant with paragraph 128FZ ibid.

 128FX. Subsequent to registration of the trusted person, an RRB shall send an acknowledgement to the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication, informing them of the successful registration.
 128FY. An RRB shall observe a 24 hour cooling period before the TPM is activated for a customer. Upon activation of the TPM, the RRB shall promptly notify the customer and the trusted person through the available channels of communication.
 EA.2A.2.3 Authentication process for transactions under TPM
 128FZ. Any transaction beyond the threshold indicated by the customer will be notified to the trusted person for authentication through the available channels of communication. The notification shall include the amount of transaction, beneficiary details [viz., name, account number, mobile number, etc.,] to which the amount is being transferred and narration (if any) entered by the customer while initiating the transaction. A trusted person shall have a one-hour window from being notified, to give consent to the transaction through the trusted mode as prescribed by the RRB for TPM. The transaction shall be executed only upon the trusted person’s consent to the transaction, subject to the RRB’s fraud risk controls and other applicable requirements. In case there is a negative response or there is no response from the trusted person within the prescribed time window as above, the transaction shall be rejected.
 128FZA. The consent of the trusted person to authenticate a transaction may be taken either through physical / digital signature or any other form of authentication given in Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions dated September 25, 2025, as amended from time to time. The RRB shall also maintain appropriate logs / records of the same.
 128FZB. An RRB shall ensure that the trusted person is not privy to aspects pertaining to the customer’s banking relationship (including but not limited to account balance, fixed deposits, investments, or insurance details) at any stage, including during transaction validation. The role of the trusted person shall be strictly limited to the transaction authentication.
 EA.2A.2.4 Customer controls
 128FZC. An RRB shall provide customers with controls to change an existing trusted person, modify the threshold amount or payment channels chosen for the TPM, or opting out of the TPM itself. Exercise of such controls shall be subject to a cooling period of 24 hours and shall be authenticated by the customer. Further, if a customer is assessed to be more vulnerable to falling prey to cyber-enabled financial crimes / frauds, the RRB shall resort to additional checks, e.g. requiring a mandatory branch visit or a tele-verification call, etc.
 128FZD. In case of change or removal of a trusted person, an RRB shall notify both the customer and the outgoing trusted person through the available communication channels of the change before it takes effect.
 EA.2A.2.5 Implementation and customer awareness
 128FZE. An RRB shall give wide publicity to the availability of the TPM and provide guidance to customers regarding its applicability and features. Such communications shall be disseminated in English, Hindi and local language of the region through all available channels of customer outreach available to the RRB, such as branches, SMS, email, etc. The RRB shall ensure that the communication explicitly delineates the role of the trusted person, benefits and limitations of the TPM, etc.”
 (R Sathish)
 Chief General Manager
 | 

 |
```

- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/notification/PDFs/NT3043637FDEB03CF4D13A0F337D17BF78F0B.PDF
- **effective date:** April 01, 2027
- **local text file name:** RBI-N13753.txt

```text
(394 kb) | 
Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 | 
 RBI/2026-27/304
 DOR.STR.REC.256/21-04-177/2026-27
 November 23, 2026
 Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026
 Please refer to Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions) Directions, 2025.
 2. On a review, and in exercise of the powers conferred by the section 21 and 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in the public interest so to do, hereby issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified.
 3. The Amendment Directions shall come into effect from April 01, 2027.
 4. The Amendment Directions modify the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions) Directions, 2025 as under:
 (1) Paragraph 27 shall be substituted by the following, namely:
 “27. The issuance, holding and subsequent transfer of securitisation notes under these Directions shall only be in a dematerialised form. The minimum ticket size shall be ₹1 crore at the time of issuance as well as at any subsequent transfers. The originator shall ensure that the agreement with the SPE requires the latter to put in place necessary arrangements with entities such as the registrar, depository, stock exchange etc., as may be applicable, to ensure compliance with the minimum ticket-size requirement.
 Provided that securitisation notes with amortisation structures shall be permitted to be traded at amortised value, if the ticket size falls below ₹1 crore.
 Explanation: Ticket size, for the purpose of these directions, refers to the size of investment by a single investor.”
 (2) Paragraph 28 shall be substituted by the following, namely:
 “28. With respect to offer of securitisation notes to the public, Regulation 21 of SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008, as amended from time to time, shall be complied with.”
 (3) Paragraph 28A shall be inserted as below:
 “28A. Transactions in securitisation notes issued prior to April 01, 2027, shall also be undertaken in compliance with the requirements mentioned in Paragraph 27 & 28 above.”
 (Vaibhav Chaturvedi)
 Chief General Manager
 | 

 |
```

## [rbi] 2026-11-23 | RBI releases 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-23
- **kind:** Press release
- **exact title:** RBI releases 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)
- **reference number:** Press Release: 2026-2027/1547
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64025
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/PR154776E60D974F0545EA975A0B550C301D87.PDF
- **local text file name:** RBI-PR64025.txt

```text
(296 kb) | 
 Date : Nov 23, 2026 | 
RBI releases 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) | 
 State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank continue to be identified as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) under the same bucketing structure as in the 2025 list of D-SIBs. The additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) requirement for these D-SIBs will be in addition to the capital conservation buffer.
 The list of D-SIBs is as follows:
 Bucket | Banks | Additional Common Equity Tier 1 requirement as a percentage of Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) | 
 5 | - | 1% | 
 4 | State Bank of India | 0.80% | 
 3 | - | 0.60% | 
 2 | HDFC Bank | 0.40% | 
 1 | ICICI Bank | 0.20% | 

Background:
The Reserve Bank had issued the Framework for dealing with Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) on July 22, 2014, which was subsequently updated on December 28, 2023. The D-SIB framework requires the Reserve Bank to disclose the names of banks designated as D-SIBs starting from 2015 and place these banks in appropriate buckets depending upon their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs). Based on the bucket in which a D-SIB is placed, an additional common equity requirement has to be applied to it. In case a foreign bank having branch presence in India is a Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB), it has to maintain additional CET1 capital surcharge in India as applicable to it as a G-SIB, proportionate to its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) in India, i.e., additional CET1 buffer prescribed by the home regulator (amount) multiplied by India RWA as per consolidated global Group books divided by total consolidated global Group RWA.
The Reserve Bank had announced SBI and ICICI Bank as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016 while HDFC Bank was classified as D-SIB in 2017 along with SBI and ICICI Bank. The current update is based on the data collected from banks as on March 31, 2026.
(Brij Raj) 
 Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/1547
 | 

 |
```

## [rbi] 2026-11-23 | RBI issues Draft Amendment Directions for ‘Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)’

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-23
- **kind:** Press release - draft for comments
- **exact title:** RBI issues Draft Amendment Directions for ‘Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)’
- **reference number:** Press Release: 2026-2027/1548
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64026
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/PR15481A16A331A8154221B1B3889AD4D0008D.PDF
- **comment deadline (drafts):** December 14, 2026
- **local text file name:** RBI-PR64026.txt

```text
(313 kb) | 
 Date : Nov 23, 2026 | 
RBI issues Draft Amendment Directions for ‘Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)’ | 
 The Reserve Bank had issued the Amendment Directions dated June 24, 2026 on ‘Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions’ which, inter alia, strengthened the existing framework for limiting liability of customers in unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs). While the revised framework primarily addresses customer liability in the event of fraudulent EBTs, a need is felt to strengthen the same from a preventive perspective by providing customers with greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels may be used.
 Further, on a review to bring in uniformity in practices adopted by banks and ensure that customers are protected against specific acts of omission or commission on part of the banks, it has been decided to expand the scope of the definition of ‘negligence by a bank’ specified in the aforementioned Amendment Directions.
 2. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the following draft Amendment Directions for public comments, which propose to amend Directions on Responsible Business Conduct issued by the Department of Regulation, RBI:
 Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026

 Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026

 Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026

 Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026

 Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026

 Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026

 Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026

 3. The comments / feedback on the draft Amendment Directions may be submitted by the regulated entities and members of public / other stakeholders on or before December 14, 2026 through the following channels:
 the ‘Connect 2 Regulate’ section on the website by following the corresponding hyperlink provided against each document in the page where they are hosted; or

 by email with the subject line ‘Feedback on (full name of the draft Amendment Directions (including the type of Regulated Entity))’.

 (Brij Raj) 
 Chief General Manager
 Press Release: 2026-2027/1548
 | 

 |
```

## [rbi] 2026-11-23 | Governor, Reserve Bank of India meets Chairpersons and Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers of select UCBs and Industry Representatives in Mumbai on No

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-23
- **kind:** Press release
- **exact title:** Governor, Reserve Bank of India meets Chairpersons and Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers of select UCBs and Industry Representatives in Mumbai on No
- **reference number:** Press Release: 2026-2027/1553
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64031
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/PR15530CC45C3FF1644BD8844402C076202FF7.PDF
- **local text file name:** RBI-PR64031.txt

```text
(170 kb) | 
 Date : Nov 23, 2026 | 
Governor, Reserve Bank of India meets Chairpersons and Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers of select UCBs and Industry Representatives in Mumbai on November 23, 2026 | 
 As part of the Reserve Bank of India's continued engagement with regulated entities, the Governor today met in Mumbai with the Chairpersons and Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) across different tiers.
 Representatives of the National Urban Cooperative Finance and Development Corporation Limited and the National Federation of Urban Co-operative Banks & Credit Societies Limited also participated.
 The meeting was also attended by Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S. C. Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank.
 In his opening remarks, the Governor noted that credit growth in the sector had improved, while growth in profitability had lagged. He emphasised the need to strengthen governance standards and support sustainable growth through prudent lending, with due regard to borrowers' repayment capacity.
 The Governor welcomed participants' positive feedback on Mission SAKSHAM, the Reserve Bank's ongoing training initiative for UCBs, and urged banks to make full use of it. As UCBs adopt technology, he advised them to put robust cybersecurity frameworks in place, underscoring that cyber risk affects banks of every size. He also emphasised the importance of customer centricity and of maintaining high standards in internal grievance redressal.
 Participants offered feedback and suggestions on policy and operational matters concerning the UCB sector.
 (Brij Raj) 
 Chief General Manager
 Press Release: 2026-2027/1553
 | 

 |
```

```text
(314 kb) | 
 Date : Nov 23, 2026 | 
Governor, Reserve Bank of India meets Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers of select NBFCs, HFCs and Industry Representatives in Mumbai on November 23, 2026 | 
 As part of the Reserve Bank’s ongoing engagement with regulated entities, the Governor, Reserve Bank of India, today met in Mumbai with the Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), including Government NBFCs, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Microfinance Institutions.
 Representatives of Sa-Dhan, the Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN) and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) also participated.
 Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S. C. Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain attended the meeting, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank. The MD & CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated.
 The Governor acknowledged the role of NBFCs and HFCs in supporting economic activity by widening access to credit. He emphasised the need for responsible and sustainable credit growth and urged NBFCs to put customers first as they expand their business. He highlighted the importance of quality service, effective grievance redressal and fair recovery practices. He also encouraged NBFCs to use the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) for customer onboarding and to keep customer records in the registry up to date to improve customer convenience.
 The Governor urged participants to strengthen their cybersecurity infrastructure and adopt a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber and IT risks, with appropriate oversight by their boards and senior management.
 Participants shared feedback on policy and operational matters concerning the NBFC sector.
 (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager
 Press Release: 2026-2027/1554
 | 

 |
```

## [rbi] 2026-11-20 | FAQs: National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) System

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-20
- **kind:** FAQ (updated)
- **exact title:** FAQs: National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) System
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/FAQDisplay.aspx?Id=60
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/faqs/PDFs/FAQNEFT20112026.PDF
- **local text file name:** RBI-FAQ60.txt
- **note:** Date is the "updated" date shown on the RBI FAQ listing.

```text
193 kb | 
 Date : Nov 20, 2026 | 
National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) System | 
 (Updated as on November 20, 2026)

 1. What is National Electronic Funds Transfer system?

 Ans: National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) is a nation-wide centralised payment system owned and operated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The set of procedures to be followed by various stakeholders participating in the system is available on the RBI website under the following link: https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/CONTENT/PDFs/NEFTPROCEDURAL27102026628C3B5E957A4B7A931C27AF7E84C5D4.PDF

 2. What are the advantages of using NEFT system?

 Ans: NEFT offers the following advantages for funds transfer or receipt:

 Round the clock availability on all days of the year.

 Near-real-time funds transfer to the beneficiary account and settlement in a secure manner.

 Pan-India coverage through large network of branches of all types of banks.

 The beneficiary need not visit a bank branch for depositing the paper instruments. Remitter can initiate the remittances from his / her home / place of work using internet banking, if his / her bank offers such service.

 Positive confirmation to the remitter by SMS / e-mail on credit to beneficiary account.

 Penal interest provision for delay in credit or return of transactions.

 No levy of charges by RBI from banks. 

 No charges to savings bank account customers for online NEFT transactions.

 The transaction charges have been capped by RBI.

 Besides funds transfer, NEFT system can be used for a variety of transactions including payment of credit card dues to the card issuing banks, payment of loan EMI, inward foreign exchange remittances, etc.

 The transaction has legal backing.

 Available for one-way funds transfers from India to Nepal.

 3. How does the NEFT system operate?

 Ans: Following is the stepwise flow of NEFT transaction.

 Step-1: An individual / firm / corporate willing to transfer funds through NEFT can use the internet / mobile banking facility offered by his / her bank for initiating online funds transfer request. The remitter has to provide details of beneficiary such as, name of the beneficiary, name of the bank branch where the beneficiary has an account, IFSC of the beneficiary bank branch, account type and account number, etc. for addition of the beneficiary to his / her internet / mobile banking module. Upon successful beneficiary addition, the remitter can initiate online NEFT funds transfer by authorising debit to his / her account. Alternatively, the remitter can also visit his / her bank branch for initiating NEFT funds transfer through branch / off-line mode. The customer has to fill-in the beneficiary details in NEFT application form available at the bank branch and authorise the branch to debit to his / her account to the extent of the amount requested in NEFT application form.

 Step-2: The originating bank prepares a message and sends the message to its pooling centre, also called the NEFT Service Centre.

 Step-3: The pooling centre forwards the message to the NEFT Processing Centre, operated by the RBI, to be included for the next available batch.

 Step-4: The Processing Centre sorts the funds transfer transactions beneficiary bank-wise and prepares accounting entries to receive funds from the originating banks (debit) and give the funds to the beneficiary banks (credit). Thereafter, bank-wise remittance messages are forwarded to the beneficiary banks through their pooling centre (NEFT Service Centre).

 Step-5: The beneficiary banks receive the inward remittance messages from the Processing Centre and pass on the credit to the beneficiary customers’ accounts.

 4. What is Indian Financial System Code?

 Ans: Indian Financial System Code (IFSC) is an alpha-numeric code that uniquely identifies a bank-branch participating in the NEFT system. It is an 11-digit code with the first 4 alpha characters representing the bank, and the last 6 characters representing the branch. The 5th character is 0 (zero). IFSC is used by the NEFT system to identify the originating / destination banks / branches and also to route the messages appropriately to the concerned banks / branches.

 5. How can I find the IFSC of a bank-branch?

 Ans: Bank-wise list of IFSCs is available with all the bank-branches participating in NEFT scheme. List of bank-wise branches participating in NEFT and their IFSCs is also available on the website of RBI at https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/bs_viewcontent.aspx?Id=2009. All member banks have also been advised to print the IFSC of the branch on cheques issued to their customers.

 6. Who can avail NEFT system for fund transfer / receipt?

 Ans: Individuals, firms and corporates maintaining accounts with any member bank, participating in the NEFT system, can electronically transfer funds to any individual, firm or corporate having an account with any other bank in the country participating in the NEFT system.

 The list of bank-wise branches participating in NEFT is available on the website of RBI at https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/bs_viewcontent.aspx?Id=2009.

 7. Is there any limit on funds / amount to be remitted through NEFT system?

 Ans: No, there is no limit imposed by the RBI for funds transfer through NEFT system. However, a member bank may place amount limits based on its own risk perception with the approval of its Board.

 8. Can the NEFT system be used for remitting funds even by those who do not have a bank account?

 Ans: Yes, a person who does not have a bank account can remit funds through NEFT to a beneficiary having a bank account, with another NEFT member bank. It can be done by depositing cash at the nearest NEFT enabled branch of any bank, by furnishing additional details such as complete address, telephone number, etc. Such cash remittances will, however, be restricted to a maximum of ₹50,000 per transaction.

 9. Can I send funds to my relative / friend residing abroad through NEFT system?

 Ans: The outbound remittances through NEFT system are permitted only to Nepal under Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility (INRF) Scheme. Under this Scheme, the remitter can transfer funds from any of the NEFT-enabled bank branches in India to Nepal, irrespective of whether the beneficiary in Nepal maintains an account with a bank branch in Nepal or not. The beneficiary would receive funds in Nepalese Rupees. To better understand the INRF Scheme please refer to FAQs available on the website of RBI at https://rbi.org.in/scripts/FAQView.aspx?Id=67.

 10. What are the operating hours of NEFT?

 Ans: The NEFT system is available round the clock throughout the year on all days, i.e., on 24x7x365 basis. NEFT presently operates in batches on half-hourly intervals throughout the day. In case of non-availability of NEFT for any reason, appropriate message will be broadcasted by RBI to all system participants.

 11. What are the essential details required for remitting funds through NEFT system?

 Ans: The essential elements of beneficiary's identification are:

 Beneficiary's Name

 Beneficiary's Branch Name

 Beneficiary's Bank Name

 Beneficiary's Account Type

 Beneficiary's Account No. 

 Beneficiary's Branch IFSC

 Sender and Beneficiary Legal Entity Identifier (for eligible transactions)

 12. What are the customer charges levied by bank for NEFT transactions?

 Ans: There are no charges to be levied for inward transactions at destination bank branches for giving credit to beneficiary accounts.

 For outward transactions undertaken using the NEFT system, RBI stopped levying processing charges on member banks from July 01, 2019.

 Also, in order to give further impetus to digital retail payments, banks have been advised not to levy any charges from their savings bank account holders for NEFT funds transfers initiated online with effect from January 01, 2020.

 The maximum charges which originating bank can levy from its customers for other outward transactions, if they so desire, are given below:

 - For transactions up to ₹10,000: not exceeding ₹2.50 (+ Applicable GST)

 - For transactions above ₹10,000 up to ₹1 lakh: not exceeding ₹5 (+ Applicable GST)

 - For transactions above ₹1 lakh and up to ₹2 lakhs: not exceeding ₹15 (+ Applicable GST)

 - For transactions above ₹2 lakhs: not exceeding ₹25 (+ Applicable GST)

 The details about charges applicable for transferring funds from India to Nepal using the NEFT system under the INRF Scheme is available on the RBI website at https://rbi.org.in/scripts/FAQView.aspx?Id=67.

 13. Can I use NEFT to transfer funds from / to NRE and NRO accounts?

 Ans: Yes, NEFT can be used to transfer funds from / to NRE and NRO accounts in the country. This, however, is subject to the adherence of the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 2000 (FEMA) and Wire Transfer Guidelines.

 14. Can I originate a NEFT transaction to draw / receive funds from another account?

 Ans: No. NEFT is a credit-push system i.e., transactions can be originated by the payer / remitter / sender only to pay / transfer / remit funds to beneficiary.

 15. How can I track status of NEFT transactions initiated? Who should be approached to know status of the NEFT transaction?

 Ans: The remitter and the beneficiary can track status of NEFT transaction by contacting NEFT Customer Facilitation Centre (CFC) of their bank, respectively. Details of NEFT CFCs of banks are available on the websites of the respective banks. The details of CFC of member banks are also available on the website of RBI at https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/bs_viewcontent.aspx?Id=2070.

 For faster tracking of transaction, you may need to provide a few details related to transaction such as Unique Transaction Reference (UTR) number / transaction reference number, date of transaction, sender IFSC, amount, beneficiary name, beneficiary IFSC, etc., to your bank. 

 16. What is the Help Desk / Contact point at the RBI?

 Ans: The NEFT Help Desk / Contact point of the RBI can be approached at nefthelpdeskncc@rbi.org.in. 

 17. How much time should I expect for receipt of funds by beneficiary?

 Ans: A timeline of two hours from the batch settlement can be expected, within which beneficiary’s account should be credited. 

 18. What happens if I write wrong account number of beneficiary?

 Ans: The credit is given to the account number written / given by remitter in his / her application / instruction. Credit to beneficiary account is released solely based on account number. It is the responsibility of remitting customer to write correct account number. The originator / sender should exercise due care in providing the correct account number of the beneficiary, in the NEFT remittance instruction / application.

 19. For an NEFT transaction what should be mandatorily given in a customer account statement?

 Ans: NEFT Members/banks shall mandatorily provide Sender Name (the ordering customer) and Creditor Name (the beneficiary customer). The member participants/banks shall furnish name of the beneficiary in the passbook / account statement of originator and name of ordering customer in the passbook / account statement of beneficiary.

 20. What is beneficiary bank account name look-up facility and how can it be used?

 Ans: This is a free facility which allows a remitter to verify the beneficiary bank’s account holder's name (as registered in beneficiary bank’s Core Banking Solution) before initiating a fund transfer. It helps to prevent fraud and wrong-account routing.

 21. Whom should I approach for raising dispute / complaint related to NEFT transaction?

 Ans: You may approach grievance redressal cell of your bank with details of the disputed transaction. In case your grievance is not resolved as per the timeline prescribed in “The Reserve Bank-Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS 2026)”, you may lodge a complaint under the said Scheme. . The RB-IOS 2026 provides a single reference point for customers to file complaints against the RBI regulated entities specified therein. The RB-IOS, 2026 is available at the following path on the RBI website: https://cms.rbi.org.in/cms/assets/Documents/Ombudsman_Scheme_English.pdf.

 22. What are the practices which should be adopted by a customer for safe and secure digital payments?

 Ans: The webpage of RBI- “RBI Kehta Hai” at https://rbikehtahai.rbi.org.in/ for information regarding ways to ensure safe and secure digital payments can be referred to. 

 23. What is Legal Entity Identifier and how is it relevant in case of large value NEFT transactions?

 Ans: The FAQs on “Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) for Large Value Transactions in Centralised Payment Systems” on the RBI website at https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/FAQView.aspx?Id=140 can be referred to.

 24. Are there special NEFT requirements for FCRA-related transactions?

 Ans. Yes. NEFT members must use the prescribed transaction type codes for transactions relating to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, wherever applicable. Customers undertaking such transactions need to provide accurate purpose and related information to their bank.

 25. What is the process for applying for the membership of NEFT?

 Ans: The entity desirous of becoming NEFT member should be an RTGS member or it should seek approval for both RTGS and NEFT at the time of applying for approval for membership of Centralised Payment Systems (CPS). The procedure for applying for CPS membership has been provided in NEFT Procedural Guidelines which can be accessed at https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/CONTENT/PDFs/NEFTPROCEDURAL27102026628C3B5E957A4B7A931C27AF7E84C5D4.PDF.

 These FAQs are issued by the Reserve Bank of India for information and general guidance purposes only. The Bank will not be held responsible for actions taken and/or decisions made on the basis of the same. For clarifications or interpretations, if any, one may be guided by the relevant circulars and notifications issued from time to time by the Bank.
```

## [rbi] 2026-11-20 | RBI imposes monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-20
- **kind:** Press release - penalty
- **exact title:** RBI imposes monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited
- **reference number:** Press Release: 2026-2027/1537
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64015
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/PressRelease/PDFs/PR15371CFC7ACEA1EB441DAABD793CBC2F8C7D.PDF
- **local text file name:** RBI-PR64015.txt

```text
(306 kb) | 
 Date : Nov 20, 2026 | 
RBI imposes monetary penalty on Fusion Finance Limited | 
 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 17, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹7.50 lakh (Rupees Seven Lakh Fifty Thousand only) on Fusion Finance Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of directions issued by RBI on ‘Know Your Customer (KYC)’ and ‘Internal Ombudsman’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under section 58G(1)(b) read with section 58B(5)(aa) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its financial position as on March 31, 2026. Based on the supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for failure to comply with the RBI directions.
 After considering the company's reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty:
 The company failed to obtain PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form 60 from customers, while establishing an account-based relationship with those customers; and,

 The company failed to escalate the partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman for a final decision within the prescribed time.

 This action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of this monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company.
 (Brij Raj) 
 Chief General Manager
 Press Release: 2026-2027/1537
 | 

 |
```

## [rbi] 2026-11-17 | FAQs: Inter-operable Regulatory Sandbox (IoRS)

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-17
- **kind:** FAQ (updated)
- **exact title:** FAQs: Inter-operable Regulatory Sandbox (IoRS)
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/FAQDisplay.aspx?Id=174
- **official PDF URL:** https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/faqs/PDFs/IORSFAQ11092025_ENG.PDF
- **local text file name:** RBI-FAQ174.txt
- **note:** Date is the "updated" date shown on the RBI FAQ listing.

```text
140 kb | 
 Date : Nov 17, 2026 | 
Inter-operable Regulatory Sandbox (IoRS) | 

(Updated as on November 17, 2026)

 These FAQs provide a comprehensive overview of the Inter-operable Regulatory Sandbox (IoRS) initiative and address common queries from potential participants:

 Q1. What is Regulatory Sandbox?

 Regulatory Sandbox usually refers to live testing of new products or services in a controlled/test regulatory environment for which regulators may permit certain regulatory relaxations for the limited purpose of the testing.

 Q2. Which regulators/authorities in India have initiatives for regulatory sandbox?

 Financial Sector regulators/ authorities in India have established regulatory sandboxes to foster innovation in their respective domains. These include:

 Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

 Link: https://fintech.rbi.org.in/FS_Publications?id=1262

 Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

 Link: https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/jun-2021/revised-framework-for-regulatory-sandbox_50521.html

 Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

 Link: https://irdai.gov.in/document-detail?documentId=6541188

 Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)

 Link: https://www.pfrda.org.in/web/pfrda/d/pfrda-regulatory-sandbox-regulations-

 2026?p_l_back_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pfrda.org.in%2Fweb%2Fpfrda%2Fsear

 ch%3Fmode%3Ddropdown%26type%3Dcom.liferay.journal.model.JournalArticle%2

 6type%3Dcom.liferay.portal.kernel.model.Layout&p_l_back_url_title=Search

 International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA)

 Link: https://ifsca.gov.in/Viewer?Path=Document%2FLegal%2Ffe-framework_27-04-

 202227042022122844.pdf&Title=Framework%20for%20FinTech%20Entity%20in%2

 0the%20International%20Financial%20Services%20Centres%20%28IFSCs%29&D

 ate=27%2F04%2F2022

 Q3. What is the genesis of Inter-operable Regulatory Sandbox (IoRS) initiative?

 An Inter-Regulatory Technical Group on FinTech (IRTG on FinTech) was constituted under the aegis of the Financial Stability and Development Council-Sub Committee (FSDC-SC). The terms of reference (ToR) of IRTG on FinTech included discussion on issues relating to hybrid product/ service falling under the regulatory ambit of more than one financial sector regulator for admission in Regulatory Sandbox and framing of Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for IoRS for hybrid products/services. The group, in addition to the members from Financial Sector Regulators/ Authority (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA and IFSCA), has representation from Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeITY), GoI. In order to facilitate testing of innovative products/services falling within the regulatory ambit of more than one financial sector regulator, a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for IoRS has been prepared by the Inter-Regulatory Technical Group on FinTech (IRTG on FinTech). The SOP can be accessed from the link: FinTech

 Q4. What is Inter-operable Regulatory Sandbox (IoRS)?

 The Inter-operable Regulatory Sandbox (IoRS) provides a common window for innovators to test hybrid financial products/ services falling within the regulatory ambit of more than one financial sector regulator. By eliminating the need to separately engage with different regulators, IoRS simplifies testing processes and fosters innovation in the financial ecosystem.

 Q5. How is the IoRS different from individual Regulatory Sandboxes?

 The IoRS supports innovation that requires collaboration between multiple regulators while the individual sandboxes of regulators cater to the solutions within the purview of a single regulator. Thus, IoRS is a unified mechanism that bridges the complexities of bespoke regulatory sandbox frameworks of different financial sector regulators and helps in fostering cross-sectoral innovation.

 Q6. Which regulators/authority are involved in the IoRS initiative?

 The initiative involves collaboration between multiple regulators:

 Reserve Bank of India (RBI) – for banking and payment systems

 Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) – for securities markets

 Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) – for insurance products

 Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) – for pension-related innovations

 International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) – unified Regulatory authority of Gujarat International Finance Tech-City International Financial Services Centre (GIFT IFSC) for testing in the domain areas as specified in the Annexure I of Framework for FinTech Entity in the International Financial Services Centres.

 Q7. Who can participate in the IoRS?

 Generally, following entities can participate in the IoRS: Financial institutions, FinTech companies, RegTech providers, Start-ups or other innovators offering products/services relevant to multiple financial sectors.

 However, the eligibility criteria will be governed primarily by the RS Framework of the Principal Regulator (Details given under FAQ Question 2)

 Q8. What types of products or services can be tested under IoRS?

 IoRS allows the testing of financial products or services whose features fall within the remit of more than one financial sector regulator (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA and IFSCA). Some of such innovative solutions include, the areas of RegTech and SupTech, Digital Payment Solutions, Cross-sectoral products for e.g. insurance products linked to banking services InsurTech, WealthTech, Cross-border payment solutions etc.

 Q9. What are the benefits of participating in the IoRS?

 Testing of innovative solutions in a controlled, low-risk environment.

 Interaction with multiple regulators through single window to ensure compliance across domains.

 Opportunity to refine products based on feedback from regulators and the sandbox testing.

 Reduced time to market for innovative solutions.

 Q10. Who is the Principal Regulator (PR) and Associate Regulator (AR) under IoRS?

 The RS framework of the regulator under whose remit the dominant/ majority feature of the product falls, will be the ‘Principal Regulator (PR)’ under IoRS. The regulator/s under whose remit the other features apart from the dominant feature of the product fall shall be the ‘Associate Regulator (AR)’ under IoRS.

 Q11. How is the dominant feature of a product determined?

 The dominant feature is assessed based on two factors:

 The type of enhancement to existing financial products (e.g., loans, deposits, insurance, pension products).

 The number of relaxations sought for the product during the testing process, with greater weightage given to the latter.

 The relaxation, if warranted, shall be considered by PR/ AR on case-to-case basis and decision to that effect shall be binding and final.

 Q12. What are the eligibility criteria to participate in IoRS?

 Based on the dominant features of the product, the eligibility criteria and networth criteria as applicable for the RS of the PR concerned shall be applicable to the applicant entity for participation in the IoRS.

 Q13. How can you apply for IoRS?

 You can apply by submitting a single application form to the Coordination Group hosted by the FinTech Department, RBI, via email at iors@rbi.org.in. The application form can be accessed via the link:

 https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/content/pdfs/IoRS12102022_APP.pdf

 Q14. Is there any fee for applying to IoRS?

 No, there is no application fee for applying to IoRS. However, for testing under IoRS the sandbox fee, if any, of the PR concerned may be applicable.

 Q15. Is there a deadline for submitting applications under IoRS?

 No, applications are accepted on an ‘On-Tap’ basis throughout the year.

 Q16. Who will scrutinize the IoRS application, and how will it be processed?

 The preliminary scrutiny will be done by FinTech Department of Reserve Bank of India. However, detailed scrutiny will be done by the PR based on its sandbox framework. The PR will also coordinate with ARs to review specific features of your product that fall under their regulatory scope, ensuring a smooth and efficient process.

 Q17. Are foreign FinTech entities eligible to participate in IoRS?

 Yes, applications from foreign FinTechs seeking entry into India or Indian FinTechs with global ambitions are eligible to participate. For such cases, IFSCA, shall act as the PR.

 Q18. Where and how will the product/ solution be tested and evaluated under IoRS?

 The product/ solution will be tested as per the sandbox framework of the PR in coordination with the ARs. The PR will also evaluate your product based on its framework, incorporating inputs and appraisals from ARs for specific aspects under their jurisdiction to assess its suitability and viability.

 Q19. What is the duration of the IoRS testing phase?

 The testing phase duration will be as per the sandbox framework of the PR concerned.

 Q20. What should I do after my product has been tested under IoRS?

 After successful testing under IoRS, the entity may approach the concerned PR and ARs to obtain necessary authorisations and regulatory approvals before launching its product in the market. The decisions of the respective regulators will be final and binding. The product being successfully exiting the IoRS shall be published by the regulator concerned vide Press Release for wider adoption.

 Q21. Where can you find more information about the IoRS?

 The Standard Operating Procedure for IoRS can be accessed at the link: https://fintech.rbi.org.in/FS_PressRelease?prid=54528&fn=2765

 Q22. Whom to reach out in case of any additional queries?

 For any inquiries, please email at iors@rbi.org.in
 |
```

```text
(317 kb) | 
 Date : Nov 17, 2026 | 
Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 – Nagar Sahakari Bank Ltd., Etawah – Extension of Period | 
 The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to Nagar Sahakari Bank Ltd., Etawah, vide Directive No. LKO.DOS.SED.No.S29/12-03-000/2026-2027 dated May 15, 2026, for a period of six months up to close of business on November 18, 2026. The Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of operation of the Directive beyond close of business on November 18, 2026. 
 2. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India, in the exercise of the powers vested in it under sub-section (1) of Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, hereby extends the Directive for a further period of three months from close of business on November 18, 2026, to close of business on February 18, 2027, subject to review. 
 3. The aforesaid extension and/or modification by the Reserve Bank of India should not per se be construed to imply that the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied with the financial position of the bank.
 4. All other terms and conditions of the Directive under reference, shall remain unchanged.
 (Brij Raj) 
 Chief General Manager
```

## [rbi] 2026-11-16 | FAQs: RBI as Banker to Government

- **section:** rbi
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-16
- **kind:** FAQ (updated)
- **exact title:** FAQs: RBI as Banker to Government
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/FAQDisplay.aspx?Id=61
- **local text file name:** RBI-FAQ61.txt
- **note:** Date is the "updated" date shown on the RBI FAQ listing.

```text
| 
 Date : Nov 16, 2026 | 
RBI as Banker to Government | 

 (Updated as on November 16, 2026)

 1. What is RBI's role with regard to conduct of Government's banking transaction?

 In terms of Section 20 of the RBI Act 1934, RBI has the obligation to undertake the receipts and payments of the Central Government and to carry out the exchange, remittance and other banking operations, including the management of the public debt of the Union. Further, as per Section 21 of the said Act, RBI has the right to transact Government business of the Union in India.

 State Government transactions are carried out by RBI in terms of the agreement entered into with the State Governments in terms of section 21 A of the Act. As of now, such agreements exist between RBI and all the State Governments except Government of Sikkim. However, a limited agreement has been signed with Government of Sikkim for opening and operation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) Single Nodal Agency (SNA) –Samyochit Pranali Ekikrit Shighra Hastantaran (SPARSH) accounts at RBI, Gangtok with no overdraft facility. Thus, the legal provisions vest Reserve Bank of India with both the right and obligation to function as banker to the government.

 2. How does Reserve Bank of India discharge its statutory obligation of being 'Banker to Government'?

 RBI carries out the general banking business of the governments through its own offices and commercial banks, both public and private, appointed as its agents. Section 45 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, provides for appointment of scheduled commercial banks as agents at all places or at any place in India, for purposes that it may specify, “having regard to public interest, convenience of banking, banking development and such other factors which in its opinion are relevant in this regard”.

 Reserve Bank of India maintains the Principal Accounts of Central as well as State Governments at its Central Accounts Section, Nagpur. It has put in place a well-structured arrangement for revenue collection as well as payments on behalf of Government across the country. A network comprising the Government Banking Divisions of RBI and branches of agency banks appointed under Section 45 of the RBI Act carry out the government transactions. At present all the public sector banks and select private sector banks act as RBI's agents. Only designated branches of agency banks can conduct government banking business.

 3. How payment into government account is made?

 All monies for credit to government account like taxes or other remittances can be made by filling the prescribed challans of the Government/Department concerned. The tax payers are encouraged to pay dues to Government electronically by login in to respective government portals. However, if they prefer to pay dues by way of cash, cheque, demand draft, these are required to be tendered with the authorized agency bank branches along with requisite challan.

 4. When is the receipted challan for payment made into government account made available?

 The receipted challans in case of cash tender are generally handed over to the remitter immediately across the counter. In case of payments made by cheque/DD, the receipted challan is issued only on realization of the instruments. Phase 1 of ‘Continuous Clearing and Settlement on Realisation in Cheque Truncation System’ has been implemented from October 04, 2025, resulting in same day settlement of instruments. In all such cases, a paper token is issued to the depositor indicating the date on which the receipted challan will be ready for delivery. The receipted challan will have to be collected within a specified number of days from the date of delivery, as indicated on the paper token, by surrendering the paper token.

 5. What if the paper token is misplaced / lost?

 In case of loss of original token, on a specific request and on payment of prescribed fees, the receipted challan is issued.

 6. What if the Receipted Challan is misplaced?

 No duplicate challan is issued under any circumstances. Instead, a 'Certificate of Credit' is issued on specific request with the requisite particulars and payment of prescribed fee.

 7. Are agency banks compensated for conduct of Central/State Government banking?

 The accredited banks are paid remuneration by RBI for conduct of State/Central Government transactions. Such remuneration is called Agency Commission. The rates of agency commission applicable at present (from April 1, 2025) are as under:

 No. | 
 Type of Transaction | 
 Unit | 
 Revised Rate | 

 a. | 
 (i) | 
 Receipts – Physical mode | 
 Per transaction | 
 ₹ 40/- | 

 (ii) | 
 Receipts – e-mode * | 
 Per transaction | 
 ₹ 12/- | 

 b. | 
 (i) | 
 Payments – Pension | 
 Per transaction | 
 ₹ 80/- | 

 (ii) | 
 Payments – Other than pension | 
 Per ₹ 100 turnover | 
 7 paise | 

 *In this context, it may please be noted that ‘Receipts – e-mode’ indicated against Sl. No. a(ii) in the above table would refer to those transactions involving remittance of funds from the remitter’s bank account through internet banking as well as all such transactions which do not involve physical receipt of cash / instruments. | 

 8. What is RBI’s role in Goods and Service Tax regime?

 The Reserve Bank of India is the aggregator for accounting of all GST collections in the respective government accounts. Agency banks who collect the GST for challans generated by tax payers online on the GST portal report the collections for settlement to government accounts to RBI. RBI has also facilitated payment of GST by tax payers directly into government accounts at RBI by using NEFT / RTGS payment options provided in GST portal.
 |
```

```text
(289 kb) | 
 Date : Nov 13, 2026 | 
Reserve Bank of India imposes monetary penalty on One Mobikwik Systems Limited | 
 Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has, by an order dated November 06, 2026, imposed a monetary penalty of ₹9.00 lakh (Rupees Nine Lakh only) on One Mobikwik Systems Limited (the company) for non-compliance with certain provisions of the directions issued by RBI on ‘Prepaid Payment lnstruments (PPIs)’ and ‘Fraud reporting’. This penalty has been imposed in exercise of powers conferred on RBI under the provisions of section 30(1) read with section 26(6) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
 The statutory inspection of the company was conducted by RBI with reference to its operations for the period from June 2025 to March 2026. Based on supervisory findings of non-compliance with RBI directions and related correspondence in that regard, a notice was issued to the company advising it to show cause as to why penalty should not be imposed on it for its failure to comply with the said RBI directions.
 After considering the company’s reply to the notice, additional submissions made by it and oral submissions made during the personal hearing, RBI found that the following charges against the company were sustained, warranting imposition of monetary penalty:
 the company had allowed fund transfer by certain PPI holders to non-pre-registered beneficiaries beyond the prescribed limit.

 the company failed to report certain frauds within the prescribed timeline.

 The action is based on deficiencies in regulatory compliance and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the company with its customers. Further, imposition of monetary penalty is without prejudice to any other action that may be initiated by RBI against the company.
 (Brij Raj) 
 Chief General Manager
 Press Release: 2026-2027/1496
```
