```text
आईआरडीएआई द्वारा गवित स्वास्थ्य बीमा संबंिी आईएसी उप-सवमवत िे स्वास्थ्य बीमा दािं

मंे पारदवशिता क बढािे और उत्तरदावयत्व क मजबूत करिेे क विए द अध्ययि दि बिाये हैं।

IAC Sub-Committee on Health Insurance constituted by IRDAI forms two study

groups to enhance transparency and strengthen accountability in health

insurance claims



जैसे-जैसे स्वास्थ्य बीमा कवरेज का ववस्तार हो रहा है, दावा विर्णयोंो में पारदवशणता, समय पर दावा संोबंोधी

अद्यति स्थिवत की जािकारी, तथा दावोंो और वशकायत पररर्ामोंो की सुसंोगत ररपोवटंिग पाविसीधारकोंोे क

विए अवधकावधक महत्वपूर्ण हंै। दावा यात्राे क मािकीृकत मेवटि क्स और तत्काि दृश्यता कायणविष्पादि

के आकिि को सुसाध्य बिा सकते हंै, उत्तरदावयत्व को मजबूत कर सकते हंै तथा पाविसीधारक ववश्वास

मंे सुधार िा सकते हंै।



इि उद्ेदश्योंो को पूरा करिे में आगे बढ़िेे क विए, आईआरडीएआई द्वारा गवित, स्वास्थ्य बीमा संोबंोधी

आईएसी उप-सवमवत िे पारदवशणता और उत्तरदावयत्व मंे वृस्थि करिे की दृवि से, दावोंो और वशकायतोंोे क

मािकीृकत मेवटि क्स, दावा-संोबंोधी कारर्ू कटोंो और स्वास्थ्य बीमा दावा यात्रा की तत्काि दृश्यताे क विए

एक सामान्य ढाँाचे की वसफाररश करिेे क विए दो अध्ययि-दि बिाये हंै।



अध्ययि-दि 1 – दािं और वशकायतंे क मेवरि क्स और मािकीृकत कारणू कर



पहिा अध्ययि-दि दावाृकत की तुििा में प्रदत्त का अिुपात, विपटाि और अस्वीकरर् दरो,ंो आंोवशक

विपटािोंो (अस्वीकरर्ों)ो , औसत कटौवतयो,ंो िकदीरवहते क उपयोग तथा दावा प्रवतवतणि कािोंो (टीएटी)

जैसे मुख्य संोेकतकोंो को समाववि करते हुए पररर्ाम-उन्मुख दावोंो और वशकायतोंोे क मेवटि क्स को

ववकवसत करेगा। यह बीमाकताणओंोे क अंोतगणत ररपोवटंिग मंे सुसंोगवत को सुविवित करिे और साथणक तुििा

को सुसाध्य बिािेे क विए एक सामान्य वगीकरर् और मािकीृकत पररभाषाएँा भी सुझायेगा।



यह दि वतणमाि बीमाकताण और टीपीएू कटोंो को सुव्यवस्थित करिे सवहत, दावा अस्वीकरर्ों,ो विराकरर्ों,ो

कटौवतयोंो और आंोवशक विपटािोंोे क विए एक सामान्य रािि ीयू कट ढाँाचा भी प्रस्ताववत करेगा। उक्त ढाँाचा

यह सुविवित करिे की अपेक्षा करेगा वक प्रत्येक अस्वीकरर् या कटौती एक वववशि कारर् और प्रभाववत

तदिुरूपी रावशे क द्वारा समवथणत हो, इसेक द्वारा दावा विर्णयोंो में पारदवशणता में वृस्थि की जाए।



अध्ययि-दि 2 – स्वास्थ्य बीमा दािा यात्रा की तत्काि दृश्यता



दूसरा अध्ययि-दि पाविसीधारकोंो और अन्य वहतधारकोंो को भुगतािे क पूवण-प्रावधकरर् से िेकर अंोवतम

विपटाि या भुगताि तक, मािकीृकत स्वास्थ्य बीमा दावा यात्रा की तत्काि दृश्यता उपिब्ध करािेे क

विए एक व्यविा की वसफाररश करेगा।



                                                        1

यह दि वतणमाि संोदेश प्रवियाओंो की जाँाच करेगा तथा न्यूितम हस्तक्षेपे क साथ, समय-वचवित अवभिेखोंो

के द्वारा मुख्य दावा घटिाओंो और पडावोंो (माइिस्टोन्स) को ग्रहर् करिेे क विए एक व्यविा की

वसफाररश करेगा। यह पाविसीधारकोंो को अवगत रखिेे क विए संोचार की उपयुक्त पिवतयोंोे क साथ

ही, दावे की स्थिवत, िंोवबत अपेक्षाओ,ंो अपेवक्षत कारण वाई और अगिी कारण वाईे क विए वजम्मेदार पक्षकार

सवहत, प्रत्येक स्तर पर उपिब्ध कराई जािेवािी सूचिा को भी विवित करेगा।



यह दि इसेक अिावा चयवित बीमाकताणओं,ो टीपीएओंो और अस्पतािोंो को संोबि करते हुए एक मागणदशी

व्यविा सवहत, एक कायाणन्वयि ढाँाचे की भी वसफाररश करेगा, वजसका अिुसरर् एक चरर्बि रूप मंे

समूचे उद्योगे क द्वारा वकया जाएगा।



संरचिा



उक्त अध्ययि-दिोंोे क अंोतगणत समस्याओंो की जाँाच करिे और व्यावहाररक वसफाररशंे ववकवसत करिे

के विए वववियामक, उद्योग और अंोतररािि ीय ववशेषज्ञता को एकसाथ िेते हुए साधारर् और स्वास्थ्य बीमा

कंो पवियो,ंो अन्य पक्ष प्रबंोधकोंो (टीपीएएस), भारतीय बीमा सूचिा ब्यूरो (आईआईबी), एवशयाई ववकास बैंक

और ववश्व बंैक से विये गये प्रवतविवध होगंोे ।



दोिोंो अध्ययि-दिोंो की अध्यक्षता डॉ. अय्याज तंोबोिी, कायणकारी विदेशक, आईआरडीएआई करंेगे,

वजिका संोयोजि स्वास्थ्य ववभाग, आईआरडीएआईे क अवधकाररयोंोे क द्वारा वकया जाएगा तथा समन्वयि

श्री मिोजु कमार, मुख्य महाप्रबंोधक (स्वास्थ्य बीमा), आईआरडीएआई करंेगे।



दोिोंो अध्ययि-दि अपिे विष्कषण, वसफाररशंे और प्रस्ताववत कायाणन्वयि व्यविाँएा , जैसी िागू हो,ंो विवित

करते हुए अपिी ररपोटें आईआरडीएआई को 26 वदसंोबर, 2026 तक प्रस्तुत करंेगे।



As health insurance coverage expands, transparency in claim decisions, timely claim

updates and consistent reporting of claims and grievance outcomes are increasingly

important for policyholders. Standardised metrics and real-time visibility of the claims

journey can facilitate performance assessment, strengthen accountability and improve

policyholder confidence.



To advance these objectives, The IAC Sub-Committee on Health Insurance,

constituted by IRDAI, has formed two study groups to recommend standardised claims

and grievance metrics, a common framework for claim-related reason codes and real-

time visibility of the health insurance claims journey, with a view to enhancing

transparency and accountability.



Study Group 1 — Claims and grievance metrics and standardised reason codes



The first study group will develop outcome-oriented claims and grievance metrics

covering key indicators such as Paid-to-Claimed Ratio, settlement and rejection rates,

partial settlements (disallowances), average deductions, cashless utilisation and

claims turnaround times. It will also suggest a common taxonomy and standardised



                                                        2

definitions to ensure consistency in reporting and facilitate meaningful comparison

across insurers.



The group will also propose a common national code framework for claim rejections,

repudiations, deductions and partial settlements, including mapping of existing insurer

and TPA codes. The framework will seek to ensure that every rejection or deduction is

supported by a specified reason and the corresponding amount affected, thereby

enhancing transparency in claim decisions.



Study Group 2 — Real-time visibility of the health insurance claims journey



The second study group will recommend a mechanism to provide policyholders and

other stakeholders with real-time visibility of the standardised health insurance claims

journey, from pre-authorisation to final settlement or payment.



The group will examine existing communication processes and recommend a

mechanism for capturing key claim events and milestones through time-stamped

records, with minimal intervention. It will also define the information to be made

available at each stage, including claim status, pending requirements, action required

and the party responsible for the next action, along with appropriate modes of

communication to keep policyholders informed.



The group will further recommend an implementation framework, including a pilot

involving selected insurers, TPAs and hospitals, followed by phased adoption across

the industry.



Composition



The study groups comprise representatives from general and health insurance

companies, third-party administrators (TPAs), the Insurance Information Bureau of

India (IIB), the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank, bringing together

regulatory, industry and international expertise to examine the issues and develop

practical recommendations.



Both study groups will be chaired by Dr. Ayyaj Tamboli, Executive Director, IRDAI,

convened by designated officers of the Health Department, IRDAI, and coordinated by

Shri Manoj Kumar, Chief General Manager (Health Insurance), IRDAI.



Both groups will submit their reports to IRDAI by 26th December, 2026, setting out their

findings, recommendations and proposed implementation arrangements, as

applicable.
```

```text
===== [attachment 1] परामर्श-पत्र “बीमा वितरण के अर्थशास्त्र का पुनरीक्षण” के संबंध में प्राप्त प्रतिक्रियाओं की जाँच करने के लिएConstitution of an Expert Committee to examine the responses received on the consultation paper “Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribut.pdf =====
संदर्भ : आईआरडीएआई/आईएनटी/ओआरडी/एमआईएससी/157/11/2016



Ref: IRDAI/INT/ORD/MISC/157/11/2026  दिनं ाक / Date: 23.11.2026



आदेश / ORDER



विषय : परामर्श-पत्र “बीमा वितरणे क अर्थशास्त्र का पुनरीक्षण”े क संबंध मंे प्राप्त प्रतिक्रियाओं

की जँ ाच करनेे क लिए एक विशेषज्ञ समिति का गठन

Re: Constitution of an Expert Committee to examine the responses received

on the consultation paper “Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution”



1. भारतीय बीमा विनियामक और विकास प्राधिकरण (“प्राधिकरण”) ने 23 सितंबर 2026 को “बीमा

       वितरणे क अर्थशास्त्र का पुनरीक्षण” शीर्षक एक सार्वजनिक परामर्श-पत्र जारी किया है। इस

       परामर्श-पत्र मंे बीमा वितरण की संरचना, प्रबंधने क व्यय और कमीशन, बाजार व्यवहार,

       पारदर्शिता और डिजिटल अवसंरचनाे क उपयोग को शामिल करते हुए सुधार प्रस्तावित किये गये

       हैं। 32 प्रश्नंोे क द्वारा इन प्रस्तावं ोे क संबंध मंे हितधारकं ोे क विचार अपेक्षित किये गये हैं।



2. उक्त सार्वजनिक परामर्शे क लिए भारी प्रतिक्रिया मिली है। 31 अक्तूबर 2026 की बढ़ाई गई

       अंतिम तारीख तक उक्त 32 प्रश्नंोे क लिए 13,000 से भी अधिक व्यक्तियं ो से लगभग 2.18 लाख

       उत्तर प्राप्त हुए हैं। ये उत्तर बीमा ईकोसिस्टमे क विस्तार और उस गंभीरता को प्रतिबं िबित करते

       हंै जिसेक साथ सहभागी उक्त प्रस्तावं ोे क साथ सक्रिय रहे हैं।



3. उक्त सुधारं ोे क उद्ेदश्य बीमा की लागत को कम करना, पालिसीधारक परिणामं ो में सुधार लाना,

       कवरेज को विस्तृत करना, तथा एक धारणीय और व्यावसायिक वितरण ईकोसिस्टम को समर्थन

       देना हैं। बीमा को पहँुचयोग्य, वहनीय और उचित रूप से विक्रययोग्य होना चाहिए, तथा वितरण

       के लिए गुणवत्तापूर्ण सलाह, सेवा और दीर्घकालिक ग्राहक संबंधं ो को पुरस्ृकत करना चाहिए। ये

       लक्ष्य `सबेक लिए बीमा’ की राष्टर्ीय परिदृष्टिे क अनुरूप पालिसीधारकं ोे क हितं ो का संरक्षण करने

       और इस क्षेत्र की सुव्यवस्थित वृद्धि का संवर्धन करनेे क आईआरडीएआईे क अधिदेशे के कन्द्र में

       हैं।



4. आईआरडीएआई अपने वितरण सुधारं ोे क अभिकल्पन और कार्यान्वयन को सुदृढ़ करने हेतु आगे

       और परामर्श देनेे क लिए इसेक द्वारा स्वतंत्र अर्थशास्त्रियं ो और बीमा व्यवसायियं ो की एक विशेषज्ञ

       समिति गठित करता है। इस समिति की भूमिका यथासंभव उक्त ढँ ाचे को सुदृढ़, स्पष्ट और प्रभावी

       बनाने में सहायता करने की है। समूचे क्षेत्र मंे और उसेक आगे उपलब्ध विशेषज्ञता की गहनता से

       लाभ उठाते हुए यह इस बात पर परामर्श देगी कि उक्त प्रस्तावं ो कोै कसे आगे संवर्धित और

       परिष्ृकत किया जाएगा, ताकि वे सुचारु रूप से कार्यान्वित किये जाँएगे और उनेक अपेक्षित लाभं ो

       का वितरण किया जाएगा। इसका कार्य बीमा उद्योगे क सभी खंडं ोे क साथ आईआरडीएआईे क

       निरंतर जुड़ाव का संपूरक होगा।



5. उक्त समितिे क विचारार्थ विषय (टीओआर) निम्नानुसार प्रस्तावित हैं :

         (i) प्रस्तावित सुधारं ो की जँ ाच करना और अतिरिक्त उपायं ो और परिष्करण ,ंो यदि कोई हं ,ो

                  की सिफारिश करना जिन्हंे पालिसीधारक ,ंो बीमाकर्ताओं और वितरकं ोे क हितं ोे क बीच

                  एक उचित और धारणीय संतुलन प्राप्त करनेे क लिए शामिल किया जा सकता है।

         (ii) यह आकलन करना कि क्या प्रस्तावित उपाय बीमा क्षेत्र में रोजगार पर तथा वैयक्तिक

                  एजेंटं ो और अन्य वितरण कर्मियं ो की आय पर प्रतिूकल प्रभाव की संभाव्यता को वहन

                  करते हंै और यदि हँ ा, तो ऐसे प्रभाव को कम करनेे क लिए सुधारं ोे क प्रस्तावित उपायं ो

                  में उपयुक्त परिष्करण सुझाना।

         (iii) अपेक्षाृकत छोटे वितरकं ो और छोटे बीमाकर्ताओंे क सरोकारं ो का समाधान करनेे क

                  लिए चरणबद्धीकरण, सुगम मार्ग और समर्थक उपायं ो सहित, उपयुक्त संक्रमण पथ

                  सुझाना।

         (iv) अपेक्षाृकत छोटे प्रीमियम वाली पालिसियं ोे क लिए लागू कमीशन सीमाओं का निर्धारण

                  करनेे क लिए सिद्धंातं ,ो मानदंडं ो और एक समीक्षा व्यवस्था सहित, उपयुक्त रूपरेखा

                  की सिफारिश करना।

         (v) यह जँ ाच करना कि क्या अपेक्षाृकत छोटे शहर ,ंो ग्रामीण क्षेत्रंो और अल्पसेवाप्राप्त खंडं ो

                  में बीमा कवरेज का विस्तार करनेे क लिए अतिरिक्त उपाय अपेक्षित हंै, तथा ऐसे उपायं ो

                  की सिफारिश करना।

         (vi) यह जँ ाच करना कि क्या संवर्धित पारदर्शिता तथा शुल्क-आधारित सेवाओं की दिशा मंे

                  एक क्रमिक परिवर्तने क द्वारा बडे़ वाणिज्यिक जोखिम खंड की बेहतर सेवा की जाएगी,

                  तथा यदि उपयुक्त पाया जाता है तो ऐसे परिवर्तने क लिए पद्धति और गति की सिफारिश

                  करना।

         (vii) उपर्ुयक्ते क लिए प्रासंगिक या संबंधित कोई अन्य विषय, जो समिति संगत समझती है

                  अथवा जैसा कि सक्षम प्राधिकारीे क द्वारा उसेक पास संदर्भित किया जा सकता है।

7. उक्त समिति टीओआर की प्रत्येक मद पर विशिष्ट सिफारिशं ो सहित, अपनी रिपोर्ट 31 दिसंबर

       2026 तक प्रस्तुत कर सकती है।



8. उक्त समिति भौतिक या आभासी पद्धति में बैठकं ोे क आयोजन सहित, जैसा कि वह उपयुक्त

       समझती है, अपने कार्ये क संचालने क लिए अपनी स्वयं की प्रक्रिया अभिकल्पित कर सकती है;

       सार्वजनिक परामर्श पर आईआरडीएआई से डेटा, विश्लेषण और सूचना मँगा सकती है; तथा

       अंतिम रिपोर्ट से पहले विशिष्ट टीओआर मदं ो पर अंतरिम टिप्पणियँ ा, यदि कोई ह ,ंो प्रस्तुत कर

       कराया जाएगा। उक्त कार्यकारी निदेशक, संयोजके क रूप में, बैठकं ो और समिति की रिपोर्ट की

       तैयारी का समन्वय करंेगे।



1. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (“the Authority”)

     issued a public consultation paper titled “Recalibrating Economics of Insurance

     Distribution” on 23 September 2026. The paper proposed reforms covering the

     structure of insurance distribution, expenses of management and commission,

     market conduct, transparency and the use of digital infrastructure. Stakeholders’

     views on these proposals were sought through 32 questions.



2. The public consultation received an overwhelming response. By the extended last

     date of 31 October 2026, about 2.18 lakh answers to the 32 questions were

     received from over 13,000 persons. The responses reflect the breadth of the

     insurance ecosystem and the seriousness with which participants have engaged

     with the proposals.



                        सर्वे संख्या 115/1, फाइनेशियल डिस्ट्रि क्ट, नानकरामगुडा, हैदराबाद 500 032

                   Survey No. 115/1, Financial District, Nanakramguda, Hyderabad 500 032



                                   दूरभाष / Phone: 040-20204000; www.irdai.gov.in



                                                                                            पृष्ठ / Page 3 / 5

3. The reforms' objectives remain to lower the cost of insurance, improve

     policyholder outcomes, widen coverage, and support a sustainable and

     professional distribution ecosystem. Insurance should be accessible, affordable

     and fairly sold, and distribution should reward quality advice, service and long-

     term customer relationships. These goals are central to IRDAI's mandate of

     protecting policyholders' interests and promoting the orderly growth of the sector,

     in line with the national vision of insurance for all.



4. IRDAI hereby constitutes an Expert Committee of independent economists and

     insurance professionals to advice further on strengthening the design and

     implementation of its distribution reforms. The Committee's role is to help make

     the framework as robust, clear and effective as possible. Drawing on the depth of

     expertise available across the sector and beyond, it will advise on how the

     proposals can be further enhanced and refined, so that they are implemented

     smoothly and deliver their intended benefits. Its work will complement IRDAI’s

     ongoing engagement with all segments of the insurance industry.



5. The Terms of Reference (ToR) of the Committee are proposed as under:



        (i) To examine the proposed reforms and recommend additional measures

                  or refinements, if any, that may be incorporated to achieve a fair and

                  sustainable balance between the interests of policyholders, insurers and

                  distributors.



        (ii) To assess whether the proposed measures carry the potential of adverse

                  impact on employment in the insurance sector and on the income of

                  individual agents and other distribution persons and, if so, to suggest

                  suitable refinements in the proposed reform measures to mitigate such

                  impact.



        (iii) To suggest appropriate transition pathways, including phasing, glide

                  paths and supportive measures, to address the concerns of smaller

                  distributors and smaller insurers.



        (iv) To recommend an appropriate framework, including principles,

                  parameters and a review mechanism, for determining the commission

                  limits applicable to smaller premium policies.



        (v) To examine whether additional measures are required to expand

                 insurance coverage in smaller towns, rural areas and underserved

                 segments, and to recommend such measures.



        (vi) To examine whether the large commercial risk segment would be better

                 served by enhanced transparency and a gradual shift towards fee-based

                 services, and to recommend the manner and pace of such transition, if

                 found appropriate.



        (vii) Any other matter incidental or related to the above, as the Committee

                   may consider relevant, or as may be referred to it by the Competent

                   Authority.

7. The Committee may submit its report, along with specific recommendations on

each item of the ToR, by 31 December 2026.



8. The Committee may devise its own procedure for the conduct of its business,

including meetings in physical or virtual mode, as it considers appropriate; call for data,

analysis and information from IRDAI on the public consultation; and submit interim

observations, if any, on specific ToR items prior to the final report.



9. Secretariat support, including data and analytical assistance, shall be provided

by IRDAI. The Executive Director, as Convener, shall coordinate the meetings and the

preparation of the Committee’s report.
```

```text
===== [attachment 1] आईआरडीएआई अपने वितरण सुधारों के अभिकल्पन और कार्यान्वयन को मजबूत करने  के लिए विशेषज्ञ समिति का गठन करता है _ IRDAI constitutes Expert Committee to strengthen the design and implementation of its distribution reforms.pdf =====
                          भारतीय बीमा विनियामक और विकास प्राधिकरण

                    Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India



                                     प्रेस प्रकाशनी I 23 नवंबर 2026

                              Press Release | 23rd November 2026



   आईआरडीएआई अपने वितरण सुधारं ोे क अभिकल्पन और कार्यान्वयन को मजबूत करने

                               के लिए विशेषज्ञ समिति का गठन करता है



         IRDAI constitutes Expert Committee to strengthen the design and

                          implementation of its distribution reforms



23 सितंबर 2026 को आईआरडीएआई ने `बीमा वितरणे क अर्थशास्त्र का पुनरीक्षण’ शीर्षक एक

सार्वजनिक परामर्श-पत्र जारी किया है। यह परामर्श-पत्र बीमा वितरण की संरचना, व्ययं ,ो कमीशन ,ंो

बाजार व्यवहार, पारदर्शिता और डिजिटल अवसंरचनाे क उपयोग को समाविष्ट करते हुए एक व्यापक

ढँ ाचा निर्धारित करता है।



उक्त सार्वजनिक परामर्श-पत्रे क लिए भारी प्रतिक्रिया मिली है। 31 अक्तूबर 2026 की बढ़ाई गई समय-

सीमा तक 32 प्रश्नंोे क लिए 13,000 से अधिक व्यक्तियं ो से लगभग 2.18 लाख प्रतिक्रियाँए मिली हैं। ये

प्रतिक्रियाँए बीमा ईकोसिस्टमे क विस्तार और उस गंभीरता को प्रतिबं िबित करती हैं जिसेक साथ

सहभागियं ो ने उक्त प्रस्तावं ोे क साथ सक्रिय रहे हंै।



उक्त सुधारं ोे क उद्ेदश्य हंै, बीमा की लागत को कम करना, पालिसीधारक परिणामं ो में सुधार लाना,

कवरेज को व्यापक बनाना, तथा एक धारणीय और व्यावसायिक वितरण ईकोसिस्टम का समर्थन करना।

बीमा पहँुचयोग्य, वहनीय और उचित रूप से विक्रययोग्य होना चाहिए, तथा वितरणे क लिए गुणवत्तापूर्ण

परामर्श, सेवा और दीर्घकालिक ग्राहक संबंधं ो को पुरस्ृकत करना चाहिए। ये लक्ष्य `सबेक लिए बीमा’ की

राष्टर्ीय परिदृष्टिे क अनुरूप पालिसीधारकं ोे क हितं ो का संरक्षण करने और इस क्षेत्र की सुव्यवस्थित वृद्धि

का संवर्धन करनेे क आईआरडीएआईे क अधिदेश (मैंडेट)े के कन्द्र में हैं।



आईआरडीएआई ने आज अपने वितरण सुधारं ोे क अभिकल्पन और कार्यान्वयन को मजबूत करने हेतु

उपायं ोे क संबंध मंे सुझाव देनेे क लिए स्वतंत्र अर्थशास्त्रियं ो और बीमा व्यवसायियं ो की एक विशेषज्ञ

समिति का गठन किया है। श्री अजय सेठ, अध्यक्ष, आईआरडीएआई ने कहा, “इस समिति की भूमिका

उक्त ढँ ाचे को यथासंभव सुदृढ़, स्पष्ट और प्रभावी बनाने की है। इसका कार्य आईआरडीएआई की उस

निरंतर संलिप्तता का पूरक बनना है जिसका अनुरक्षण वह उद्योगे क सभी खंडं ो में करता है।” इस समूचे

क्षेत्र में और उसेक आगे उपलब्ध विशेषज्ञता की गहनता का लाभ उठाते हुए, यह प्रत्याशित है कि उक्त

समिति इस विषय में परामर्श देगी कि उक्त प्रस्तावं ो का आगेै कसे परिष्करण किया जा सकता है ताकि

उन्हंे सुचारु रूप से कार्यान्वित किया जा सेक और उनेक उद्दिष्ट लाभं ो को वितरित किया जा सेक।



इस समिति की अध्यक्षता डा. इन्दु भूषण, आईएएस (सेवानिवृत्त), भूतपूर्व सीईओ, आयुष्मान भारत मिशन

द्वारा की जाएगी। इसेक सदस्य हंै, श्री सुरेश गोयल, महानिदेशक, राष्टर्ीय अनुप्रयुक्त आर्थिक अनुसंधान

परिषद (एनसीएईआर); श्री ए.वी. गिरिजाु कमार, भूतपूर्व सीएमडी, दी ओरियन्टल इंश्योरंेसं कपनी लि.;

श्री प्रवीण वशिष्ठ, भूतपूर्व सीईओ और अध्यक्ष, हाउडेन इंश्योरेंस ब्रोकर्स इंडिया; तथा श्री महेशु कमार

शर्मा, भूतपूर्व एमडी और सीईओ, एसबीआई लाइफ इंश्योरेंस। डा. अय्याज तंबोली, आईएएस, कार्यकारी

निदेशक, आईआरडीएआई संयोजक ह गंोे । समिति को अपनी रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करनेे क लिए 31 दिसंबर

2026 तक समय दिया गया है।

On 23 September 2026, IRDAI issued a public consultation paper titled “Recalibrating

Economics of Insurance Distribution”. The paper sets out a comprehensive framework

of reforms covering the structure of insurance distribution, expenses, commissions,

market conduct, transparency and the use of digital infrastructure.



The public consultation received an overwhelming response. By the extended

deadline of 31 October 2026, about 2.18 lakh responses to the 32 questions had been

received from over 13,000 persons. These responses reflect the breadth of the

insurance ecosystem and the seriousness with which participants have engaged with

the proposals.



The objectives of the reforms remain to lower the cost of insurance, improve

policyholder outcomes, widen coverage, and support a sustainable and professional

distribution ecosystem. Insurance should be accessible, affordable and fairly sold, and

distribution should reward quality advice, service and long-term customer

relationships. These goals are central to IRDAI's mandate of protecting policyholders'

interests and promoting the orderly growth of the sector, in line with the national vision

of insurance for all.



IRDAI, today, constituted an Expert Committee of independent economists and

insurance professionals to suggest on measures to strengthen the design and

implementation of its distribution reforms. Mr. Ajay Seth, Chairman, IRDAI, said, “The

Committee's role is to help make the framework as robust, clear and effective as

possible. Its work will complement the ongoing engagement IRDAI maintains with all

segments of the industry.” Drawing on the depth of expertise available across the

sector and beyond, the Committee is expected to advise on how the proposals can be

further refined so that they are implemented smoothly and deliver their intended

benefits.



The Committee will be chaired by Dr. Indu Bhushan, IAS (Retd.), former CEO,

Ayushman Bharat Mission. Its members are Shri Suresh Goyal, Director General,

National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER); Shri A.V. Girija Kumar,

former CMD, The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.; Shri Praveen Vashishta, former CEO

and Chairman, Howden Insurance Brokers India; and Shri Mahesh Kumar Sharma,

former MD & CEO, SBI Life Insurance. Dr. Ayyaj Tamboli, IAS, Executive Director,

IRDAI, will be the Convenor. The Committee has been given time until 31 December

2026 to submit its report.
```

```text
Ref: IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



 Order in the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd arising out

of Show Cause Notice (“SCN”) reference No. IRDA / ENF / 2022-23 / 706 / SCN /



                               LR / 081 dated 04th December, 2024



1. Based on the



       1.1. Show Cause Notice (“SCN”) reference No. IRDA / ENF / 2022-23 / 706 /

                SCN / LR / 081 dated 04th December, 2024 issued to Star Health and

                Allied Insurance Co. Ltd (“Insurer” or “Company”) in connection with the

                inspection conducted by the Authority from 31st January to 11th February,

                2022.



       1.2. Submissions made by the insurer vide email dated 10 January 2025 in

                response to the aforesaid SCN.



       1.3. Submissions made by the insurer during the personal hearing held on 18th

                June, 2025 at 12.00 PM, by a panel of Two Whole Time Members of the

                Authority - Shri Deepak Sood (Member-Non-Life) and Shri P.K. Arora

                (Member- Actuary).



       1.4. Further submissions made by the insurer vide email dated 11th July 2025.



2. Background



       2.1. The Authority had conducted a General inspection of the insurer from 31st

                January to 11th February 2022. The inspection report, inter alia, revealed

                certain violations of Regulations and Guidelines issued thereunder.



       2.2. A copy of the inspection report was forwarded to the insurer on 18th April

                2022 seeking their response. The insurer provided their response vide

                letter dated 25th May 2022.



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 1 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



       2.3. On examining the submissions made by the insurer, Show Cause Notice

                (SCN) was issued on 04th December, 2024. The insurer replied to the SCN

                vide email dated 10th January 2025.



       2.4. As requested by the insurer, personal hearing was granted to the insurer

                on 18th June, 2025 by the panel of Two Whole Time Members of the

                Authority - Shri Deepak Sood (Member-Non-Life) and Shri P.K. Arora

       2.5. On behalf of the insurer, Shri Anand Roy, MD & CEO, Shri Amitabh Jain,

                (Manager) attended the hearing.



       2.6. Due to the re-constitution of the panel of WTMs, the insurer was offered

                an opportunity of fresh hearing with the re-constituted panel of Member

                (Non-Life) and Member (F&I) vide email dated 10th March, 2026 to which

                the insurer responded that all relevant facts and justifications were

       2.7. The submissions made by the insurer vide its letter dated 25th May 2022,

                submission made after SCN vide email dated 10th January 2025 and

                submission made during the personal hearing on 18th June 2025 and

                those made vide email dated 11th July 2025 have been carefully

                considered by the Authority and are summarized below:



3. Charge 1 (Observation No. - 23)



       3.1. Violation of Regulation 13(iii) of IRDAI (Health Insurance) Regulations,

                2016.



       3.2. Inspection Observation

                While examining the details of Advance Premium and the relevant

                documents, it was noticed that the insurer has been collecting advance



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 2 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



                premium for renewal of some policies more than 90 days in advance which

                is a violation of proviso to Regulation 13(iii) of the IRDAI (Health

                Insurance) Regulations, 2016.



3.3. Summary of Insurer’s Submissions



3.3.1.  The insurer, in its response, accepted that the lapse has occurred

        due to a technical issue and the system has since been modified to

        ensure that such lapse does not occur in the future.



3.3.2.  It has been submitted that the earlier validation system in the

        insurer’s system was applied at the policy conversion stage wherein

        the validation was for the date of approval of policy rather than the

        date of collection of premium. This gap has now been rectified.



3.3.3.  Insurer further submitted that IRDAI Master circular on Protection of

        Policyholders Interest, 2024 has done away with the requirement of

        90 days’ limit on advance premium for renewal of health policy.



3.3.4.  During the personal hearing, the insurer submitted that, in February

        2023, two steps validation mechanism was introduced to avoid

        collection of premium beyond 90 days in advance.



3.3.5.  The Panel, during the Personal Hearing, instructed the insurer to

        submit an undertaking covering the cases (along with the amount of

        premium) where was received more than 90 days in advance before

        the repeal of this requirement. The insurer has submitted the

        undertaking, as required.



3.4. Issues and Concerns on Charge 1



3.4.1.  The Insurer has accepted that lapses did occur, as observed by the

        Inspection team, which led to the violation of Proviso to Regulation

        13(iii) of the IRDAI (Health Insurance) Regulations, 2016.



3.4.2.  The Insurer has further submitted during the personal hearing that

        the required modifications were brought in to ensure compliance to

        the stated regulation.



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 3 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



3.5. Decision on Charge 1



         Given that the additional validation and required modification were

         brought to ensure compliance with the regulations, the insurer is

         hereby cautioned for the lapse and advised to ensure compliance

         with extant regulations and circulars as applicable.



4. Charge 3 (Observation No.- 18)



4.1. Violation of Regulation 27(v) of the IRDAI (Health Insurance)

        Regulations, 2016.



4.2. Inspection Observation



4.2.1.  The Insurer was asked to furnish select documents/records with

        regard to the repudiation of cases selected on sample basis. Upon

        perusal of the documents provided, it was observed that the insured

        persons had undergone treatment in hospitals as per the advice of

        the medical experts and the treating doctors. However, the Insurer

        has repudiated the claims on the ground that the condition of the

        patient did not require hospitalization and that he/she should have

        been treated at home.



4.2.2.  The Insurer, in its communication to the Insured, quoted guidelines

        from All India Institute of medical Sciences, New Delhi and Ministry

        of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India regarding the

        treatment of Covid 19 patients and stated that the patient required

        only self-isolation by home quarantine.



4.3. Summary of Insurer’s submissions



4.3.1. The Insurer drew attention to the fact that the Covid 19 pandemic

          was an unprecedented situation for the healthcare industry which led



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 4 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



        to reliance on guidance and protocols issued by the Institutions like

        WHO, ICMR, AIIMS etc.



4.3.2.  The guidelines and protocols issued by the State Health Department

        during the Covid 19 pandemic were framed under the Disaster

        Management Act and the Clinical Establishment Act and were legally

        binding on the healthcare sector.



4.3.3. The Insurer also emphasized that many hospitals took advantage of

          the prevailing situation and overcharged under various heads.



4.3.4.  Further, the Insurer has also referred in its email to the authority

        dated 24 July 2021 where it informed that all the Covid Claims are

        being repudiated after review by its In-house Claims Appellate

        Committee.



4.4. Concerns with respect to Charge 3



4.4.1.  The Insurer has invoked quoted guidelines from All India Institute of

        medical Sciences, New Delhi and Ministry of Health and Family

        Welfare, Government of India to deny claims.



4.4.2.  The Insurer, in its response, submitted the policy document of its

        flagship product, Family Health Optima Policy to the Authority. The

        policy document clearly mentions that “In cases where the insured

        contract any disease or suffer from any illness and if such disease

        or injury shall require the insured, upon the advice of a duly Qualified

        Physician / Medical Specialist / Medical Practitioner or of duly

        Qualified Surgeon to incur Hospitalization expenses during the

        period stated in the schedule for medical/surgical treatment at any

        Nursing Home / Hospital in India as an in-patient, it will indemnify the

        Insured the amount of such expenses.



4.4.3.  The coverage provided under the policy stipulates that the expenses

        must be incurred upon advice of a Qualified Physician / Medical

        Specialist / Medical Practitioner or of duly Qualified Surgeon.



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 5 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



4.4.4.  While hospitals are expected to follow treatment guidelines and

        protocols issued by various bodies, Covid 19 was an exceptional

        period and ailment. Despite various protocols issued, medical

        professionals may have preferred to take precautions and act with

        extra caution in many cases. In marginal cases, medical

        professionals, in the interest of taking a prudent approach would

        have suggested hospitalization. Being a pandemic, such

        hospitalization may also have been preferred for isolating the patient

        to safe guard family members and others. The insurer ought to have

        considered this in evaluating the hospitalization.



4.4.5.  Therefore, the claims processed by the Insurer are, in a manner,

        inconsistent with its own policy terms and conditions and therefore it

        is a violation of IRDAI Circulars on Covid Claim settlements and

        Regulation 27 (v) of IRDAI (Health Insurance) Regulations, 2016

        which states “Every Insurance Claim shall be disposed of in

        accordance to the Terms and Conditions of the policy contract”.



4.4.6.  Moreover, the panel, in the personal hearing, enquired whether the

        insurer has communicated to the policyholder in each sample case

        why hospitalization is not required. The insurer was also instructed

        to give details of the actions initiated against the hospitals involved

        in the malpractice of overcharging. While the Insurer has submitted

        documents related to actions taken against the hospitals on sample

        basis, it has failed to provide documents proving that the

        communication was sent to the policyholder leading to the

        conclusion that no such communication was sent to the policyholder.

        The insurer is unable to justify its decision of stating “hospitalization

        not required”.



4.4.7.  The subjective nature of what constitutes "necessary" hospitalization

        is further exaggerated by the insurer in a unique situation like the

        Covid pandemic. In cases where this provision is invoked there must

        be more than due justification which cannot be easily established in

        a situation like Covid pandemic.



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 6 of 21

       4.5. Decision on Charge 3



4.5.1.  In view of the above, in exercise of the powers vested under

4.5.2.  The Insurer is further advised to ensure that the all the policies

5. Charge 2 (Observation No.- 17) & Charge 4&5 (Observation No. - 19 and 20)



5.1. Violation of-



     a) Regulation 27(v) of the IRDAI (Health Insurance) Regulations, 2016;

     b) Regulation 33 (d) (ii) and (iv) of IRDA (Health Insurance) Regulations,



            2016;

     c) Regulation 21 (3) (c) (i) (c) of IRDAI (TPA – Health Services)



            Regulation, 2016;

     d) Clause 6 of Guidelines of Corporate Governance Dated 18.05.16



            issued vide Circular IRDA / F&A / GDL / CG / 100 / 05 / 2016.



5.2. Inspection Observation (No. 17)



5.2.1.  Insurer is making deductions from the claims of the policyholders,

        which are out of purview of the terms & conditions of the policies

        issued. In the document inspected namely “Bill Assessment Sheet”

        the reason for deductions was mentioned as “Member Payment vis

        a vis terms & conditions of the policy issued”.



5.2.2.  The Insurer was advised to furnish select documents/records with

        regard to settlement of cases selected on sample basis by the

        Inspection team. The Insurer, in its response, furnished “Bill



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 7 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



        Assessment Sheet – Member payment” which furnished details of

        items which were partially or completely disallowed at the time of

        claim settlement.



5.2.3.  Upon perusal of the submitted document, it was found that none of

        the terms and conditions of the policy issued empowered the insurer

        to make deductions on these grounds.



5.2.4.  The insurer was also advised to furnish explanation / clarification on

        the disallowance of items of expenses by giving reference to the

        particular terms & conditions of the policy issued, in terms of which

        the said deductions were made. However, the insurer did not furnish

        any such information.



5.3. Inspection Observation (No. 19 and 20)



5.3.1.  The Inspection team requested the Insurer to furnish the copy of

        communication, if any sent to the claimant, among the sample cases,

        giving details of the item wise deductions made from the claim filed

        and also the detailed reasons for the said deductions according to

        the terms and conditions of the policy issued.



5.3.2.  The Insurer submitted a document namely “Bill Assessment Sheet –

        Member Payment and communication” informing the claimant about

        the amount for which the claim has been finally settled. However, the

        Insurer could not demonstrate that the communication part of the

        document was actually sent from its system to the claimants.



5.3.3.  It was noted on the perusal of copy of communications furnished by

        the Insurer that it has not informed the policyholder of the particular

        terms and conditions of the policy under which the claim has been

        repudiated.



5.4. Summary of Insurer’s Submissions

     5.4.1. The insurer submitted that as there was no uniformity in the charges

                levied by the hospitals for treatment of patients with Covid-19, some



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 8 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



        of the hospitals resorted to unreasonable billing exploiting the

        situation.



5.4.2.  While settling claims, the insurer applied “reasonable and customary

        charges” wherever hospitals had resorted to excessive billing. In

        determining reasonable and customary charges for Covid 19

        treatment, they were guided by the rates prescribed by various

        Governments and other bodies.



5.4.3.  All the deductions were made in accordance with the “reasonable

        and customary” and “medical necessary” definitions which were the

        basic coverage definition under the policy terms duly approved by

        the Authority.



5.4.4.  In the personal hearing, the insurer was advised to submit the

5.4.5.  Insurer submitted that in the 15 cases under consideration, no

        or any redressal forum. This would imply that these customers were

        not aggrieved and were satisfied with the insurer’s settlement.



5.4.6. The Panel, in the personal hearing, advised the insurer to submit the

          following details duly certified by CCO and CEO:



        5.4.6.1. Data showing the total deductions made from the claim paid

                    and the amount of deduction made on account of

                    “Reasonable and Customary” charges for last five years

                    ending with FY 2024-25;



        5.4.6.2. Provide percentage of reasonable and customary deduction

                    made to the total claim amount for last five years ending with

                    FY 2024-25.



5.4.7. The data, as advised in the personal hearing, was submitted by the

          Insurer.



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 9 of 21

5.4.8.  The Insurer, in its response, stated that in respect of payment of

        reimbursement claims, the communication to the claimant is

        automatically sent consisting of a Covering Letter, Discharge

        Voucher and the Bill Assessment Sheet showing the details of the

        settlement.



5.4.9.  The insurer has accepted that during the stated period, due to

        technical error, the covering letter was not sent which contains the

        details of Grievance Redressal Mechanism and Details of the

        Ombudsman of the competent jurisdiction.



5.4.10. The insurer, in its reply to SCN dated 10 Jan 2022, accepted the

          observations made by the Authority regarding policy conditions not

          indicated in rejection letters and state to having taken the corrective

          action.



5.5. Concerns with respect to Charge 2, 4 and 5



5.5.1.  The insurer, resorted to arbitrary deductions as seen in the cases

        sampled in the inspection report. The reasons for many of these

        deductions, as submitted by the Insurer, were mentioned as “Claims

        Processed as per GIC Rates”.



5.5.2.  Using, GI Council rates to deny or reduce COVID claims without

        tagging the repudiation to applicable policy clauses is detrimental to

        the interests of the policyholders and therefore is a violation of

        IRDAI’s Covid Claim Circulars as well as regulation 27 (v) of the

        IRDAI (Health Insurance) Regulations 2016 which states that every

        Insurance Claim shall be disposed of in accordance with the Terms

        & Conditions of the policy contract and the extant Regulations

        governing the settlement of claims.



5.5.3.  In addition, Authority issued a circular vide Reference No.: IRDAI /

        HLT / REG / CIR / 054 / 03 / 2020 dated 04th March, 2020 where it

        instructed the Insurers that “The costs of admissible medical

        expenses during the course of treatment including the treatment

        during quarantine period shall be settled in accordance with the



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 10 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



        applicable terms and conditions of policy contract and the extant

        regulatory framework”.



5.5.4.  The Insurer, in its response, to the SCN vide email dated 10th

        January, 2025 submitted reasons for the deductions made in the

        cases sampled by the Inspection team. In many cases, the amount

        settled was reconsidered by the Insurer for the sample cases

        highlighted by the inspection team and an additional claim amount

        was paid. This shows that the deduction/denial in the first instance

        was not as per the terms and conditions of the policy contracts and

        the Insurer only reconsidered them when the cases were highlighted

        by the Authority, as an afterthought.



5.5.5.  From the data submitted by the insurer post-personal hearing, it has

        been noted that both percentage of Reasonable and Customary

        Charges to total deduction and Percentage of Reasonable and

        Customary Charges to Total Allowances were highest in FY 2021-

        22. The increase in such deductions strongly indicate that the clause

        was being invoked not in isolated circumstances, but as a matter of

        practice to reduce payment of claim amount to the policyholders. The

        insurer has claimed that the hospitals resorted to excessive billing

        given the vulnerability induced by COVID 19 but failed to

        substantiate the same for the cases cited by tagging the deductions

        to respective clauses or item-wise overbilling.



5.5.6.  The Insurer, in its response after the personal hearing, has furnished

        some sample cases where policyholders were provided detailed

        breakdown of claim amounts, along the specific terms and conditions

        under which repudiations or deductions were made. However, it is

        observed that the insurer has submitted sample cases which differ

        materially from the cases identified during the inspection. This

        discrepancy raises concerns regarding the accuracy, completeness

        and reliability of the information furnished by the insurer.



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 11 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



5.5.7.  The insurer has indicated that they have improved their processes

        by including a formal covering letter in all their claims communication

        along with the Bill assessment sheet in order to provide more clarity

        and transparency to their customers. The response of the insurer is

        silent on informing the policyholder of the particular terms and

        conditions of the policy contract under which the deduction or

        repudiation of the claim has been done.



5.5.8.  Regulation 33(d)(iv) of IRDAI (Health Insurance) Regulations, 2016

        mandates that where a claim is denied or repudiated, the

        communication about the denial or the repudiation shall be made

        only by the Insurer, specifically stating the reasons for the denial or

        repudiation, while necessarily referring to the corresponding policy

        conditions. The insurer shall also furnish the grievance redressal

        procedures available with the Insurance Company and with the

        Insurance Ombudsman along with the detailed addresses of the

        respective offices. The practice of not communicating decisions

        regarding claim settlements along with detailed reasons

        corresponding to the policy terms deprives the claimants of making

        an informed decision to challenge the decision of the Insurer and

        significantly harms policyholders by creating confusion- and,

        increasing financial stress. Insurers are, at all-times, expected to be

        transparent in their communication and keep policyholders informed

        and engaged throughout the claims process.



5.5.9.  By not communicating the decision to repudiate the claims to the

        policyholders and by not mentioning the specific terms and

        conditions under which repudiations were made, the Insurer has

        violated Regulation 33(d)(iv) and 33(d)(ii) of IRDAI (Health

        Insurance) Regulations, 2016 (where there is no TPA, Regulation

        21(3) to be followed) Regulation 21(3) (c) (i) (c) of IRDAI (TPA –

        Health Services) Regulation, 2016.

       5.6. Decision on Charge 2, 4 and 5 -



                In view of the above, in exercise of the powers vested under Section

                102 of the Insurance Act, 1938, the Authority hereby imposes a

                penalty of Rs. One Crore for the violation of Regulation 27(v) and

                33(d)(ii) and (iv) of IRDA (Health Insurance) Regulations, 2016;

                Regulation 21(3)(c)(i)(c) of IRDAI (TPA – Health Services) Regulation,

                2016.



6. Charge 6 (Observation No. - 21)



6.1. Violation of Regulation 20 (9) of IRDAI (TPA – Health Services)

        Regulation, 2016.



6.2. Inspection Observation



6.2.1.  Upon examination of copies of bills, invoices, discharge summaries

        and documents titled “Bill Assessment Sheet – Hospital Payment”,

        furnished by the Insurer and setting out the details of deductions

        made from the claims submitted, it was observed, in respect of

        sample cases examined, that the Insurer had made deductions

        towards discounts purportedly agreed to be offered by the Network

        Service Providers, without verifying whether such discounts had

        actually been granted by the respective Network Service Providers

        by way of upfront deductions in the bills raised by them on the

        claimants.



6.2.2.  The insurer was informed that since the discount, although stated to

        be agreed between the insurer and the respective network service

        provider, is not reflecting in the bills itself, it implies that the benefit

        of discount did not pass to the respective policyholder under the

        policy.



6.3. Summary of Insurer’s submissions

     6.3.1. The Insurer submitted that the hospital submits the final bill, prior to

                the discharge of the patient, requesting for final authorization. If the



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 13 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



        charges are found to be excessive, the Insurer’s medical team

        negotiates with the hospital for reduction. Based on these

        negotiations, hospital submits the final bill wherein the negotiated

        reduction is shown as “Discounts”. The final authorization given by

        the Insurer takes into account such reductions agreed by the

        hospital, a copy of which is communicated to the customer.



6.3.2.  The full benefit of such reductions have been passed on the

        policyholders’ since without the negotiated reductions, the insured

        would have suffered additional loss of sum insured and higher

        proportion of non-payables. In all cases, the insured had borne only

        the non-payables as per policy.



6.3.3. The Insurer in its response to the SCN vide email dated 10 January

          2025 stated that



6.3.3.1.  Tariff discounts are deducted while making payments to the

          Hospitals and the Sum Insured is protected.



6.3.3.2.  In terms of Regulation 20 (9) of IRDAI (Third Party

          Administrators - Health Services) Regulations, 2016, the

          “benefit is passed on to the insured”. It does not specifically

          state that methodology of passing the benefit and can be in

          cash as discount line item or reduction in the claim amount

          thereby protecting the sum insured of the customer in the

          policy.



6.4. Concerns on Charge 6



6.4.1.  The Insurer needs to ensure that the discounts, if any stated to be

        agreed between the Network Service Providers and / or TPA and /

        or Insurers, are mentioned in the bills raised upon the policyholders

        upfront.



6.4.2.  Where such discounts are not reflected in the bills raised by the

        hospitals but are instead adjusted by the insurer through deductions

        from the hospital bills, the insurer is required to have an effective



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 14 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



        mechanism to ensure that such discounts are not subsequently

        recovered by the hospital from the policyholder(s) as under the

        pretext of “disallowed items”. The matter assumes greater

        seriousness where the insurer has also failed to communicate to the

        policyholder the specific reasons for the deductions made while

        settling the claim, thereby compromising transparency and the

        policyholder’s ability to understand and verify the deductions.



6.4.3.  Regulation 20(9) requires insurers and TPAs to ensure that

        discounts agreed with hospitals are passed on to the policyholder or

        claimant. Sub-regulation (c) prescribes how this is to be done as

        under:



         i. hospitals must be mandated to show the agreed discount in

                the final bill, so the claimant can see the actual bill raised;



        ii. where the admissible claim exceeds the sum insured, the

                discount is applied to the gross bill before the claimant bears

                the excess;



        iii. co-payment or deductible is applied only after netting off the

                discount.



6.4.4.  Regulation 20(9) prescribes specific procedures, namely disclosure

        in the bill and netting for co-payment, deductible and excess. The

        Insurer has failed to demonstrate compliance with these procedures

        despite being advised to do so at the hearing.



6.5. Decision on Charge 6



6.5.1.  In view of the above, the insurer is warned for not establishing

        effective procedures to ensure that hospital discounts are

        reflected on the invoice itself and the policyholder is made

        aware of the same.



6.5.2.  The insurer is further directed to put in place the required

        systems to ensure the final settlement letter issued from the

        insurer to the policyholder narrates each allowed, disallowed,

        non-payable and discount items clearly. The final settlement



Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 15 of 21

Ref. IRDAI/E&C/ORD/MISC/153/11/2026



                       letter should also provide details of the Sum Insured reduced

                       from the policy limit, following settlement of the claim

Order – In the matter of M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.  Page 16 of 21

8.2.1.  Further the insurer reported rewards paid to Agents as Rs.146.63

        crore in Schedule V return for FY 2020-21, however as per Trial

        Balance as on 31st March,2021 (refer Schedule 3) the Rewards to

        of “agent club expenses” which were Rs.8.39 crore. If agent club

        expenses are added to the rewards, the total rewards come to

        Rs.156.99 crore. Thus in the Schedule V, rewards paid to agents

        were under reported by the insurer.



8.2.2.  Similarly, the insurer reported rewards paid to Agents as Rs.90.99

        comes to Rs.100.88 crore. Thus in the Schedule V rewards paid to

        agents were under reported.
```

```text
===== [attachment 1] मेसर्स स्टार हेल्थ एण्ड अलायड इंश्योरेंस कंपनी लिमिटेड के मामले में आदेश _ Order in the matter of Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited.pdf =====
                          भारतीय बीमा विवियामक और विकास प्राविकरण

               Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India



                                     प्रेस प्रकाशिी I 20 ििंबर 2026

                              Press Release | 20th November 2026



          मेससस स्टार हेल्थ एण्ड अलायड इंश्योरंेसं कपिी वलवमटेडे क मामले में आदेश

    Order in the matter of Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited



भारतीय बीमा विवियामक और विकास प्राविकरण (`आईआरडीएआई’ अथिा `प्राविकरण’) िे मेससस

स्टार हेल्थ एण्ड अलायड इंश्योरंेसं कपिी वलवमटेड (`बीमाकतास’)े क विरूद्ध, 31 जििरी से 11 फरिरी

2022 तक वकये गये एक विरीक्षण तथा अिुिती कारण बताओ िोवटस वििांक 4 विसंबर 2024 और 18

जूि 2025 को आयोवजत एक िैयक्तिक सुििाई से उत्पन्न वकया गया एक आिेश पाररत वकया है।



प्राविकरण िे पाया वक कोविड-19 िािों सवहत, स्वास्थ्य बीमा िािों को संभालिे मंे बीमाकतास िे

असमथसिीय आिारों पर िािों को विराृकत वकया था। प्राविकरण िे यह भी पाया वक बीमाकतास िे ऐसी

कटौवतयाँा की थीं जो पावलसी की शतोंे क द्वारा समवथसत िहीं थीं, तथा कई प्रवतिशीृकत मामलों में, उि

रावश का भुगतािे किल प्राविकरण द्वारा उजागर करिेे क बाि ही वकया गया था। पावलसीिारकों को

विवशष्ट पावलसी की शतें सूवित िहीं की गई थीं वजिेक अंतगसत िािों का विराकरण वकया गया था अथिा

उन्हंे कम वकया गया था, वजससे उन्हें इि विणसयों को िुिौती िेिेे क वलए प्रामावणक आिार से िंवित

वकया गया था।



प्राविकरण िे बीमा अविवियम, 1938 की िारा 102े क अिीि रु. 2 करोड़ काु कल अथसिंड लगाया है

वजसमें िािोंे क विराकरणे क संबंि में आईआरडीएआई (स्वास्थ्य बीमा) विवियम, 2016े क विवियम

27(v)े क उल्लंघिे क वलए रु. 1 करोड़, तथा उपयुसि विवियमोंे क विवियम 27(v), 33(घ)(ii), और

33(घ)(iv) एिं िािोंे क संबंि मंे कटौवतयों और िािा विणसयों की सूििाे क संबंि मंे आईआरडीएआई

(अन्य पक्ष प्रबंिक – स्वास्थ्य सेिाँएा ) विवियम, 2016े क विवियम 21(3)(ग)(i)(ग)े क उल्लंघिोंे क वलए

रु. 1 करोड़ सक्तिवलत हंै।



बीमाकतास को यह सुविवित ि करिेे क वलए िेताििी भी िी गई है वक िेटिकस अस्पतालोंे क साथ सहमवत-

प्राप्त कटौवतयाँा अस्पताले क वबलों मंे प्रवतवबंवबत हों तथा पावलसीिारकों को सूवित की जाँएा (उपयुसि

टीपीए विवियमों का विवियम 20(9)) एिं यह सुविवित करिेे क वलए वििेश विया गया वक उसेक िािा

विपटाि पत्ों मंे सभी अिुमवत-प्राप्त, अिुमवत ि िी गई, अिेय औरू छट की रावशयों और बीमाृकत रावश

मंे कटौती को मििार वलखा जाए। उसको आगे ििीकरण प्रीवमयम 90 विि से अविक अविम रूप से

िसूल करिेे क वलए (स्वास्थ्य बीमा विवियम का विवियम 13(iii)) तथा वशकायतकतासओं को बीमा

लोकपाल का वििरण उपलब्ध ि करािेे क वलए भी िेताििी िी गई; इिेक संबंि मंे सुिारात्मक किम

अवभलेखबद्ध वकये गये थे। यह आिेश अिुिती कारस िाई की ररपोटस सवहत बीमाकतासे क बोडसे क समक्ष

प्रस्तुत वकया जािा िावहए।



विस्तृत आिेश https://irdai.gov.in/web/guest/document-detail?documentId=10053459

पर उपलब्ध है।



आईआरडीएआई पावलसीिारक संरक्षण एिं िािोंे क विष्पक्ष, पारिशी विपटािे क वलए विरंतर प्रवतबद्ध

है।

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (‘IRDAI’ or ‘Authority’) has

passed an Order against M/s Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited (‘Insurer’)

arising from an inspection conducted from 31st January to 11th February 2022, following a

Show Cause Notice dated 4th December 2024 and a personal hearing on 18th June 2025.



The Authority found that, in handling health insurance claims including COVID-19 claims, the

Insurer had repudiated claims on untenable grounds. The Authority further found that the

insurer had made deductions which were not supported by the policy terms, and in many

sampled cases, the amount was paid only after the Authority highlighted them. Policyholders

were not informed of the specific policy conditions under which claims were repudiated or

reduced, depriving them of an informed basis to challenge these decisions.



The Authority has imposed a total penalty of Rs. 2 crore under Section 102 of the Insurance

Act, 1938, comprising Rs. 1 crore for violation of Regulation 27(v) of the IRDAI (Health

Insurance) Regulations, 2016 in respect of repudiation of claims, and Rs. 1 crore for violations

of Regulations 27(v), 33(d)(ii) and 33(d)(iv) of the said Regulations and Regulation

21(3)(c)(i)(c) of the IRDAI (Third Party Administrators – Health Services) Regulations, 2016 in

respect of deductions from claims and communication of claim decisions.



The Insurer has also been warned for not ensuring that discounts agreed with network

hospitals are reflected in hospital bills and made known to policyholders (Regulation 20(9) of

the said TPA Regulations), and directed to ensure that its claim settlement letters itemise all

allowed, disallowed, non-payable and discount amounts and the reduction in Sum Insured. It

was further cautioned for collecting renewal premium more than 90 days in advance

(Regulation 13(iii) of the Health Insurance Regulations) and for not providing Insurance

Ombudsman details to complainants; its corrective steps on these were taken on record. The

Order is to be placed before the Insurer’s Board, with an Action Taken Report to follow.



The detailed Order is available at https://irdai.gov.in/web/guest/document-

detail?documentId=10053459.



IRDAI remains committed to policyholder protection and fair, transparent settlement of claims.
```

```text
===== [attachment 1] भारतीय लेखांकन मानकों (इंड एएस) के साथ जोखिम आधारित पूँजी (आरबीसी) ढाँचे के अभिसरण संबंधी कार्य दलों का गठन _ Constitution of Working Groups on Convergence of the Risk Based Capital (RBC) Framework with the Indian Accounting Standards (IndAS).pdf =====
संदभभ सं. आईआरिीएआई/आरबीसी/ओआरिी/शर्वशर्वध/150/11/2026 शदनांकः 10 नर्वंबर 2026



Ref No.: IRDAI/RBC/ORD/MISC/150/11/2026  Date: 10 November, 2026



                                            कार्ाालर् आदेश

                                          OFFICE ORDER



भारतीर् लेखांाकन मानकोंा (इंाड एएस)े क साथ जोखखम आधाररत पँूजी (आरबीसी) ढाँूचेे क

                               अभभसरण संाबंाधी कार्ा दलोंा का गठन



Constitution of Working Groups on Convergence of the Risk Based Capital (RBC)

                 Framework with the Indian Accounting Standards (IndAS)



1. प्राशधकरण भारतीय बीमा क्षेत्र को र्वतभमान कारक-आधाररत िोधन-क्षमता व्यर्वस्था से एक

    जोखखम आधाररत पूँजी (आरबीसी) व्यवस्था में अशभसरण तक पररर्वतभन की प्रशिया मंे है,

    शिसेक अंतगभत बीमाकताभ की पूँिीगत अपेक्षा उसेक द्वारा र्वहन शकये िानेर्वाले िोस्ट्िमोंे क

    अनुरूप होनी चाशहए शिसका मापन एक आशथभक (बािार-संगत) तुलन-पत्र पर शकया गया हो।



2. भारतीय बीमा शर्वशनयामक और शर्वकास प्राशधकरण (बीमाकताभओंे क बीमांशकक, शर्वत्त और शनर्वेि

    कायभ) (संिोधन) शर्वशनयम, 2026 30 माचभ 2026 को अशधसूशचत शकये गये थे शिनेक अंतगभत

    शर्वत्तीय शर्वर्वरण लागू भारतीय लेिांकन मानक (इंि एएस) शसद्ांतों और नीशतयोंे क अनुसार

    तैयार शकये िाते हंै और सूशचत शकये िाते हैं।



3. दोनों ढाँूचे भार्वी नकदी प्रर्वाहों, बट्टा कटौती (शिस्काउंशटंग), और िोस्ट्िमे क शलए सुस्पष्टू छटे क

    र्वतभमान अनुमानोंे क मापन पर शनशमभत हंै। दोनों ढाँूचों को अलग-अलग, असंबद् आधारों पर

    संचाशलत करने से बीमाकताभओं पर दोहरी लागत लागू होगी, समाधान की िशटलता प्रारंभ होगी,

    तथा असंगत पररणामों और शर्वशनयामक अंतरपणने क शलए गुंिाइि शनशमभत होगी।



4. इस पृष्ठभूशम में, प्रभार्वी दृशष्टकोण यह हो सकता है शक इंाड एएस भवत्तीर् भववरण आरबीसीे क

    भलए प्रारंाभभक भबन्दु और आधार बनेंगे, िो स्पष्ट रूप से पररभाशषत, पारदिी और साक्ष्य-

    आधाररत समायोिनोंे क साथ होंगे, िहाूँ भी आरबीसीे क शर्वर्वेकपूणभ उद्ेदश्ोंे क शलए इस प्रकार

    की आर्वश्कता हो।



5. इस दृशष्टकोण को लागू करने और आर्वश्क शर्वशनयामक शलितों को शर्वकशसत करनेे क शलए,



सक्षम प्राशधकारी ने अनुबंाध 1 और 2 मंे शनधाभररत रूप मंे दो कायभ दलों (`कायभ-दल’)े क गठन



के शलए अनुमोदन प्रदान शकया है।

6. सुश्री िमुना चौधरी और श्री परमेश्वर िेल्ेक िमिः िीर्वन और गैर-िीर्वन कायभ-दलोंे क सदस्य-

    संयोिक होंगे।



7. उक्त कायभ-दल घशनष्ठ समन्वये क साथ कायभ करंेगे। िहाँू भी आर्वश्क हो र्वहाँू दोनों िीर्वन और

    गैर-िीर्वन व्यर्वसाये क शलए सामान्य शर्वषयों पर दोनों कायभ-दलों की संार्ुक्त बैठकोंा में शर्वचार-

    शर्वमिभ शकया िा सकता है ताशक उद्योगे क शलए एक एकल, सुसंगत स्ट्स्थशत उभर सेक।



8. उक्त कायभ-दल समय-सीमाे क अंदर कायभ पूरा करनेे क शलए आर्वश्कताे क अनुसार बारंबारता

    के साथ बैठक करेंगे।



9. प्रत्येक कायभ-दले क शलए गणपूशतभ (कोरम) कम से कम उसेक सदस्ोंा का 50% होगी। शकसी

    संयुक्त बैठके क शलए गणपूशतभ अलग-अलग प्रत्येक कायभ-दले क सदस्यों का कम से कम 50%

    होगी।



10. बैठकों का आयोिन भौशतक, आभासी अथर्वा शमशश्रत पद्शत मंे शकया िा सकता है; र्वीशियो

    कान्फ्ेंरशसंगे क माध्यम से सहभाशगता कोरमे क शलए गणना मंे िाशमल की िाएगी।



11. शनयुक्त बीमांककों अथर्वा मुख्य शर्वत्तीय अशधकाररयोंे क अशतररक्त, अथर्वा उनकी अनुपस्ट्स्थशत

1. The Authority is in the process of transitioning the Indian insurance sector from

    the existing factor-based solvency regime to a Risk Based Capital (RBC)

    framework, under which the capital requirement of an insurer is to be

    commensurate with the risks it carries, measured on an economic (market-

    consistent) balance sheet.



2. Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Actuarial, Finance

    and Investment Functions of Insurers), (Amendment) Regulations, 2026 were

    notified on 30th March, 2026 wherein the financial statements are prepared and

    reported in accordance with applicable Indian Accounting standards (IndAS),

    principles and policies.



3. Both frameworks are built on the measurement of current estimates of future

    cash flows, discounting, and explicit allowance for risk. Running the two

    frameworks on separate, unconnected bases would impose duplicative cost on

    insurers, introduce reconciliation complexity, and create room for inconsistent

    outcomes and regulatory arbitrage.



4. In this background the effective approach could be that the Ind AS financial

    statements shall form the starting point and basis for RBC, with clearly

    defined, transparent, and evidence-based adjustments, wherever the

    prudential objectives of RBC, so necessitate.



5. To give effect to this approach and to develop the necessary regulatory

    instruments, the Competent Authority has approved the constitution of two

    Working Groups (‘WGs’), as set out in Annexures 1 and 2.



6. Ms. Jamuna Choudhary and Mr. Parmeshwar Shelke shall be Member

    Conveners of Life and Non-Life WG, respectively.



7. The WGs shall function in close coordination. Matters common to both life and

    non-life business may be deliberated in joint sittings, whenever necessary, of

    the two WGs so that a single, consistent position emerges for the industry.



8. The WGs shall meet as frequently as necessary to complete the work within

    the timeline.



9. The quorum for a meeting of each WG shall be at least 50% of its members.

    The quorum for a joint sitting shall be at least 50% of the members of each WG

    separately.



10. Meetings may be held in physical, virtual or hybrid mode; participation through

    video-conferencing shall count towards quorum.



                                                                                      पृष्ठ / Page 6 / 12

11. In addition to or in absence of the Appointed Actuaries or the Chief Financial

    Officers, the Valuation Actuaries or the Deputy Chief Financial Officer of

    the respective insurer may be authorized to attend the meeting of the WGs.



12. The WGs may co-opt or invite any expert/official, as may be considered

    necessary.



13. All deliberations, data, drafts and documents of the WGs are strictly

    confidential and shall not be disclosed, shared or used for any purpose other

    than the work of the WGs.



14. Objectives of the Working Groups are as under:

         a. To achieve a coherent convergence of the RBC framework with IndAS,

             using the IndAS financial statements as the basis for RBC, so that a

             single set of underlying data, models and assumptions, of valuation

             framework, serves both purposes to the maximum extent. The resulting

             RBC framework shall be transparent, comparable across insurers,

             resistant to arbitrage, proportionate, and implementable within a realistic

             transition path.

         b. To prepare the Exposure Draft of the RBC Regulations and an

             associated Approach Paper.



15. Guiding Principles for the Working Groups are as under:

         a. The proposed framework shall not lose sight of the objectives and the

             integrity of the principles of both frameworks. Convergence shall

             neither dilute the prudential purpose of RBC (policyholder protection at

             a defined confidence level), nor distort Ind AS objectives (faithful

             representation).

         b. While IndAS allows various choices for insurers, the WGs need to

             investigate the possibility of narrowing in on them based on data and

             outcomes, without curtailing the reasoned flexibility of the options

             available to the insurers.

         c. A standard approach shall be adopted across the industry, however,

             where any divergent approach is possible, the WG shall attempt to

             bridge the divergence by defining the level of governance and the

             methods of monitoring the divergence.



                                                                                      पृष्ठ / Page 7 / 12

         d. Every recommendation shall be backed by analysis, data and quantified

             impact, including sensitivity testing.



16. The Terms of Reference of the Working Groups are as under:

         a. To prepare the Exposure Draft of the RBC Regulations, suitable for

             issue for public consultation, under which the IndAS financial

             statements shall be the basis for the RBC Balance Sheet. The

             Exposure Draft shall, inter alia, provide for the following in consideration

             of the converged approach

                  i. definitions, applicability and commencement;

                 ii. the valuation of assets and liabilities for the RBC Balance Sheet,

                      starting from IndAS carrying values, with an exhaustive list of

                      permitted and mandatory adjustments, wherever necessary;

                 iii. the determination of Available Capital, including its classification

                      into tiers and eligibility limits, wherever necessary, for IndAS

                      based financial statements;

                 iv. the determination of Required Capital, including risk modules,

                      calibration standard, aggregation and diversification;

                 v. appropriate treatment and approach for key components for RBC

                      as derived from IndAS based financial statements — Debt

                      Securities & ECL, Grouping, Initial Recognition, Contract

                      Boundary, Valuation of Properties, Discounting, Contractual

                      Service Margin (CSM), Risk Adjustment for non-financial risk,

                      loss component, Insurance Acquisition Cash Flows, and

                      reinsurance contracts held;

                 vi. solvency ratio, supervisory intervention levels and the ladder of

                      supervisory action as per Section 64VA;

                vii. governance, actuarial and Board responsibilities, use of internal

                      or entity-specific approaches (if any), validation and audit;

               viii. reporting, public disclosure and data-submission requirements;

                 ix. transitional provisions and the phased implementation path; and

                 x. consequential amendments required to other existing regulations

                      of the Authority.



                                                                                      पृष्ठ / Page 8 / 12

b. To prepare an Approach Paper setting out recommendations covering

    all possible scenarios, alternative approaches and their

    consequences, including but not limited to:

         i. Sensitivity testing — sensitivity of Available Capital, Required

             Capital and the solvency ratio to each key assumption and

             methodological choice;

        ii. Ranges — where a single prescribed value is not appropriate,

             recommended acceptable ranges (e.g. for confidence levels,

             cost-of-capital rates, illiquidity premium, lapse or expense

             assumptions), with criteria for positioning within the range;

       iii. Materiality — quantitative and qualitative materiality thresholds

             for adjustments, simplifications, disclosures and changes in

             approach;

       iv. Discounting — construction of the risk-free yield curve,

             reference instruments, extrapolation beyond the last liquid point,

             ultimate forward rate (if any), currency and the top-down versus

             bottom-up approach;

        v. Flooring — whether and at what level (contract, group, portfolio

             or entity) negative best-estimate liabilities or negative CSM

             should be floored, and the treatment of surrender value floors,

             UPR etc;

       vi. Risk margin — scope of alignment between RBC’s risk margin

             with IndAS’s Risk Adjustment;

       vii. Illiquidity premium — necessity and appropriateness of

             illiquidity premium; and

      viii. any other area where alternative approaches are possible.



c. To prepare draft template for submission of RBC data by insurers to

    the Authority, covering the RBC Balance Sheet, the Ind AS-to-RBC

    reconciliation, Available and Required Capital by module, sensitivities,

    assumptions, and qualitative information.



d. To make recommendations on adopting the converged framework for

    actuarial valuation of assets and liabilities under Section 13 and 49 of

    Insurance Act, 1938.



                                                                             पृष्ठ / Page 9 / 12

         e. Assess requirement of recalibration and recommend stress factors

             and additional accounting information required based on IndAS

             valuation.



         f. Examine the treatment of foreign business under RBC vis-à-vis

             requirements of respective foreign jurisdictions.



         g. To examine any other matter incidental to, or connected with, the above,

             or as may be referred to the WGs by the Authority, to ensure a well

             calibrated approach for implementation of RBC overlapping IndAS

             approach



17. The WGs shall complete their work and submit all deliverables within one (1)

    month from the date of issue of this Office Order.



18. This is issued with the approval of the Competent Authority.
```

```text
===== [attachment 1] आईआरडीएआई शिकायत समाधान माह 2026 के दौरान देश भर में 16 शिकायत निवारण शिविर आयोजित करेगा _ IRDAI to organise 16 Grievance Redressal Camps across the country during Grievance Resolution Month 2026.pdf =====
                भारतीय बीमा विवियामक और विकास प्राविकरण

     Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India



                           प्रेस विज्ञप्ति | 06 ििम्बर, 2026

                    Press Release | 06th November, 2026



आईआरडीएआई विकायत समािाि माह 2026े क दौराि देि भर मंे 16 विकायत वििारण



विविर आयोवित करेगा

IRDAI to organise 16 Grievance Redressal Camps across the country during

Grievance Resolution Month 2026



भारतीय बीमा विवियामक और विकास प्राविकरण (आईआरडीएआई) बीमा क्षेत्र में लंवबत विकायतंे क



िीघ्र समािाि क सुसाध्य बिािेे क उद्ेदश्य से, ििंबर 2026े क दौराि विकायत समािाि माह मिा रहा



है।



इस पहले क भागे क रूप में, ििंबर 2026े क दौराि विवभन्न स्थािं पर देि भर में 16 विकायत वििारण



विविर आय वित वकये िाँएगे।



उक्त विविरं का िगर-िार काययक्रम विम्नािुसार हैैः



     क्रम सं.           शहर                  वतवि        द्वारा आयोजित

       1       गुवाहाटी                13 नवंबर 2026   िीिि बीमा पररषद

       2       जयपुर                   14 नवंबर 2026   िीिि बीमा पररषद

       3       अमरावती (आंध्र प्रदेश)  16 नवंबर 2026  सािारण बीमा पररषद

       4       चंडीगढ़                 16 नवंबर 2026   िीिि बीमा पररषद

       5       चेन्नई                  17 नवंबर 2026  सािारण बीमा पररषद

       6       भोपाल                   18 नवंबर 2026  सािारण बीमा पररषद

       7       लखनऊ                    18 नवंबर 2026   िीिि बीमा पररषद

       8       देहराूदन                20 नवंबर 2026  सािारण बीमा पररषद

       9       कोलकाता                 20 नवंबर 2026  सािारण बीमा पररषद

       11      अहमदाबाद                21 नवंबर 2026   िीिि बीमा पररषद

       12      भुवनेश्वर               21 नवंबर 2026  सािारण बीमा पररषद

       13      पटना                    23 नवंबर 2026  सािारण बीमा पररषद

       14      ततरुवनंतपुरम            24 नवंबर 2026   िीिि बीमा पररषद

       15      रांची                   25 नवंबर 2026  सािारण बीमा पररषद

       16      बेंगलुरु                27 नवंबर 2026   िीिि बीमा पररषद



संबंवित स्थािं का वििरण बीमा पररषदंे क द्वारा सूवित वकया िाएगा।

पावलसीिारकं क प्र त्सावहत वकया िाता है वक िे अपिी लंवबत विकायतंे क तत्परतापूणय समािाि की

अपेक्षा करिे तथा बीमा ल कपाल व्यिस्था सवहत, बीमा क्षेत्र मंे उपलब्ध विवभन्न विकायत वििारण

व्यिस्थाओं से पररिय प्राप्त करिेे क वलए इि विविरं मंे सहभावगता करें।



The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is observing

Grievance Resolution Month during November 2026, with the objective of facilitating

the expeditious resolution of pending grievances in the insurance sector.



As part of this initiative, 16 Grievance Redressal Camps will be organised across the

country at various locations during November 2026.



The city-wise schedule of the camps is as follows:



S. No.                  City                  Date      Organised By

   1    Guwahati                    13th November 2026     LI Council

   2    Jaipur                      14th November 2026     LI Council

   3    Amaravati (Andhra Pradesh)  16th November 2026    GI Council

   4    Chandigarh                  16th November 2026     LI Council

   5    Chennai                     17th November 2026    GI Council

   6    Bhopal                      18th November 2026    GI Council

   7    Lucknow                     18th November 2026     LI Council

   8    Dehradun                    20th November 2026    GI Council

   9    Kolkata                     20th November 2026    GI Council

  10    Pune                        20th November 2026     LI Council

  11    Ahmedabad                   21st November 2026     LI Council

  12    Bhubaneswar                 21st November 2026    GI Council

  13    Patna                       23rd November 2026    GI Council

  14    Thiruvananthapuram          24th November 2026     LI Council

  15    Ranchi                      25th November 2026    GI Council

  16    Bengaluru                   27th November 2026     LI Council



The details of the respective venues will be communicated by the insurance councils.



The policyholders are encouraged to participate in these camps to seek prompt

resolution of their pending grievances and familiarise themselves with the various

grievance redressal mechanisms available in the insurance sector, including the

Insurance Ombudsman framework.
```
