```text
===== [attachment 1] आईआरडीएआई (सहायक अनुदेश और परामर्शदात्री समितियाँ) विनियम, 2026 पर एक्सपोज़र प्रारूप _ Exposure Draft on the IRDAI  - Subsidiary Instructions and Consultative Committees Regulations 2026.pdf =====
     भारतीय बीमा विवियामक और विकास प्राविकरण (सहायक अिुदेश और परामशशदात्री

                            सवमवतयाँा) विवियम, 2026 पर एक्सपोज़र प्रारूप



Exposure Draft on the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India

    (Subsidiary Instructions and Consultative Committees) Regulations, 2026.



                                                                                दिनं ाक / Date: 03.11.2026



    1. कायशकारी सारांाश



    भारतीय बीमा विवियामक और विकास प्राविकरण (आईआरडीएआई) सबका बीमा सबकी रक्षा (बीमा

    विवियोंो का संोशोिि) अविवियम, 2025 (इस एक्सपोज़र प्रारूप में इसेक बाद “एसबीएसआर

    अविवियम”े क रूप मंे उल्लिल्लित)े क अंोतर्गत लार्ू वकये र्ये ढाँाचेे क आलोक मंे आईआरडीएआई

    (सहायक अिुदेश और परामशगदात्री सवमवतयाँा) विवियम, 2026 (इस एक्सपोज़र प्रारूप में इसेक बाद

    “प्रस्तावित विवियम”े क रूप में उल्लिल्लित) जारी करिे का प्रस्ताि करता है।



    एसबीएसआर अविवियम द्वारा सविविष्ट वकये र्ये रूप मंे बीमा अविवियम, 1938 की िारा 114बी िे

    परामशगदात्री सवमवतयोंोे क साथ परामशग करिेे क बाद सहायक अिुदेशोंोे क विर्गमे क वलए पद्धवत और

    शतों से संोबंोवित उपबंोि लार्ू वकये हंै। इसेक अलािा, बीमा अविवियम की िारा 114सी प्राविकरण

    को परामशगदात्री सवमवतयोंोे क संोवििाि की पद्धवत विविवदगष्ट करिेे क वलए सशक्त बिाती है।



    आईआरडीएआई िे एक्सपोज़र प्रारूप वदिांोक 17.06.2026े क अिुसार आईआरडीएआई (विवियम

    और सहायक अिुदेश बिािे की प्रविया) विवियम, 2026 का प्रारूप जारी वकया था। अब यह प्रस्तावित

    है वक बीमा अविवियम, 1938े क अंोतर्गत सहायक अिुदेशोंोे क विर्गम को वियंोवत्रत करिेिाला ढाँाचा

    एक अलर् विवियमे क माध्यम से विविवदगष्ट वकया जाए। एक अलर् विवियामक ढाँाचा िारा 114बीे क

    अंोतर्गत शल्लक्ते क विस्तार और सीमाओंो को स्पष्ट रूप से अंोवकत करेर्ा। यह प्राविकरण को, अस्पष्टता

    को स्पष्ट करिे की प्रविया को वियंोवत्रत करिेिाले विवशष्ट रक्षोपायो,ंो अिुमवत-योग्य प्रवियार्त

    अपेक्षाओंोे क स्वरूप, संोबंोवित परामशगदात्री सवमवते क साथ परामशग, उि पररल्लिवतयोंो को वजिमंे

    अत्यािश्यकता, प्रकाशि, समीक्षाे क कारण परामशग को समाप्त वकया जा सकता है और सहायक

    अिुदेशोंो को िापस वलया जाता है, विविवदगष्ट करिेे क वलए सशक्त करेर्ा।



    प्रस्तावित विवियम इि सांोविविक उपबंोिोंो को पररचावलत करिे तथा सहायक अिुदेशोंोे क विर्गम और

    सलाहकार सवमवतयोंोे क र्ठिे क वलए एक संोरवचत, और परामशी ढाँाचा िावपत करिे की अपेक्षा

    करते हैं।



    प्रस्तावित विवियम, अन्य बातोंोे क साथ-साथ, विम्नवलल्लिते क वलए व्यििा करते हंै :



    • सहायक अिुदेशोंोे क विर्गम को वियंोवत्रत करिेिाला ढाँाचा;

    • परामशगदात्री सवमवतयोंो का र्ठि, संोरचिा और कायग-पद्धवत;

    • सहायक अिुदेशोंो की आिविक समीक्षा;

    • सहायक अिुदेशोंोे क संोशोििे क वलए प्रविया; तथा

    • अत्यािश्यक सहायक अिुदेशोंोे क वलए ढाँाचा।



    2. प्रस्तावित विवियमोंा की मुख्य विशेषताएँा :

2.1 सहायक अिुदेशोंाे क विए ढाँाचाःा

एसबीएसआर अविवियम एक सुस्पष्ट विवियामक वलिते क रूप में सहायक अिुदेशोंो की पहचाि करता

है। प्रस्तावित विवियम सहायक अिुदेशोंोे क विस्तार और स्वरूप को विविवदगष्ट करते हंै वजन्हंे विम्नवलल्लित

के वलए जारी वकया जा सकता हैैः



         • विवियमोंो में अस्पष्टताओंो का स्पष्टीकरण; और

         • विवियमोंोे क वलए अिुषंोर्ी प्रवियार्त विषय।

प्रस्तावित विवियम बीमा अविवियम, 1938 की िारा 114बी में अपेवक्षत `अस्पष्टता की पहचाि’ और

`प्रवियार्त आिश्यकता’े क विस्तारे क वलए व्यििा करते हैं।



2.2 परामशशदात्री सवमवतयोंा का गठिाः

बीमा अविवियम, 1938 की िाराओंो 114बी और 114सीे क विवशष्ट प्रयोजिोंोे क वलए, प्रस्तावित विवियम

सहायक अिुदेशोंो से संोबंोवित विषयोंो और आईआरडीएआई द्वारा विवदगष्ट वकये जािेिाले ऐसे अन्य विषयोंो

पर परामशग उपलब्ध करािे की व्यििा करते हंै।

2.3 संाशोिि और समीक्षा का ढाँाचाःा

प्रस्तावित विवियम विविवदगष्ट आिारोंो पर सहायक अिुदेशोंो की समीक्षाे क वलए व्यििा करते हैं तथा उक्त

सहायक अिुदेशोंो मंे संोशोििोंो की अपेक्षा करते हंै।

2.4 अत्यािश्यक सहायक अिुदेशाः

प्रस्तावित विवियम जहाँा संोबंोवित परामशगदात्री सवमवते क साथ पूिग परामशग करिा व्यिहायग िहींो है, िहाँा

अत्यािश्यकता को ध्याि मंे रिते हुए अत्यािश्यक सहायक अिुदेशोंोे क विर्गम को मान्यता प्रदाि करते

हंै।

उक्त ढाँाचा ऐसी कारग िाईे क वलए कारण दजग करिे तथा इसेक द्वारा उत्तरदावयत्वे क साथु कछ

अत्यािश्यकताओंोे क प्रवत विवियामक प्रवतवियाओंो को संोतुवलत रििे की अपेक्षा करता है।



2.5 विषय वििेक विए परामशशदात्री सवमवतयोंा का गठि वकया िाएगाःा

प्रस्तावित विवियम उि विषयोंो की सूची प्रस्तुत करते हैं वजिेक वलए परामशगदात्री सवमवतयोंो का र्ठि वकया

जाएर्ा, वजिमें शावमल हंै पावलसीिारक संोरक्षण, क्षेत्रीय (सेक्टोरल) विकास, बाजार व्यिहार, वित्तीय ल्लिरता

और विवियवमत संोिाओंो की सुल्लिवत, बीमा और बीमा संोबंोिी सेिाँएा , बीमा वितरण और संोबद्ध कायगकलाप,

पुिबीमा और आिश्यक समझे जािेिाले ऐसे अन्य विषय।



2.6 परामशशदात्री सवमवत की बैठक का आयोिि और पदािवियाँा

प्रस्तावित विवियम र्णपूवतग (कोरम) सवहत, परामशगदात्री सवमवत की बैठकोंोे क संोचालि की प्रविया और

पद्धवते क वलए व्यििा करते हंै।



वहतिारकोंा की प्रवतसूचिा (फीडबैक): प्राविकरण उक्त प्रस्तावित संोशोििोंो पर वहतिारकोंो की

विप्पवणयाँा आमंोवत्रत करता है। विवियम का एक्सपोज़र प्रारूप अिुबंाि 1े क अिुसार है। वहतिारक उक्त

एक्सपोज़र प्रारूप पर अपिी विप्पवणयाँा अिुबंाि 2 मंे विविवदगष्ट फामेि मंे प्रस्तुत कर सकते हैं। प्रवतसूचिा

(फीडबैक) 23 ििंोबर 2026 को या उसेक पहले सुश्री अंोजली जाली को anjaly.jolly@irdai.gov.in पर

और श्री आयगिीर चौहाि को aaryaveer.chauhan@irdai.gov.in पर प्रस्तुत की जा सकती है।



यह परामशग-पत्र जिता और वहतिारकोंो की विप्पवणयोंोे क वलए जारी वकया जाता है।

1. Executive Summary



The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) proposes to issue

the IRDAI (Subsidiary Instructions and Consultative Committees) Regulations, 2026

(“herein after referred to as ‘ the proposed Regulations”) in light of the framework

introduced under the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act,

2025 (“herein after referred to as SBSR Act”).



Section 114B of the Insurance Act, 1938 as inserted by the SBSR Act has introduced

provisions relating to the manner and conditions for issuance of Subsidiary Instructions

after consulting the Consultative Committees. Further, section 114C of the Insurance Act

empowers the Authority to specify the manner of constitution of Consultative Committees.



IRDAI vide Exposure draft dated 17.06.2026 had issued draft IRDAI (Procedure for

making Regulations and Subsidiary Instructions) Regulations, 2026. It is now proposed

that the framework governing the issuance of subsidiary instructions under the Insurance

Act, 1938 be specified through a separate regulation. A separate regulatory framework

would clearly delineate the scope and limits of the power under section 114B. It would

also enable the Authority to specify specific safeguards governing the procedure for

clarification of ambiguity, the nature of permissible procedural requirements, consultation

with the concerned Consultative Committee, the circumstances in which consultation may

be dispensed with on account of urgency, publication, review and withdrawal of

subsidiary instructions.



The proposed Regulations seek to operationalize these statutory provisions and establish

a structured, and consultative framework for issuance of subsidiary instructions and

constitution of Consultative Committees.



The proposed Regulations, inter alia, provide for:

• Framework governing issuance of subsidiary instructions;

• Constitution, composition and functioning of Consultative Committees;

• Periodic review of subsidiary instructions;

• Procedure for amendment of subsidiary instructions; and

• Framework for urgent subsidiary instructions.



2.  Key Features of the proposed Regulations:



2.1 Framework for Subsidiary Instructions:



The SBSR Act recognises subsidiary instructions as a distinct regulatory instrument.

The proposed Regulations specify the scope and nature of subsidiary instructions that

may be issued for:



    • Clarification of ambiguities in regulations; and

    • Procedural matters ancillary to regulations.



    The proposed regulations provide for the scope of ‘identification of ambiguity’ and

    ‘procedural requirement’ contemplated in section 114B of the Insurance Act, 1938.

2.2 Constitution of Consultative Committees:



For the specific purpose of Sections 114B and 114C of the Insurance Act,1938, the

proposed Regulations provide for constitution of Consultative Committees to provide

advice on matters relating to subsidiary instructions and such other matters as may be

referred by IRDAI.



2.3 Amendment and Review Framework:



The proposed Regulations provide for review of the subsidiary instructions on specified

grounds and require amendments to the subsidiary instructions.



2.4 Urgent Subsidiary Instructions:



The proposed regulations recognise issuance of Urgent Subsidiary Instructions

considering the urgency where prior consultation with the concerned Consultative

Committee is not practicable.



The framework requires recording of reasons for such action, thereby balancing

regulatory responses to certain exigencies with accountability.



2.5 Subject matters for which Consultative Committees shall be constituted:



The proposed regulations list out the subject matter for which Consultative Committees

shall be constituted, including Policyholder Protection, Sectoral development, Market

conduct, Financial Stability and Health of regulated entities, Insurance and insurance

related services, Insurance distribution and allied activities, Reinsurance and such other

matters as deemed necessary.



2.6 Conduct of meeting and terms of office of Consultative Committee



The proposed regulations provide for the procedure and manner of conduct of meetings

of the Consultative Committee including the quorum.



Stakeholder Feedback: The Authority invites comments from stakeholders on the



proposed amendments. Exposure draft of the Regulation is as per Annexure 1.



Stakeholders may submit their comments on the Exposure Draft in the format specified



in Annexure 2. Feedback may be submitted to Ms. Anjaly Jolly at



anjaly.jolly@irdai.gov.in  and  Mr.  Aaryaveer                    Chauhan  at



aaryaveer.chauhan@irdai.gov.in on or before 23rd November, 2026.



This Consultation Paper is issued for public and stakeholders comments.

         (क)धिशेर्ज्ञताे क संबंधित क्षेत्रों का उधचत प्रधतधिधित्व;

                                                             5

          (ख) धहतोंे क संघर्श से स्वतंत्रता और उससे बचाि;

          (ग) व्यािसाधयक और संस्थागत अिुभि की धिधििता; तथा

          (घ) पाधलसीिारकोंे क धहतों या उपभोिाओंे क धहतों का प्रधतधिधित्व, जहाँा भी धिर्य से संबंधित



              हो।



(5) प्राधिकरण सधमधते क सदस्य-सधचिे क रूप में प्राधिकरणे क एक अधिकारी को िामांधकत कर

सकता है।



(6) परामशशदात्री सधमधत का अध्यक्ष ऐसे धकसी व्यक्ति को आमंधत्रत कर सकता है धजसकी धिशेर्ज्ञता

संगत समझी जाती है।



15. पदािवध

(1) सदस्ये क पद की अिधि धियुक्ति की तारीख से दो िर्श की अिधिे क धलए होगी तथा प्राधिकरण

द्वारा इसे बढाया जा सकता है।

(2) सदस्य प्राधिकरण को धलक्तखत सूचिा देिेे क द्वारा त्याग-पत्र दे सकता है।

(3) प्राधिकरण धकसी सदस्य को हटा सकता है, जहाँा—



          (क) सदस्य अपिे कायों का धििशहण करिे में असमथश है;

          (ख) सदस्ये क पास धहतों का संघर्श है जो महत्वपूणश ढंग से कायोंे क धििशहण को प्रभाधित करता



              है;

          (ग) सदस्य िे ऐसी पद्धधत में कायश धकया है जो सधमधते क उद्ेदश्योंे क प्रधतूकल है; अथिा

          (घ) प्राधिकरण मािता है धक इस प्रकार हटािा लोक धहत मंे आिश्यक है।



16. बैठेंक

(1) परामशशदात्री सधमधत की बैिकों का आयोजि ऐसे समयों और स्थािों पर और इतिी बार धकया

जाएगा, जैसा धक सधमधते क अध्यक्ष द्वारा धििाशररत धकया जाएगा।

(2) बैिकों का संचालि भौधतक रूप से, इलेक्ट्र ाधिक तौर पर अथिा धकसी अन्य पद्धधते क द्वारा धकया

जाएगा जो कायशिाही को अधभधलक्तखत करिे मंे सक्षम हो।

(3) बैिक की सूचिाे क साथ सामान्यतः कायशसूची और संबंधित दस्तािेज धिधिधदशष्ट धकये जाँएा गे।



17. गणपूवतश (कोरम) और वनणशयन

(1) बैिके क धलए गणपूधतश (कोरम) न्यूितम छह सदस्योंे क अिीि, सदस्यों कीु कल संख्या मंे से

आिी होगी।

(2) परामशशदात्री सधमधत का परामशश सामान्यतः सिशसम्मधत से धििाशररत धकया जाएगा।

(3) जहाँा सिशसम्मधत पहुँाचिा संभि िहीं होगा, िहाँा सदस्योंे क धिचार अलग-अलग दजश धकये जाएँा गे।



                                                              6

(4) सधमधत का परामशश धिसम्मत धभन्न धिचारों सधहत, बैिके क कायशिृत्त में दजश धकया जाएगा।



18. वहतों का संघषश

(1) परामशशदात्री सधमधत का प्रत्येक सदस्य धिचारािीि धकसी भी धिर्ये क संबंि में प्रत्यक्ष या अप्रत्यक्ष

धहत का प्रकटीकरण करेगा जो धकसी संघर्श को उत्पन्न कर सकता है।

(2) जहाँा धकसी सदस्ये क धलए धहतों का कोई िोस संघर्श है, िहाँा ऐसा सदस्य संबंधित धिर्ये क धिचार-

धिमशश से स्वयं को अलग रखेगा।



19. गोपनीयता



परामशशदात्री सधमधत का सदस्य अपिे कायोंे क दौराि प्राप्त सूचिाे क संबंि मंे गोपिीयता बिाये रखेगा

तथा धिम्नधलक्तखत को छोड़कर ऐसी सूचिा का प्रकटीकरण िहीं करेगा—

(क) प्राधिकरणे क साथ; अथिा

(ख) धिधिे क द्वारा अपेधक्षत रूप में।



                             अध्याय IV (विविध)



20. शक्तियों का प्रत्यायोजन



प्राधिकरण इि धिधियमों मंे धिधहत अपिी शक्तियों और कायों का प्रत्यायोजि अध्यक्ष अथिा प्राधिकरण

के एक या उससे अधिक पूणशकाधलक सदस्यों अथिा दोिों अथिा प्राधिकरणे क धकसी अधिकारी को कर

सकता है।



21. स्पष्टीकरण जारी करने और कवठनाइयों, यवद कोई हों, कोू दर करने की शक्ति

इि धिधियमोंे क धकसी भी उपबंि को लागू करिे अथिा उसका अथशधिणशय करिे में उत्पन्न होिेिाली धकसी

भी शंका या कधििाई कोू दर करिेे क धलए अध्यक्ष जब भी आिश्यक समझा जाएगा तब उपयुि

स्पष्टीकरण जारी कर सकता है।



In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (zca) and (zcb) of sub section (2) of

Section 114A read with Section 114B and Section 114C of the Insurance Act, 1938 and

section 14 and section 26 of Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act,

1999, the Authority, in consultation with the Insurance Advisory Committee, hereby

makes the following regulations, namely, -



                               CHAPTER I

                             PRELIMINARY



                                       7

1. Short title and commencement

(1) These regulations may be called the Insurance Regulatory and Development

Authority of India (Subsidiary Instructions and Consultative Committees) Regulations,

2026.

(2) These regulations shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official

Gazette.

(3) These Regulations shall be reviewed once every three years from the date of

publication, unless a review, repeal or amendment is warranted earlier.



2. Objective

To lay down the manner for issuing subsidiary instructions and constitution of

consultative committees. The framework seeks to standardize the process of issuing

subsidiary instructions in a transparent and consultative manner.



3. Definitions

(1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires, -



     (a) ‘Act’ means the Insurance Act, 1938 (4 of 1938);

     (b) “Authority” means the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India

     established under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Insurance Regulatory and

     Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999);

     (c) ‘Consultative Committee’ means the Committee constituted by the Authority

     under Section 114C of the Act.

     (d) ‘Regulations’ means the regulations framed by the Authority under section 114A

     of the Act or Section 26 of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority

     Act, 1999.

     (e) ‘Subsidiary Instructions’ mean the instructions issued under section 114B of the

     Act.

(2) All words and expressions used herein and not defined in these regulations but

defined in the Insurance Act, 1938 (4 of 1938) or the Insurance Regulatory and

Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999) or any Rules or Regulations made

thereunder shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in those Acts or

Rules or Regulations.



                                                 CHAPTER II

                                    SUBSIDIARY INSTRUCTIONS



                                                             8

4. Scope and nature of subsidiary instructions

The Authority may issue subsidiary instructions for the purposes specified in sub

section (1) of section 114B of the Act, namely—



   (a) clarifying the ambiguity of any regulation, if any; and

   (b) laying down any procedural requirement ancillary to any regulation.



5. Persons competent to issue subsidiary instructions

(1) Subsidiary instructions may be issued by—



     (a) the Chairperson; or

     (b) one or more whole-time Members authorised by the Chairperson; or

     (c) jointly by the Chairperson and one or more whole-time Members.

(2) Every subsidiary instruction shall expressly mention—

     (a) the regulation to which it relates; and

     (b) the specific purpose under sub section (1) of section 114B.



6. Procedure for issuing subsidiary instructions

(1) Before issuing any subsidiary instruction, the concerned Consultative Committee

constituted under these regulations shall be consulted.

(2) The Authority may consult Insurance Councils, associations or organisations of

insurance intermediaries, agents and other stakeholders before issuing any Subsidiary

Instruction.



7. Identification of ambiguity



(1) For the purposes of clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 114B of the Act, an

ambiguity may include—



         (a) an expression or provision in a regulation which is reasonably capable of

         more than one interpretation;



         (b) an apparent inconsistency between two provisions of the same regulation; or



         (c) an omission in the provision which is necessary to give effect to the

         regulation;



         (d) any other matter in the regulation for which clarification is required.



                                                             9

(2) A subsidiary instruction issued for clarification of an ambiguity shall not alter the

substantive obligation or substantive right established by the regulation.



8. Procedural requirements



(1) A subsidiary instruction may lay down procedural requirements relating to the

implementation or administration of a regulation, including—



         (a) the manner and form of submission of information, statements, returns or

         applications;



         (b) timelines for procedural steps, where such timelines are ancillary to the

         regulation;



         (c) the electronic or other mode of submission;



         (d) the format, authentication or manner of maintenance of records;



         (e) the manner of communication between the Authority and a regulated entity;

         and



         (f) such other procedural matter as is necessary for giving effect to the

         regulation.



(2) No subsidiary instruction shall be issued under this regulation for specifying a matter

which, by virtue of the Act, is required to be specified by regulations.



9. Consultation with Consultative Committee



(1) The concerned Consultative Committee shall be consulted either at a in person

meeting or virtually or through circulation of agenda and notes thereof, before a

subsidiary instruction is issued.



Provided that where subsidiary instructions are required to be made urgently, it may be

issued without consulting the Consultative Committee but after recording the reasons

thereof.



(2) For the purposes of sub-regulation (1), the draft subsidiary instruction, together with

the reasons for proposing the instruction, shall be placed before the concerned

Consultative Committee.



                                                             10

(3) The Consultative Committee shall ordinarily furnish its advice within such period as

may be specified.



10. Publication and Commencement

(1) All subsidiary instructions shall be issued by notification and published on the

website of the Authority.



(2) Subsidiary instructions shall come into effect from the date specified therein.



11. Review and Amendment



(1) The Authority may, on its own motion or on consideration of any representation,

review a subsidiary instruction.



(2) Where a subsidiary instruction is found to—



(a) be inconsistent with the Act, Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act,

1999, rules or regulations;



(b) be no longer necessary; or



(c) have become impracticable or redundant,



the Authority may amend, replace or withdraw such subsidiary instruction.

(3) An amendment or replacement under this regulation shall be issued in the same

manner as the original subsidiary instruction.



                                                CHAPTER III

                                   CONSULTATIVE COMMITTEES

12. Constitution of Consultative Committee(s)

The Authority shall constitute Consultative Committees for the purposes of section

114C of the Act on the following matters:

    1. Policyholder Protection;

    2. Sectoral development;

    3. Market conduct;

    4. Financial Stability and Health of regulated entities;

    5. Insurance and insurance related services;

    6. Insurance distribution and allied activities;

    7. Reinsurance;



                                                             11

    8. Such other matters as deemed necessary.



13. Functions of Consultative Committee

(1) The Consultative Committee shall advise the Authority on—



     (a) matters relating to the making of the subsidiary instructions under section 114B;

     and

     (b) any other issue as may be determined by the Authority.

(2) The advice of the Consultative Committee shall be recommendatory in nature and

shall not be binding on the Authority.



14. Composition of Consultative Committees



(1) The Authority may constitute each Consultative Committee with such number of

members as it may determine, subject to the composition specified in this regulation.



(2) Each Consultative Committee shall ordinarily consist of not more than eleven

members, including—



         (a) Chairperson, being nominated by the Authority from among the members;



         (b) such whole time members or officers of the Authority, not exceeding three,

         as the Authority may nominate;



         (c) five members having domain expertise or experience;



         (d) one person representing policyholder interests or consumer interests;



         (e) one person having non-insurance financial services experience; and



         (f) one person from the field of technology, analytics or data science.



(3) The Authority shall ensure that the composition of a Committee is balanced and

has a fair representation of all relevant stakeholders.



(4) In constituting a Committee, the Authority shall have regard to the need for—



         (a) appropriate representation of relevant areas of expertise;



         (b) independence and avoidance of conflicts of interest;



         (c) diversity of professional and institutional experience; and

                                                             12

         (d) representation of policyholder interests or consumer interests, wherever

         relevant to the subject matter.

(5) The Authority may nominate an officer of the Authority as Member-Secretary of a

Committee.

(6) The Chairperson of the Consultative Committee may invite any person whose

expertise is considered relevant.

15. Term of office

(1) The term of office of a member shall be for a period of two years from the date of

appointment and may be extended by the Authority.

(2) A member may resign by giving written notice to the Authority.

(3) The Authority may remove a member where—

         (a) the member is unable to discharge his functions;

         (b) the member has a conflict of interest which materially affects the discharge

         of functions;

         (c) the member has acted in a manner prejudicial to the objectives of the

         Committee; or

         (d) the Authority considers such removal necessary in the public interest.

16. Meetings

(1) A Consultative Committee shall meet at such times and places and in such manner

as may be determined by the Chairperson of the Committee.

(2) Meetings may be conducted physically, electronically or through any other mode

capable of recording the proceedings.

(3) The notice of a meeting shall ordinarily specify the agenda and relevant documents.

17. Quorum and decision-making



                                                             13

(1) The quorum for a meeting shall be one-half of the total number of members, subject

to a minimum of six members.



(2) The advice of the Consultative Committee shall ordinarily be determined by

consensus.



(3) Where consensus cannot be reached, the views of the members may be recorded

separately.



(4) The advice of the Committee, including dissenting views, shall be recorded in the

minutes of the meeting.



18. Conflict of interest



(1) Every member of a Consultative Committee shall disclose any direct or indirect

interest which may give rise to a conflict in relation to any matter under consideration.



(2) Where a member has a material conflict of interest, such member shall recuse

himself from consideration of the relevant matter.



19. Confidentiality



A member of a Consultative Committee shall maintain confidentiality in respect of

information obtained in the course of the member's functions and shall not disclose

such information except—



         (a) with the Authority; or

         (b) as required by law.



                                                CHAPTER IV

                                            MISCELLANEOUS

20. Delegation of powers

The Authority may delegate its powers and functions in these regulations to

Chairperson or one or more Whole-Time Members or both or any officer of the

Authority.

21. Power to issue clarification and to remove difficulties, if any



In order to remove any doubts or the difficulties that may arise in the application or

interpretation of any of the provisions of these regulations, the Chairperson may issue

appropriate clarifications as and when deemed necessary.



                                                             14
```

```text
धनलक्ष्मी और अन्य मंे माननीय भारते क सिोच्च न्यायालये क वनदेशों का कायाान्वयन – वनजी

िाहनों (कारों और दपवहया िाहनों)े क वलए मोटर बीमा किर की चार स्तररत संरचना, विकल्प

फामा और ग्राहक सूचना पत्रक का वनगाम

Subject: Implementation of directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in

the matter CA No. 14369 / 2025 National Insurance Company Ltd. V. Smt.

Thungala Dhana Laxmi & others- four layered structure of motor insurance

cover for private vehicles (cars and two wheelers), option form and issuance of

सीए सं. 14369/2025 नेिनल इंश्योरंेसं कपनी शल. बनाम श्रीमर्ी र्ुंगला धनलक्ष्मी और अन्य मंे माननीय

सर्वोच्च न्यायालये क शनदेिों की ओर ध्यान आकशषभर् शकया जार्ा है; शजनमंे शनजी र्वाहनों (4 पशहयों र्वाले

और 2 पशहयों र्वाले)े क संबंध मंे; i) अन्य पक्ष देयर्ा, ii) अशधभोशगयोंे क प्रशर् शर्वशधक देयर्ा, iii) र्वैयस्ट्िक

दुर्भटना, और iv) र्वाहन की शनजी क्षशर्े क शर्वरुद्ध बीमा कर्वर देर्े हुए चार-स्तररर् मोटर बीमा पाशलसी

Attention is drawn to the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, in CA No.

14369/2025 National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Smt. Thungala Dhana Laxmi &

others); wherein it has directed to bring in a four-layer motor insurance policy structure

offering insurance cover against i) Third Party liability, ii) Legal liability to occupants,

iii) Personal accident, and iv) Own damage of the vehicle; with respect to private

vehicles (4 wheelers and 2 wheelers). This is to bring clarity about availability of

various policy options to the vehicle-owner so as to allow him/her to make an informed

choice of purchasing suitable insurance protection. It has also stated that the IRDAI

in consultation with General Insurance Council and insurance companies, shall

formulate uniform policy wordings for the above optional covers.

2. Accordingly, based on the draft wordings submitted by the General Insurance

Council in consultation with the industry, in accordance with the above directions of

the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the Authority, in exercise of the powers conferred by

Section 14(2) of Insurance Act 1938, hereby issues the uniform wordings for the

policies issued under four-layer motor insurance policy structure and also customer

option form for private vehicles given as Annexure. After the introduction of four-layer

motor insurance policy structure for new cars and new two-wheelers, an insured may

be given the following options:



       I. SECTION I - LIABILITY TO THIRD PARTIES (MANDATORY)

      II. SECTION II - LEGAL LIABILITY TO OCCUPANT(S) OR PILLION RIDER



             INCLUDING EMPLOYEES OF THE INSURED (OPTIONAL)

     III. SECTION III - PERSONAL ACCIDENT COVER



             (i) Mandatory Personal Accident Cover for Owner-Insured

             (ii) Personal Accident Cover for Occupants / Pillion Rider including any



                  driver other than owner-driver (Optional)

     IV. SECTION IV - LOSS OF OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHILCLE INSURED



             (OPTIONAL).



3. All General Insurers carrying on motor insurance business, shall provide the cover

vide a policy as per four-layer motor insurance policy structure adopting uniform

wordings along with mandatory option form and customer information sheet for all

private vehicles including new cars and new two wheelers. Obtaining the duly

completed option form from customers is mandatory for all insurance policies issued

to this category of vehicles.



4. For existing policies also, if cover under section II is sought during the currency

of the policy, the same shall be made available upon the payment of an additional

premium. However, the risk shall start from the date and time mentioned in the

endorsement issued thereupon. This option can only be availed from the insurer

who has issued the Third Party insurance policy. No existing Motor Third Party

Insurance need to be cancelled by either the insurer or the insured for opting the

additional covers.

       सर्वे सं. 115/1, फाइनंशियल शिस्ट्रि क्ट, नानकरामगुिा, हैदराबाद 500 032

Survey No. 115/1, Financial District, Nanakramguda, Hyderabad 500 032



                 दूरभाष Phone: 040-20204000; www.irdai.gov.in

5. The schedule shall reflect the actual coverage offered along with premium

charged against each section in a transparent manner and the certificate of

insurance shall be issued in compliance with the provisions of CMV Rules, 1989.

In addition, the option form duly completed by insured should form part of the policy.



6. Every customer, at the time of purchase of insurance, to be issued customer

option form informing about the four-layer motor insurance policy structure,

whereby, they can opt in by tick whether offline or online. It is also mandatory to

issue Customer Information Sheet at the point of sale.



7. The policies issued by the insurance company, the Policy and Schedule shall be

read together and any word or expression to which a specific meaning has been

attached in any part of this Policy or of the Schedule shall bear the same meaning

wherever it may appear.



8. Insurance companies may continue to innovate the coverage and determine the

pricing of the Own Damage covers, in consonance with market forces. The insurer

is free to add/delete General exclusions and conditions based on the coverage

opted, standard exclusions, conditions etc., provided there is no restriction to the

basic coverage under four-layer motor insurance policy structure offered to the

insured.



9. The four-layer motor insurance policy structure and standard wordings along

with option form shall come into force from December 15, 2026. All policies issued

w.e.f. December 15, 2026 shall conform to the above.



10. Insurers are also directed to ensure that integration of the 4 tier policy structure

with Bima Sugam is completed simultaneously, so that their policies are available

from Bima Sugam from the same date.
```

```text
                            Chapter – I: Applications to be submitted



A.1 No-objection Certificate (NOC) [refer Regulation 6(1)(b) of Registration Regulations,

2024]:

The application for issuance of No-Objection Certificate (NOC), as referred in

Regulation 6(1)(b) of Registration Regulations, 2024 shall be in the form IRDAI/NOC as

per Annexure 1. The application shall be submitted to IRDAI, at email ID registrations-



                                                                                                                    पृष्ठ / Page 19 / 35

cell@irdai.gov.in. Further, physical copy of the duly authenticated application shall also

be sent to In-charge of Registration Cell at following address:



              “In-charge, Registration Cell

              Finance and Investment Department,

              Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India,

              Survey No. 115/1, Financial District, Nanakramguda,

              Gachibowli, Hyderabad – 500032, Telangana, India”



The application may also be submitted online at IRDAI website i.e. www.irdai.gov.in

[currently, the form to apply for NOC for ‘New Insurers Registration’ is placed under the

‘E-services’ section on the website of the Authority.]



B.1 Application for Issuance of Form IRDAI/R1 [refer Regulation 6(1)(c) of Registration

Regulations, 2024]:



    The application for issuance of Form IRDAI/R1, as referred in Regulation 6(1)(c) of

    Registration Regulations, 2024 shall be made on the letter head of the applicant,

    duly signed by its authorized person and shall be accompanied with the following

    documents:



       i. Copy of Certificate of Incorporation of the applicant.

      ii. Copy of Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association of the



             applicant.

      iii. A Resolution passed by the Board of the promoter(s) of the applicant for



             following:

                  a. Approval for entering into the insurance business.

                  b. Authorization of person to act on behalf of the promoter(s).



      iv. A Resolution passed by the Board of the applicant for the following:

                  a. Approval for entering into the insurance business.

                  b. Authorization of person to act on behalf of the applicant.



C.1 Format of Form IRDAI/R4, as referred to in Regulation 57 of Registration

Regulations, 2024, is at Annexure 2.



D.1 Format of Form IRDAI/ToS, as referred to in Chapter IV of Registration Regulations,

2024 is at Annexure 3.



     Chapter- II: Clarifications, Submission of Returns and Transitory Provisions



A.1 With respect to Regulation 21: With regard to shares allotted pursuant to

Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) or any other similar scheme for the benefit of the

employees or directors of the insurer, the following shall be complied with:



    1. Exercise of ESOP is subject to provisions of section 6A(4)(b) of the Act read with

         Registration Regulations, 2024.



                                                                                                                    पृष्ठ / Page 20 / 35

    2. Where specific trust has been formed by an insurer for issuance of ESOPs to

         their employees, the issue of shares to such trust and exercise of option by one

         or more employees shall also fall within the ambit of the section 6A(4)(b) of the

         Act read with Registration Regulations, 2024.



    3. Where exercise of ESOP by one or more KMPs or Directors, whether singly or

         jointly, is beyond the threshold limit specified in section 6A(4)(b) of the Act read

         with Registration Regulations, 2024, the prior approval of the Authority shall be

         sought before such exercise, in the manner as specified in Regulation 22 of the

         Registration Regulations, 2024.



A.2 Regulation 21 of the Registration Regulation, 2024 shall be applicable to all insurers

including the insurers having its equity shares listed on the stock exchange(s). The

insurer shall put-in place necessary mechanism to ensure compliance with the said

Regulations including necessary communication with stock exchange(s) and capital

market intermediaries such as Registrar and Transfer Agent or Depository Participant.

It shall be duty of the concerned insurer to ensure compliance with the said Regulation.



B.1 With respect to Regulation 29(5) of Registration Regulations, 2024: The insurer

shall submit the application seeking prior-approval for transfer of shares as per the form

IRDAI/ToS, as specified in Annexure-3 of this Circular, subject to following additional

requirements:



  1. The details of transferee may be furnished if the same is available. In case the

       details of transferee are unavailable or unascertainable, the same shall not be

       mandatory to be furnished.



  2. The resolution passed by the Board of insurer, certified by the Company Secretary,

       approving the issuance of capital/ offer for sale proposed shall also be submitted

       along with the application.
```

```text
===== [attachment 1] आईआरडीएआई ने आधार प्रमाणीकरण, डिजिलॉकर और डार्क पैटर्न पर कार्यशाला का आयोजन किया _ IRDAI organizes Workshop on Aadhaar Authentication, DigiLocker and Dark Patterns.pdf =====
                           भारतीय बीमा विवियामक और विकास प्राविकरण

                Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India



                                      प्रेस विज्ञप्ति | 02 ििम्बर, 2026

                                     Press Release | 2nd November, 2026



आईआरडीएआई िे आिार प्रमाणीकरण, वडविलॉकर और डाकक पैटिक पर कायकशाला का आयोिि वकया

 IRDAI organizes Workshop on Aadhaar Authentication, DigiLocker and Dark Patterns



आईआरडीएआईे क प्रधान कार्ाालर्, हैदराबाद में 2 नवंबर 2026 को सभी बीमाकर्ााओंे क मुख्य

अनुपालन अधधकाररर्ों (सीसीओ)े क धलए आधार प्रमाणीकरण, धडधिलॉकर और डाका पैटना पर एक

कार्ाशाला आर्ोधिर् की गई।



कार्ाशाला का उ्दघाटन श्री अिर् सेठ, अध्यक्ष, आईआरडीएआई और श्री सौरभ धविर्, मुख्य कार्ाकारी

अधधकारी, भारर्ीर् धवधशष्ट पहचान प्राधधकरण (र्ूआईडीएआई)े क द्वारा धकर्ा गर्ा। अपने मुख्य संबोधन

मंे, अध्यक्ष ने बीमा उद्योग को आधार प्रमाणीकरण सेवाओं को अपनाने, धडधिलॉकर को अपनी कार्ाप्रणाली

मंे शाधमल करने और पारदशी र्था धनष्पक्ष धडधिटल प्रथाओं को सुधनधिर् करनेे क धलए प्रेररर् धकर्ा।

र्ूआईडीएआईे क मुख्य कार्ाकारी अधधकारी ने बर्ार्ा धक आधार बीमा िीवनचक्र की प्रधक्रर्ाओं कोै कसे

मिबूर्ी प्रदान कर सकर्ा है।



र्ूआईडीएआईे क प्रधर्धनधधर्ों ने आधार प्रमाणीकरण पर एक सत्र आर्ोधिर् धकर्ा, धिसमंे चेहरे,

बार्ोमेधटि क और ओटीपी-आधाररर् प्रमाणीकरण शाधमल था। बीमाकर्ााओं से चेहरेे क प्रमाणीकरण को

अपनाने का आग्रह धकर्ा गर्ा, िो िीधवर्र्ा का पर्ा लगाने में सक्षम बनार्ा है और मोबाइल फोने क

माध्यम से कभी भी, कहीं भी प्रर्ोग धकर्ा िा सकर्ा है। र्ह रेखांधकर् धकर्ा गर्ा धक ग्राहक िुड़ने(ऑन-

बोधडंिग)े क दौरान आधारे क उपर्ोग से एक धनबााध, र्ीव्र और कागज़ रधहर् अनुभव प्राप्त होर्ा है, साथ

ही डेटा की शुद्धर्ा बढ़र्ी है और धोखाधड़ीे क िोखखम को कम करने मंे सहार्र्ा धमलर्ी है। ग्राहक िुड़ने

से लेकर दावा धनपटान र्के क उपर्ोगे क उदाहरण प्रस्तुर् धकए गए, धिनमंे दशाार्ा गर्ा धक आधार

प्रमाणीकरण पॉधलसीधारकों को सेवा प्रदान करने की प्रधक्रर्ा को सुरधक्षर्, धनबााध औरु कशल बना सकर्ा

है। इसेक अधर्ररक्त, इस बार् पर धवशेष बल धदर्ा गर्ा धक आधार प्रमाणीकरणे कवल र्ूआईडीएआई

द्वारा ही धकर्ा िाना चाधहए, िो प्रमाधणकर्ा का एकमात्र स्रोर् है।



इलेक्ट्ि ॉधनकी और सूचना प्रौद्योधगकी मंत्रालर् (एमईआईटीवाई)े क राष्टि ीर् ई-गवनंेस प्रभाग(एनईिीडी)े क

प्रधर्धनधधर्ों ने धडधिलॉकर पर एक सत्र आर्ोधिर् धकर्ा, धिसमें बीमा मूल्य श्रंरखला और उत्पाद श्रेधणर्ों में

धडधिलॉकर और संस्था लॉकरे क उपर्ोगे क उदाहरण प्रस्तुर् धकए गए।

श्री आर.े क. शमाा, कार्ाकारी धनदेशक, आईआरडीएआई द्वारा धडधिटल बीमा र्ात्रा में डाका पैटना पर

आर्ोधिर् सत्र में,ें कद्रीर् उपभोक्ता संरक्षण प्राधधकरण (सीसीपीए) द्वारा अधधसूधचर् डाका पैटना का

धनवारण और धवधनर्मने क धलए मागादशाक धसद्धांर्, 2023े क प्रमुख प्रावधानों पर चचाा की गई। बीमा

कंपधनर्ों को कहा गर्ा धक वे सूचना प्राप्त करने र्ा मूल्य भाव प्राप्त करने की शर्ाे क रूप में वेबसाइट

आगंर्ुकों को मोबाइल नंबर िैसी व्यखक्तगर् िानकारी साझा करनेे क धलए बाध्य न करंे। इस बार् पर िोर

धदर्ा गर्ा धक धडधिटल बीमा र्ात्रांए भ्रामक अधभकल्पनाओं से रधहर् होनी चाधहए और उपभोक्ताओं को

बीमा उत्पादों को समझने, सूधचर् धनणार् लेने और अपनी व्यखक्तगर् िानकारी र्था संप्रेषणों पर धनर्ंत्रण

रखने में सक्षम बनानी चाधहए। पारदशी प्रकटीकरण, उधचर् धवकल्प संरचना और उद्ेदश्य-धवधशष्ट सहमधर्

को एक धनष्पक्ष, धिम्मेदार और भरोसेमंद धडधिटल बीमा पाररखस्थधर्की र्ंत्रे क प्रमुख स्तंभोंे क रूप में

पहचाना गर्ा, िो दीघा अवधधे क धलए उपभोक्ता में धवश्वास और धनष्ठा का धनमााण करर्ा है।



A workshop on Aadhaar Authentication, DigiLocker and Dark Patterns for the Chief

Compliance Officers (CCOs) of all insurers was held on 2nd November 2026 at the IRDAI

Head Office, Hyderabad.



The workshop was inaugurated by Mr. Ajay Seth, Chairman, IRDAI, and Mr. Saurabh

Vijay, CEO, Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI). In his keynote address, the

Chairman encouraged the insurance industry to adopt Aadhaar authentication services,

integrate DigiLocker into its operational workflows and ensure transparent and fair

digital practices. The CEO, UIDAI, outlined how Aadhaar can strengthen processes

across the insurance lifecycle.



Representatives of UIDAI conducted the session on Aadhaar Authentication, which

covered face, biometric and OTP-based authentication. Insurers were urged to adopt

face authentication, which enables liveness detection and can be accessed anytime,

anywhere through a mobile phone. It was highlighted that the use of Aadhaar during

customer on-boarding enables a seamless, faster and paperless experience, while

improving data accuracy and helping mitigate the risk of fraud. Use cases from customer

onboarding to claims settlement were presented, showing how Aadhaar authentication

can make service delivery to policyholders secure, seamless and efficient. Further, it

was emphasized that Aadhaar authentication should be done exclusively from UIDAI

which is the only source of truth.



Representatives of the National e-Governance Division (NeGD), Ministry of Electronics

and Information Technology (MeitY), conducted the session on DigiLocker, presenting

use cases of DigiLocker and Entity Locker across the insurance value chain and product

lines.



The session on Dark Patterns in the Digital Insurance Journey, conducted by Mr. R. K.

Sharma, Executive Director, IRDAI, covered the key provisions of the Guidelines for

Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, notified by the Central Consumer

Protection Authority (CCPA). Insurers were told to avoid forcing visitors to their website

to part with personal details such as mobile number, as a condition for getting access

to information or generating a quote. It was stressed that digital insurance journeys

should be free of dark patterns and should empower consumers to understand

insurance products, make informed decisions and control their personal information and

communications. Transparent disclosures, fair choice architecture and purpose-specific

consent were identified as key pillars of a fair, responsible and trustworthy digital

insurance ecosystem that builds long-term consumer trust and loyalty.
```

- **official PDF URL:** https://ifsca.gov.in/CommonDirect/DownloadFile?id=fc2cfb582037f82d92801abc771712f1&fileName=Guidelines_on_critical_issues_to_be_discussed_during_the_meetings_of_Public_Interest_Directors_of_the_Market_Infrastructure_Institutions_20261127_1226.pdf
- **effective date:** with immediate effect
- **local text file name:** IFSCA-1127-01.txt

```text
                                        CIRCULAR



IFSCA/CMD/MIIT/PID/2026/001                              November 27, 2026



To,



All Stock Exchanges in the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC);



All Clearing Corporations in the IFSC;



The Depository in the IFSC;



(Collectively the ‘Market Infrastructure Institutions’)



Madam/Sir,



Subject: Guidelines on critical issues to be discussed during the meetings of Public

Interest Directors of the Market Infrastructure Institutions



1. Reference may be drawn to the International Financial Services Centre Authority (Market

     Infrastructure Institutions) Regulations, 2021 [hereinafter referred to as "MII

     Regulations”] particularly, sub-regulation (1) of regulation 25, which requires the

     governing board, directors, committee members and key management personnel of

     Market Infrastructure Institutions to abide by the Code of Conduct specified under Part

     B of Schedule I of the MII Regulations.



2. Reference may also be drawn to clause (b) of Section II.C of Part B under Schedule I of the

     MII Regulations, which inter-alia, requires Public Interest Directors of the Market

     Infrastructure Institutions to meet separately, at least once in six months to exchange

     views on critical issues and submit a report of such meeting to the Authority and to the

     governing board of the Market Infrastructure Institution.



3. To ensure that such meetings, and the reports focus on critical issues, the Authority

     hereby specifies guidelines for the conduct of such meetings and deliberations to be made

     therein.



4. The critical issues to be discussed in the meetings of the Public Interest Director shall,

    inter-alia, include the following:

     i. to review the status of compliance with all applicable Acts, regulations, circulars,

           guidelines, communications issued by the Authority, from time to time;



    ii. to review the functioning of Vertical-1 i.e. “Critical Operations” and Vertical-2 i.e.

           “Regulatory, Compliance, Risk Management and Investor Grievances”, as specified

           under Schedule-II of the MII Regulations;



    iii. to review the adequacy of resources (both financial and human) for effective

           functioning of Verticals 1 and 2, as specified under Schedule-II of the MII

           Regulations;



    iv. to identify issues which may involve conflict of interest for the Market Infrastructure

           Institutions or may have significant impact on the functioning of the Market

           Infrastructure Institutions or may not be in the interest of securities market;



     v. to review and rationalize the reliance of the Market Infrastructure Institutions on

           the parent entity, particularly in relation to technology infrastructure, critical

           operational functions or any other material matters;



    vi. to review and evaluate the adequacy of the safeguards adopted by the Market

           Infrastructure Institutions for the protection, confidentiality, integrity and security

           of investor data, including measures to address risks arising from the use of

           emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML);



   vii. to assess the quality, adequacy and timeliness of the flow of information furnished

           by the management of the Market Infrastructure Institutions to its governing board

           and to the Public Interest Directors, and to identify the observations and concerns

           raised by the Public Interest Directors in the meetings of the governing board or its

           committees that have not been appropriately documented, satisfactorily addressed

           or followed through to their logical conclusion; and



  viii. to review the corrective steps taken by the Market Infrastructure Institutions on the

           observations made by the Authority in its inspections, and on the findings of system

           audit and cyber security audit of the Market Infrastructure Institutions, particularly

           in respect of governance standards, technology and cyber security.



5. Every Public Interest Director shall mandatorily attend the meetings of the Public Interest

    Directors held to deliberate on the objectives/critical issues specified in clause 4 above;



6. The report of such meetings of the Public Interest Directors shall be prepared for each

    half-year, namely, April to September and October to March, and shall be submitted to the

    Authority vide email to capital-market@ifsca.gov.in , within such time as stipulated under

    the ‘Master Circular for recognised Stock Exchanges and recognised Clearing Corporations’

    dated June 05, 2026;



7. The report referred in clause 6 above, shall cover the matters specified in clause 4,

    including the deliberations held, the key observations made, the concerns raised and the

    outcome of such meetings;



8. The Public Interest Directors shall also place a copy of the report before the Governing

    Board of the Market Infrastructure Institutions, where deemed appropriate;



    Provided that such submission of report to the Governing Board shall not be a prerequisite

    for, or otherwise affect the obligation of the Public Interest Directors to submit the report

    directly to the Authority within the stipulated timeline.



9. Every Public Interest Director who is a member of the committee of the Market

    Infrastructure Institutions, including a statutory committee, shall brief to the other Public

    Interest Directors on the working of that committee.



10. For the purpose of deliberating on the critical issues specified in clause 4, Public Interest

    Directors may discuss with the concerned Vertical Heads or Key Management Personnel

    or any other personnel of the Market Infrastructure Institution, as deemed appropriate.



11. This Circular is issued in exercise of powers conferred by Sections 12 and 13 of the

    International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019 read with regulation 72 of

    the MII Regulations, and shall come into force with immediate effect.



A copy of this Circular is available on the website of the International Financial Services

Centres Authority at www.ifsca.gov.in .



                                                                                                   Yours faithfully,



                                                                                                 Shubham Goyal

                                                                                    Deputy General Manager

                                    Division of Market Infrastructure Institutions & Technology

                                                                               Capital Markets Department

                                                                      Email: goyal.shubham@ifsca.gov.in

                                                                                     Tel: +91- 079-61809806


```

- **kind:** Circular
- **exact title:** Adherence to advisories and vulnerability notes issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)
- **addressed to / applies to:** All Regulated Entities in the International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs)
- **official URL (detail page):** https://ifsca.gov.in/Legal/Index?MId=DFLOIsPqR10=
- **official PDF URL:** https://ifsca.gov.in/CommonDirect/DownloadFile?id=fc2cfb582037f82d92801abc770f5f9e&fileName=Adherence_to_advisories_and_vulnerability_notes_issued_by_the_Indian_Computer_Emergency_Response_Team__CERT_In__20261125_0641.pdf
- **effective date:** with immediate effect
- **local text file name:** IFSCA-1125-02.txt

```text
                           CIRCULAR



IFSCA-CSD/MSC/05/2026-DCS            November 25, 2026



To,

All Regulated Entities in the International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs)



Dear Madam/Sir,



Sub: Adherence to advisories and vulnerability notes issued by the Indian

Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)



1. IFSCA, vide circular dated March 10, 2025, issued the 'Guidelines on Cyber Security

     and Cyber Resilience for Regulated Entities in IFSCs', as amended vide circular IFSCA-

     CSD/MSC/1/2026-DCS dated March 10, 2026 (hereinafter referred to as the

     'Guidelines on Cyber Security for all REs'), prescribing a principles-based minimum

     baseline framework applicable to all Regulated Entities (REs). Subsequently, vide

     circular IFSCA-CSD/MSC/2/2026-DCS dated April 20, 2026, IFSCA issued the

     'Guidelines on Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience for Market Infrastructure

     Institutions (MIIs) in IFSC' (hereinafter referred to as the 'Guidelines on Cyber

     Security for MIIs').



2. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), the national agency for

     incident response under Section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000

     (hereinafter referred to as the 'IT Act'), regularly issues advisories and vulnerability

     notes on cyber threats and vulnerabilities affecting software, hardware and services,

     along with the recommended countermeasures. These are published on the website

     of CERT-In (www.cert-in.org.in).



3. The Guidelines on Cyber Security for MIIs, inter alia, require the MIIs to:



i) align their log retention policy with the guidelines and directions issued by

       CERT-In



ii) align their Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing with the

       applicable guidelines and requirements prescribed by the National Critical

       Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC) and CERT-In



                                                                                Page 1 of 4

     iii) report cyber incidents to CERT-In in accordance with the guidelines and

            directions issued by CERT-In from time to time.



4. Accordingly, with a view to strengthening cyber resilience and ensuring timely

     identification, assessment and remediation of known vulnerabilities across the IFSC

     ecosystem, it has been decided that all REs shall ensure compliance with the

     applicable advisories and vulnerability notes issued by CERT-In from time to time.

     Such compliance shall extend to all relevant IT systems, applications, network

     infrastructure and services deployed, operated or managed by the REs, including

     those hosted, operated or managed on their behalf by parent entities, group entities

     or third-party service providers.



     REs shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with these requirements,

     irrespective of the ownership, hosting or operational management arrangements

     governing such systems and services.



     Towards this effect, all REs, including the MIIs, shall:



     a) Put in place a mechanism for the timely receipt, monitoring and tracking of

            advisories and vulnerability notes issued by CERT-In. This shall include regular

            monitoring of the official CERT-In website, subscription to CERT-In alerts and

            maintenance of an appropriate internal tracking mechanism to ensure that

            relevant advisories are promptly identified and acted upon.



     b) Assess, without undue delay, each advisory and vulnerability note for its

            applicability to the RE’s IT systems, applications, network devices and services,

            including those hosted, operated or managed on its behalf by its parent entity,

            group entity or third-party service provider.



     c) Implement the countermeasures recommended by CERT-In, such as patches,

            configuration changes or compensating controls, within the timelines specified

            in the patch management policy of the RE, which shall be commensurate with

            the severity of the vulnerability. Vulnerabilities rated as critical or high severity

            by CERT-In in the relevant advisory or vulnerability note, those known to be

            actively exploited and those affecting internet-facing systems shall be accorded

            the highest priority for remediation.



     d) Where a recommended countermeasure cannot be implemented within the

            timelines referred to in clause (c) above, the RE shall formally document:



                                                                                                   Page 2 of 4

             • the reasons thereof

             • the associated risks

             • the compensating controls adopted

             • the expected date of implementation



            with the approval of the Designated Officer referred to in para 6 of the

            Guidelines on Cyber Security for all REs, or in the case of MIIs, the Chief

            Information Security Officer (CISO) appointed in terms of para 7 of Annexure A

            to the Guidelines on Cyber Security for MIIs.



     e) Maintain adequate and verifiable records of the assessment of each CERT-In

            advisory and vulnerability note and the action taken thereon. Such records shall

            be made available to IFSCA as and when sought and to the cyber security

            auditor for examination during the course of the cyber security audit.



5. Clauses (b) to (e) of para 4 above shall apply to the advisories and vulnerability notes

     issued by CERT-In on or after the date of this circular.



6. REs operating within group-wide security arrangements may rely on group-level

     arrangements for compliance with para 4 above, provided that such arrangements

     cover the systems supporting their operations in the IFSC and the records referred

     to in para 4(e) above are available with the RE and can be produced to IFSCA as and

     when sought. The responsibility for compliance shall remain with the RE.



7. REs are also reminded that the Directions issued by CERT-In under Section 70B(6) of

     the IT Act, vide No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In dated April 28, 2022, apply to them

     independently of the guidelines issued by IFSCA. These include the requirements to

     report cyber incidents to CERT-In within six (6) hours of noticing such incidents or

     being brought to notice about such incidents, and to maintain logs of all ICT systems

     securely for a rolling period of 180 days. The REs shall also ensure that logs

     maintained on their behalf by their parent entity, group entity or third-party service

     provider are maintained, and can be produced to CERT-In, in accordance with the

     said Directions.



8. Compliance with this circular shall be covered in the annual cyber security audit of

     the RE under the Guidelines on Cyber Security for all REs, or in the case of MIIs, the

     annual cyber audit under the Guidelines on Cyber Security for MIIs. This para shall



                                                                                                   Page 3 of 4

     not apply to the REs exempted from the annual cyber security audit under para 23 of

     the Guidelines on Cyber Security for all REs.

9. REs shall put in place the mechanism referred to in para 4(a) above within thirty (30)

     days from the date of this circular.

10. This Circular is issued in exercise of the powers conferred by Sections 12 and 13 of

     the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019, to develop and

     regulate the financial services market in the International Financial Services Centre.

This Circular shall come into force with immediate effect. A copy of this circular is

available on the website at www.ifsca.gov.in.



                                                                                            Yours Faithfully,

                                                                                            Praveen Kamat

                                                                        Chief General Manager & CISO

                                                                              Division of Cyber Security

                                                                 Email: praveen.kamat@ifsca.gov.in

                                                                              Tel: +91- 079 - 61809820



                                                                                                   Page 4 of 4


```

- **addressed to / applies to:** All the recognised Stock Exchanges in the International Financial Services Centres (IFSC) All the recognised Clearing Corporations in the IFSC All the recognised Depositories in the IFSC All Broker Dealers and Clearing Members in the IFSC
- **official URL (detail page):** https://ifsca.gov.in/Legal/Index?MId=7mer%201NZ3CQ=
- **official PDF URL:** https://ifsca.gov.in/CommonDirect/DownloadFile?id=fc2cfb582037f82d92801abc770d995c&fileName=Circular_on_Amendment_to_the_Master_Circular_for_recognised_Stock_Exchanges_and_recognised_Clearing_Corporations_20261125_0114.pdf
- **effective date:** with immediate effect
- **local text file name:** IFSCA-1125-03.txt

```text
    CIRCULAR



IFSCA-MIIT0IINX/1/2021-Capital Markets  November 25, 2026



To



All the recognised Stock Exchanges in the International Financial Services Centres

(IFSC)

All the recognised Clearing Corporations in the IFSC

All the recognised Depositories in the IFSC

All Broker Dealers and Clearing Members in the IFSC



Madam/Sir



Sub: Amendment to the “Master Circular for recognised Stock Exchanges and

recognised Clearing Corporations”



Reference may be drawn to the Circular dated June 05, 2026, titled “Master Circular for

recognised Stock Exchanges and recognised Clearing Corporations” (hereinafter referred

to as the “Master Circular”) issued under International Financial Services Centres

Authority (Market Infrastructure Institutions) Regulations, 2021 (the “MII Regulations”).



2. The Authority has received representations from stakeholders highlighting that

    providing additional time period to market makers to fulfil their delivery obligations

    would encourage greater participation by market makers in the secondary market and

    incentivise them to increase their quoting activities, thereby enhancing liquidity in the

    order book.



3. Based on the representations received and consultations held with stakeholders, the

    Authority has decided to amend the Master Circular to permit market makers for

    specified products to fulfil their delivery obligations within an additional period of up

    to two working days after expiry of the applicable settlement cycle, subject to such

    conditions as may be specified.



                                        Page 1 of 2

4. To operationalize the aforementioned, the Authority hereby amends the Master

    Circular, as under:



         a) under clause 27.1.1 of Chapter - IV of the Master Circular, the following

             proviso shall be added, namely: -



             “Provided that in case of specified products, market maker(s) may fulfil their

             delivery obligations within an additional period of up to two working days after

             the expiry of the applicable settlement cycle, subject to such conditions as may

             be specified.

             Explanation.- For the purpose of this proviso, the term ‘specified’ means

             specified by the recognised Clearing Corporation in consultation with the

             Authority.”



5. This Circular is being issued in exercise of powers conferred by Sections 12 and 13 of

    the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019, read with regulation

    72 of the MII Regulations and regulation 45 of the IFSCA (Capital Market

    Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025, and shall come into force with immediate effect.



A copy of this Circular is available on the website of International Financial Services

Centres Authority at www.ifsca.gov.in at “Legal Framework → Circulars”.



                                                                                       Yours faithfully



                                                                                                       Sd/-



                                                                                        Amit Prajapati

                                                                                     General Manager

                                                                   Department of Capital Markets

                                                                        prajapati.amit@ifsca.gov.in
```

```text
                                               Press Release



 Advisory to Regulated Entities to Take Note of IOSCO's Statement on Rising Fraud

               Targeting Retail Investor Accounts at Market Intermediaries



         The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO), vide its press

release dated November 16, 2026, titled – “IOSCO’s Statement on Rising Fraud

Targeting Retail Investor Accounts at Market Intermediaries”, issued a warning that

fraudulent schemes targeting retail investor accounts held at market intermediaries are

on the rise and becoming more sophisticated. The Statement, inter alia, highlights that:



        a) Fraudulent actors are increasingly leveraging artificial intelligence (AI), social

             engineering, and digital channels to reach more investors, across more

             jurisdictions, and with greater impact than before.



        b) Common schemes to recognize include impersonation of trusted individuals or

             organizations, including regulators, account takeover and identity theft. Such

             schemes have the potential to harm investors, weaken market integrity, and

             diminish investor confidence in financial markets.



2. The Statement details areas contributing to the rise in this type of fraud. New

technologies, including AI, are amplifying existing fraud, and facilitating it at a greater,

industrialized scale. Digital finance lowers barriers to execution, speeding up the scam

process, and victims are increasingly deceived into authorizing the transactions

themselves.



3. The Statement shares lessons learned and practical steps that can help reduce

investor harm, both through enhanced resilience for market intermediaries and through

investor awareness. As contemporary fraud schemes frequently span multiple products

and jurisdictions, timely information exchange and coordinated responses are essential,

with complementary roles for regulators and market intermediaries.



4. In this regard, IFSCA Regulated Entities are advised to take note of the IOSCO’s

Statement. The Regulated Entities are encouraged to remain vigilant and periodically

review the adequacy and effectiveness of their existing systems and controls to address

evolving fraud risks.



Gandhinagar,

November 16, 2026
```

```text
INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL SERVICES

             CENTRES AUTHORITY



   REPORT OF WORKING GROUP



    Developing a Framework for Issuance of Insurance-Linked

    Securities (ILS) from GIFT-IFSC

                      CHAPTER I SUBMISSION OF REPORT



Working Group on developing a framework for issuance of Insurance-Linked Securities

                                           (ILS) from GIFT-IFSC



                                                              19th October, 2026



Shri K. Rajaraman, Chairperson

International Financial Services Centre Authority (IFSCA)

GIFT City, Gandhinagar



Dear Sir,



We, the members of Working Group (WG), constituted by the IFSCA in October 2025, are

pleased to submit this Report in accordance with the mandate entrusted to us.



The increasing frequency and severity of catastrophic events, driven by climate change, rapid

urbanisation and growing concentrations of economic assets, have significantly heightened

the demand for innovative catastrophe risk financing solutions. In response, the global market

for ILS, particularly Catastrophe Bonds (CAT Bonds), has witnessed substantial growth over

the past two decades. The broader ILS market reached roughly $120 billion at year-end 2025,

up from $107 billion in 2024, per a joint AM Best and Guy Carpenter estimate. That growth

has continued into 2026: the outstanding cat bond market hit a record $65.6 billion by the end

of Q2 2026, up 7% from year-end 2025, even after $9.6 billion of maturities that quarter.1



India presents a compelling case for the development of an ILS market. As one of the world's

most disaster-prone countries, India faces recurrent exposure to cyclones, floods,

earthquakes, droughts and other natural catastrophes. At the same time, the country's

insurance sector is expanding rapidly, accompanied by increasing policy emphasis on climate

resilience, disaster risk financing and financial innovation. These developments present a

timely opportunity to explore the role of capital markets in complementing traditional insurance

and reinsurance capacity.

                                             ACKNOWLEDGMENTS



ILS2 have emerged as important instruments for strengthening the resilience of insurance

markets by enabling the transfer of catastrophe risks to global capital markets. Recognising

the potential of these instruments and the need to establish an internationally aligned

regulatory framework within GIFT IFSC, the IFSCA constituted a WG in October 2025 to

examine the legal and regulatory aspects of introducing an enabling framework for ILS in

IFSC.



The WG places on record its sincere gratitude to Shri K. Rajaraman, Chairperson, IFSCA, for

reposing confidence in the Group and entrusting it with this important assignment. IFSCAs

vision for developing GIFT IFSC as a globally competitive international financial centre,

coupled with constant encouragement, invaluable guidance and unwavering support, served

as a source of inspiration throughout the deliberations of the WG.



The WG also gratefully acknowledges the continuous support extended by the Authority and

its officers during the course of this exercise. Their valuable inputs, constructive discussions

and administrative assistance greatly facilitated the timely completion of the Group's work.



The WG benefited immensely from the collective expertise and rich experience of its

members who brought together diverse perspectives from insurance regulation, reinsurance,

capital markets, catastrophe risk financing and structured finance.



Finally, the WG expresses its appreciation to all those who, directly or indirectly, contributed

to the preparation of this Report. It is our sincere hope that the recommendations contained

herein will assist the IFSCA in establishing a robust and internationally competitive framework

for ILS, thereby contributing to the continued growth of GIFT IFSC as a global centre for

innovative risk financing and strengthening India's catastrophe risk financing ecosystem.

                                                                                                          Chairperson
```
