```text
National Stock Exchange of India Limited

Circular



                            DEPARTMENT: INSPECTION



Download Ref No: NSE/INSP/77487  Date: November 18, 2026



Circular Ref. No: 57/2026



To All Members,



Subject: Reminder for Submission of VAPT Action Taken Report for the FY 2025-26



This is with reference to Exchange circular reference no. NSE/INSP/74185 dated May 14, 2026, on

‘Submission of VAPT Report for the FY 2025-26’.



As mentioned in the above circular, in case of any “Open Vulnerabilities” have been identified and

reported by the CERT-In empanelled auditor in the VAPT Report for FY 2025-26, the trading members

are required to submit the Action Taken Report (ATR), to the Exchange through the Member Portal on or

before November 30, 2026. The submission of VAPT Action Taken Report shall be considered complete

only upon submission of the digitally signed action taken report by the auditor to the Exchange.



The guidelines for submitting the VAPT Action Taken Report (ATR)/ Compliance Report on Member portal

is enclosed for reference as Annexure – A. The due date of submission of Action Taken report

(ATR)/Compliance Report is November 30, 2026.



Trading members are requested to take note of penalty/disciplinary action applicable for delayed/non-

submission and non-closure of vulnerabilities within prescribed timelines, as prescribed in the Annexure

1.2 of Exchange circular no. NSE/INSP/73792 dated April 17, 2026, regarding “Ease of Doing Business -

Rationalization and Standardization of penalties levied on Trading Members”.



All Members are requested to take note of the above and ensure timely submission of VAPT Action Taken

Report (ATR)/ Compliance Report.



For and on behalf of

National Stock Exchange of India Limited



Prashant Aier

Chief Manager – Inspection



                                                                                 Page 1 of 10

In case of any clarifications, Members may contact our below offices:



Regional Office    Email Address                                       Contact No.

Ahmedabad (ARO)

Chennai (CRO)      inspectionahm@nse.co.in                             079- 49008632

Delhi (DRO)

Kolkata (KRO)      inspection_cro@nse.co.in                            044- 66309915 / 17

Mumbai (WRO)

Central Help Desk  delhi_inspection@nse.co.in                          011- 23459127 / 38 / 46



                   inspection_kolkata@nse.co.in 033- 40400412 / 459



                   compliance_wro@nse.co.in                            022-26598200 / 022-61928200



                   compliance_assistance@nse.co.in



                                                                                           Page 2 of 10

                                    Annexure – A

Guidelines for submission of VAPT audit Action Taken Report (ATR)



   I. Member Submission



Submission of Action Taken Report by Member

 1) Click on INSPECTION tab and follow the path below to submit Action Taken Report



Inspection > VAPT > Submit VAPT ATR report for VAPT Auditor Action Taken Report



 2) Upon Clicking VAPT ATR below screen will be displayed, select eligible audit period and click

on ‘Search’ button.



                                                                                                                                              Page 3 of 10

 3) Member details will be displayed with appropriate audit period, click on ‘Submit VAPT ATR 1

     Report’ button.



(Note: - If VAPT ATR 1 report is submitted then click VAPT ATR 2 and If VAPT ATR 2 report is

submitted then click VAPT ATR 3)



 4) The details for the Vulnerability Assessment report submitted at preliminary report will be

     displayed with open vulnerability. Clicking the link, following screen will appear member needs to

     fill the remark for the same in Member ATR Remark and Submit the report.



                                                                                                                                              Page 4 of 10

 5) Click on Submit report to proceed further.



 6) Click on ‘Download’ button to download PDF file of ATR.



Once file is downloaded Sign the PDF, click on choose file button to upload the signed PDF. (Please

note that, If E-Lock utility is not working in the system then members can sign the report outside the

system and upload the report to the system.)



                                                                                                                                              Page 5 of 10

7) Click on ‘Submit’ button to Submit the VAPT ATR report.



Note: -   Submission of Action Taken Report shall be considered complete only after Auditor

      1.  submits the report to the Exchange.



                                                            Page 6 of 10

II. Auditor Submission



Submission of Action Taken Report by Auditor.

 1) After clicking on VAPT-Auditor, kindly follow the path below to submit Action Taken Report



VAPT-Auditor > VAPT > Submit VAPT ATR Report



 2) upon Clicking Auditor MIS below screen will be displayed, select eligible audit period, and enter

     Auditor Membership No and Auditor Identifier used during submission of preliminary audit

     report. Click on ‘Search’ button.



                                                                                                                                              Page 7 of 10

 3) Click on ‘ATR Request Ref No’ link to proceed further with submission.



 4) On following screen, Auditor must provide Status of compliance, Auditor’s Comments and

Date.



 5) Auditors must provide High, Medium, Low for open vulnerabilities in the table with auditor

     remarks after filling in the details of an open vulnerability.



 6) Click on confirmation check box before clicking on ‘Submit ATR Details’ button.



                                                                                                                                              Page 8 of 10

 7) Following page opens after clicking on ‘Submit ATR Details’ button. Check details entered

before clicking on ‘Submit report’ button at the top.



 8) Click on ‘Download’ button to download PDF file of ATR.



Once file is downloaded Sign the PDF, click on choose file button to upload the sign PDF. (Please note

that, If E-Lock utility is not working in the system then auditors can sign the report outside the system

and upload the report to the system.)



                                                                                                                                              Page 9 of 10

 9) Click on ‘Submit’ button to Submit the VAPT ATR report.

(End of document)



                                                                                                                                            Page 10 of 10
```

## [exchanges] 2026-11-09 | Submission of Details of Websites, Mobile Applications and Social Media Handles

- **section:** exchanges
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-09
- **kind:** BSE notice (Others; segment Investment Advisers)
- **exact title:** Submission of Details of Websites, Mobile Applications and Social Media Handles
- **reference number:** BSE Notice No. 20261109-1
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.bseindia.com/markets/MarketInfo/DispNewNoticesCirculars.aspx?page=20261109-1
- **official PDF URL:** https://www.bseindia.com/downloads/UploadDocs/Notices/20261109-1/20261109-1.pdf
- **local text file name:** BSE-20261109-1.txt
- **note:** Date is the BSE Notice_Date field. Separate attachments, if any, not fetched.

```text
Notice No.            NOTICE

Notice Date

Category     20261109-1

Segment

Department   09 Nov 2026

Subject

Attachments  Others



             Investment Advisers



             Membership Compliance

             Submission of Details of Websites, Mobile Applications and Social

             Media Handles

             User_Manual_IA_Social_Media

This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. HO/(79)2026-MIRSD-PODMMC dated February 26, 2026 and

Exchange Notice Nos. 20260721-16 dated July 21, 2026, 20260602-35 dated June 02, 2026, and 20260428-48

dated April 28, 2026, regarding the disclosure of digital platforms used by Investment Advisers (IAs) for carrying

out investment advisory activities.



In accordance with the aforesaid circulars and notices, the Exchange has made available a facility on its portal

for submission and modification of details pertaining to websites, mobile applications, and social media

handles used by Investment Advisers.



All registered Investment Advisers are required to log in to the Exchange portal and access the “Digital

Platform” option available in their existing login.



    • In cases where the details have already been submitted to the Exchange, the existing information will be

         auto-populated. Investment Advisers are advised to verify the details, make modifications wherever

         required, and submit the case.



    • In cases where no information has been previously reported, the relevant fields will appear blank.

         Investment Advisers shall be required to furnish the requisite details and submit the case.



Accordingly, all registered Investment Advisers are advised to report and/or update the details of their websites,

mobile applications, and social media handles through the Exchange portal.



The websites, mobile applications, and social media handles reported to the Exchange shall be considered for

whitelisting with Meta and Google, wherever applicable. Investment Advisers are therefore advised to

ensure that all digital platforms being used for investment advisory activities are duly reported to the Exchange.



The aforesaid activity shall be completed on or before November 25, 2026.



Please note that any website, mobile application, or social media handle used for investment advisory

activities and not reported to the Exchange within the stipulated timeline may not be considered for whitelisting

and may be liable for deletion, removal, or such other action as may be applicable under the prevailing

regulatory framework.



Guidance for Submission



    1. Links should be provided only for the main landing page/profile of the respective website, mobile

         application, or social media handle and not for any individual post, reel, story, video, or other specific

         content.



    2. Investment Advisers should ensure that the correct links are provided in the corresponding fields. All

         details should be carefully verified and cross-checked before submission.



    3. Ensure that the information furnished is complete, accurate, and updated as on the date of submission.



    4. Refer to the attached User Manual for detailed instructions on the submission process.

Investment Advisers are advised to complete the submission within the prescribed timeline to ensure

regulatory compliance.



For any clarification, please contact the Exchange at 022-2272 5854 / 5680.



Neeky Subramaniam  Krishna Pandey

Manager            Deputy Manager

Membership         Membership


```

```text
Notice No.            NOTICE
```

```text
Attachments  Compliance



             General

             Client) Registration Agency (KRA) Regulations, 2011

             No Attachment

To

All Trading Members of the Exchanges

Sub: Guidelines in pursuance of amendment to SEBI KYC (Know Your Client) Registration Agency (KRA)

Regulations, 2011



This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/FATF/P/CIR/2023/0144 dated August 11, 2023, and

pursuant to Exchange Circular issued on monthly basis in respect to Guidelines in pursuance of amendment to

SEBI KYC (Know Your Client) Registration Agency (KRA) Regulations, 2011 with the latest notice no. 20261014-

35 dated October 14, 2026 on “Simplification of KYC process and rationalisation of Risk Management

Framework at KYC (Know Your Client) Registration Agencies (KRAs)” and “Guidelines in pursuance of

amendment to SEBI KYC (Know Your client) Registration Agency (KRA) Regulations, 2011”.



Members may note that, pursuant to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-1/P/CIR/2023/163 dated

October 03, 2023, on the Centralized Mechanism for Reporting the Demise of an Investor through KRAs, all SEBI-

registered Regulated Entities are required to block debit transactions in such accounts, suspend all transactions

in the respective trading accounts, and inactivate/close the UCC across all Stock Exchanges. Trading Members

are informed that demise-related data is being shared by the KRAs on a daily basis.



The Exchange provides details of PANs marked as “On Hold” and "Not Available" by KRAs, based on data

uploaded by Members.



Path: UCC → Download UCCs Having Invalid PAN (by KRA) → Download UCCs PAN Which Are Not Available (at

KRA)



Members are hereby informed to download records and take the necessary actions in accordance with SEBI

Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/SECFATF/P/CIR/2023/169 dated October 12, 2023.

Further to the above referred circulars, Trading Members are hereby advised to ensure that the KYCs of all the

clients are uploaded to the KRAs and only those clients shall be permitted to trade whose KRA status is either

“KYC Registered” or “KYC Validated”.



It is hereby informed that the clients whose KYC are not found to be validated by KRAs, i.e. where the KYCs are

“On Hold” for any reasons (both AADHAAR and Non-AADHAAR based OVD) uploaded to the KRA from October

01, 2026 to October 31, 2026, shall neither be Permitted to Trade on the Exchange, nor will they be allowed to

square off their open positions, if any, w.e.f. November 21, 2026, until they comply with the validation

requirements. Eventually, such open positions will naturally expire on the expiry date of the respective contract.



The Exchange shall flag the above non-compliant PANs, provided by the KRAs, as Not Permitted to Trade w.e.f.

November 21, 2026. All PANs that become KRA compliant subsequently, will be permitted to trade on T+1, based

on the information received from KRA by the Exchange on T Day.



The list of such non-compliant clients as mentioned above have been provided at the below mentioned location:



Path                                Name of File

EQ\TRANSACTION\Nov-2026\09-11-2026  Non_Validated_Clients_by_KRAs_Clgno_xxxx.TXT

In case of any clarifications, members may contact us on details given as under:



Contact Nos.           Email ID

022- 2272 8435/5785    ucc@bseindia.com



Abhijit Pai            Shubham Benere

Deputy Vice President  Deputy Manager

Investigation          Investigation


```

```text
National Stock Exchange of India Limited



  Circular



Department: Listing                       Date: November 09,2026

Download Ref No: NSE/CML/77360

Circular Ref. No: 2028/2026



All Members



             Exit Offer to the Dissenting Unitholders of Oriental InfraTrust (InvIT)



Oriental Tollways Private Limited (Acquirer) has approached the Exchange for usage of web-based tender offer

facility for providing exit opportunity to dissenting Unitholders of Oriental Infra Trust. The offer shall be in

accordance with Regulation 22(7) of SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations,2014 and Chapter

11 of the Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) dated July 11, 2025 along with the

Tender Offer Scheme as per Exchange circular NSE/CMTR/52776 dated June 29, 2022. The details of the live

session are as given below:



Issue Period                              Live Bidding Details

Bidding Time and Custodial confirmation            11-November-2026 to 17-November-2026

Custodial confirmation on Issue closure            9.15 a.m. to 3.30 p.m.

Live URL for Members                               9.15 a.m. to 4.00 p.m.

Security Parameters                                https://eipo.nseindia.com
```

```text
Department: INVESTOR SERVICES CELL  Date: November 09, 2026

Download Ref No: NSE/ISC/77375

Circular Ref. No: 50/2026



To All Members,



Sub: Guidelines in pursuance of amendment to SEBI KYC (Know Your Client) Registration

Agency (KRA) Regulations, 2011



This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/FATF/P/CIR/2023/0144 dated August 11,

2023, and pursuant to Exchange Circular issued on monthly basis in respect to Guidelines in pursuance of

amendment to SEBI KYC (Know Your Client) Registration Agency (KRA) Regulations, 2011 with the

latest issued on dated October 14, 2026, NSE/ISC/76893 on “Simplification of KYC process and

rationalisation of Risk Management Framework at KYC (Know Your Client) Registration Agencies

(KRAs)” and “Guidelines in pursuance of amendment to SEBI KYC (Know Your client) Registration

Agency (KRA) Regulations, 2011”.



It may be noted that as per SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-1/P/CIR/2023/0000000163 dated

October 03, 2023, on Centralized mechanism for reporting the demise of an investor through KRAs, all

SEBI-registered Trading Members are required to exercise due diligence as per above circular and block

all debit transactions in the accounts of deceased investors. Trading Members must subsequently mark the

relevant Unique Client Codes (UCCs) as "Closed" in the Exchange’s UCC database. Trading Members

are hereby informed that demise-related data is being shared by the KRAs on a daily basis.



Further, Trading Members are hereby advised to ensure that the KYCs of all the clients have been

uploaded to the KRAs and only those clients are permitted to trade whose KRA status is either “KYC

Registered” or “KYC Validated”.



Trading Members are hereby informed to take note of the below:



    1. All PANs uploaded to the KRAs till October 31, 2026, and whose Primary KYC status has been

         reported by the KRAs as “On-Hold” shall not be Permitted to Trade or square-off open positions

         if any, effective November 21, 2026.

NSE                                                      Continuation Sheet



2. Exchange provides a file of such PANs which have not been uploaded by the Members to the

    KRAs and hence the KYC status of such PANs is “Not Available” with the KRAs. The File Name:

    <TMcode>_KRA_NOT_AVAILABLE. Members are hereby informed to take necessary action.



3. Further, Exchange also provides a list of PANs, which have been marked as Demise by the KRAs.

    File name: <TMcode>_Demise_Clients_by_KRA. For those PANs which have been reported by

    the KRAs till October 31, 2026, as Demised, members are hereby required to mark the relevant

    Unique Client Codes (UCCs) as "Closed" in the Exchange’s UCC database before November 21,

    2026, post requisite due diligence.



The list of such KYC non-compliant PANs as mentioned above have been provided at the below

mentioned location:



       Link: https://enit.nseindia.com/MemberPortal/

       Path: ENIT > Log > Downloads



KRA Status     File Name

On Hold        <TM Code>_Non-Validated_Clients_by_KRA

Not Available  <TMcode>_ KRA_NOT_AVAILABLE

Demise         <TMcode>_ Demise_Clients_by_KRA.



The Exchange shall flag the above KYC non-compliant PANs (including Not Available and Demise Status),

provided by the KRAs on November 04, 2026, as Not Permitted to Trade w.e.f. November 21, 2026. Hence,

these PANs shall not be able to trade or square off open positions if any from the above referred date. All

PANs that become KRA compliant subsequently, will be permitted to trade on T+1, based on the

information received from KRA by the Exchange on T Day.
```

```text
clients



SEBI has issued Circular Ref No. HO/38/30/12(3)2026-MIRSD-POD2/I/25175/2026 dated

November 04, 2026, regarding ‘Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person

Resident Outside India clients’.



The SEBI circular is attached as Annexure A.



Trading Members are requested to take note of the same and ensure compliance.



For and on behalf of

National Stock Exchange of India Limited



Kapil Marwah

Associate Vice President

                                                                       Continuation Sheet



In case of any clarifications, Members may contact our below offices:



 Regional Office  Contact No.                      Email ID

 Ahmedabad        079-65278024/55                  inspectionahm@nse.co.in

((ARO)

 Chennai (CRO)    044- 66309915/17                 inspection_cro@nse.co.in

 Delhi (DRO)      011-23459146/ 127/144/ 147       delhi_inspection@nse.co.in

 Kolkata (KRO)    033-40400412 / 59                inspection_kolkata@nse.co.in

 Mumbai (WRO)     022-61928200                     compliance_wro@nse.co.in



Central Help Desk compliance_assistance@nse.co.in

                                            Annexure A



CIRCULAR



HO/38/30/12(3)2026-MIRSD-POD2/I/25175/2026  November 04, 2026



To,



All intermediaries registered with SEBI under Section 12 of the Securities and

Exchange Board of India Act, 1992;

Recognised Stock Exchanges;

Recognised Clearing Corporations; and

All Depositories



Dear Sir/ Madam,



Subject: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident

            Outside India clients



1. SEBI vide Master Circular SEBI/HO/MIRSD/SECFATF/P/CIR/2023/169 dated

    October 12, 2023 (‘KYC Master Circular’), inter-alia, specifies the Know Your Client

    (KYC) requirements for on-boarding client by an intermediary and a framework for

    validation of KYC records by a KYC Registration Agency (KRA)1.



2. The extant provisions of the KYC Master Circular, inter-alia, requires an

    intermediary to ensure that, during digital KYC, the physical location of the client is

    in India. This requirement in effect restricts a client outside India, at the time of on-

    boarding, to submit the KYC documents and complete the KYC process digitally.



3. In order to ease the process of on-boarding of an individual Person Resident

    Outside India (PROI)2 client, it has been decided to review the existing provisions

    governing the KYC process. Individual PROI client shall mean Non-Resident Indian

    (NRI)3, Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)4 or foreign national.



1 KYC Registration Agencies as per SEBI (Know Your Client Registration Agencies) Regulations, 2011;

2 PROI is defined under section 2(w) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, as a “person who is not resident in India”;

3 In terms of section 2(30) read with section 2(42) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, "non-resident" means a person who is not a



  "resident", and for the purposes of sections 92, 93 and 168, includes a person who is not ordinarily resident within the meaning

  of clause (6) of section 6 thererof; "resident" means a person who is resident in India within the meaning of section 6 thereof;

4 OCI cardholder is defined under section 2 (ee) of the Citizenship Act, 1955, as a person registered as an Overseas Citizen of

India Cardholder by the Central Government under section 7A thereof;

4. Upon review of the said framework, and after taking into account the

    representations from market participants, the modifications being introduced, inter-

    alia, includes the following:



    4.1. The requirement of a client being in India during digital on-boarding is being

         relaxed for an individual PROI client located in a Financial Action Task Force

         (FATF) compliant country5 and the intermediary may accept digital submission

         of KYC information and supporting documents from such client.



    4.2. KRA shall tag individual attributes in the KYC record as “validated”, if verified

         with official or source database. All KYC records shall be portable i.e. can be

         shared with another intermediary, irrespective of every individual attribute

         being validated or not.



    4.3. The intermediary may rely on the KYC undertaken by a SEBI registered

         intermediary or by an entity regulated by other financial sector regulators,

         based on record obtained from KRA or Central KYC Records Registry

         (CKYCRR).



    4.4. The authorised official of the intermediary shall be present during Video In

         Person Verification of a client and the VIPV process shall be subject to

         concurrent audit.



5. Accordingly, the on-boarding of individual PROI clients through intermediaries and

    KRAs, are being detailed below:



    5.1. The intermediary shall, at the time of commencement of an account based

          relationship, identify its client, verify the identity and obtain information on the

          purpose and intended nature of the business relationship.



    5.2. When the client approaches an intermediary to initiate an account based

          relationship or update KYC, the intermediary shall seek the PAN and CKYC

          ID6 from the client, if available. Thereafter, the intermediary shall retrieve the

          KYC records (i.e. information and documents) from KRA and CKYCRR.



    5.3. If the client record already exists, the intermediary shall obtain additional

          details from the client only when:



          5.3.1. there is a change in the existing records of the client;



5 As per details published by FATF;

6 The unique number or code assigned to a client by CKYCRR;

          5.3.2. details retrieved are incomplete or are not as per extant norms;



          5.3.3. the validity of the Officially Valid Document or deemed officially valid

                  document7 has lapsed;



          5.3.4. the intermediary considers it necessary to verify the identity or address;

                  or



          5.3.5. to perform enhanced due diligence (EDD) or to build an appropriate risk

                  profile of the client.



    5.4. The intermediary shall provide the updated KYC information of the client to

         KRA, which shall update the existing KYC record and inform all intermediaries

         that avail of the services of the KRA in respect of that client, in line with the

         provisions of the SEBI {KYC (Know Your Client) Registration Agencies)

         Regulations, 2011 (‘KRA Regulations’).



    5.5. The KYC process shall involve the following aspects:



          5.5.1. PAN:



                  a. The intermediary shall collect the PAN of the client and verify the

                      same with the Income Tax Database, without insisting on producing

                      the original PAN or providing a copy thereof.



                  b. The KRA shall also verify the PAN and the name of the client, as

                      mentioned in the KYC form, with the Income Tax Database.

                      Accordingly, the said attribute shall be tagged as “validated” in the

                      KYC record.



          5.5.2. Passport:



                  a. The intermediary shall collect a copy of the Passport from the client.



                  b. The intermediary shall also collect Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)

                      card from the client, as applicable.



                  c. The intermediary shall verify the passport of the client, if feasible.



7 OVD and deemed to be OVD, as defined under the Prevention of Money Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005

(PMLR);

                  d. KRA shall verify the passport of the client, if feasible. Accordingly, the

                      said attribute shall be tagged as “validated” in the KYC record.



          5.5.3. KYC form:



                  a. The intermediary shall collect the KYC information from the client, as

                      per CKYCRR template8 prescribed for “individuals”, in physical or

                      through app, website or digital mode.



                  b. The intermediary can collect the filled KYC form in any of the

                      following manners:



                       i. original physical form; or



                      ii. scanned copy of physical form, under electronic signature9; or



                      iii. digital KYC form, under electronic signature.



          5.5.4. Specimen signature:



                  a. The intermediary shall collect specimen signature from the client in

                      any of the following forms:



                       i. wet signature on the physical KYC form; or



                      ii. cropped image of specimen signature, under electronic signature.



                  b. In case of digital submission of specimen signature, the client shall

                      do wet signature before the intermediary during Video In Person

                      Verification (VIPV), and the intermediary in turn shall verify if the said

                      signature matches with the client’s submission.



          5.5.5. Proof of Identity and Proof of Address:



                  a. The intermediary shall collect any one of the specified officially valid

                      documents or deemed officially valid documents, for proof of identity

                      and proof of address, from the client. For this purpose, the current

                      address for an individual PROI client shall be an overseas address.



8 KYC template provided by Central Registry of Securitization Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI);

9 “electronic signature” shall have the meaning as defined under the Information Technology Act, 2000;

       b. In case the officially valid documents presented by a foreign national

            does not contain the details of address, a document issued by a

            Government department of a foreign jurisdiction and letter issued by

            a Foreign Embassy or Mission in India can be collected by the

            intermediary as proof of address.



       c. The intermediary shall verify the address mentioned in the KYC form

            with the address mentioned in the officially valid document or

            deemed officially valid document submitted by the client and with the

            official or source database, if feasible.



       d. The KRA shall also verify the address mentioned in the KYC form

            with the address mentioned in the officially valid document or

            deemed officially valid document submitted by the client and with the

            official or source database, if feasible. Accordingly, the said attributes

            shall be tagged as “validated” in the KYC record.



5.5.6. Original, Seen and Verified (OSV):



       a. The intermediary shall see and verify the original of the officially valid

            document or deemed officially valid document submitted by the

            client, for proof of identity and proof of address, and collect the

            physical self-attested copies of the same.



       b. In case the original of the officially valid document or deemed officially

            valid document is not produced for verification, then the intermediary

            shall collect any of the following:



             i. equivalent e-document of officially valid document or deemed

                 officially valid document through Digi Locker; or



            ii. equivalent e-document of officially valid document or deemed

                 officially valid document, issued by the issuing authority through

                 any verifiable mechanism; or



           iii. One Time Password (OTP) or biometric or face authentication

                 based Aadhaar e-KYC authentication; or



           iv. copy of officially valid document attested by any of the certifying

                 authorities (i.e. Notary Public, authorised official of overseas

                 branch of Scheduled Commercial Banks registered in India,

                 branches of overseas banks with whom Indian banks have

                 relationships, Court Magistrate, Judge, Indian Embassy or

                 Consulate General of the country where the client resides).



       c. The intermediary shall ensure that the details of the authorised official

            undertaking the OSV and the date and time stamp are recorded at

            the time of OSV.



       d. The intermediary shall ensure that the copy of the certified OVD

            provided by the client contains the date, location, name and license

            number/ employee code, if any, of the certifying authority.



5.5.7. Mobile number and email id:



       a. The intermediary shall collect the mobile number (Indian or

            international) and the email id of the client. The mobile number and

            email id recorded in Aadhaar may be preferred.



       b. The intermediary shall verify the mobile number, if feasible, and the

            email id of the client through OTP or any other verifiable mechanism.



       c. If the mobile number of the client cannot be verified, then the

            intermediary shall ensure that all communications are sent on the

            verified email id of such client.



       d. The KRA shall also verify the mobile number, if feasible, and the

            email id of the client through OTP or any other verifiable mechanism.

            Accordingly, the said attributes shall be tagged as “validated” in the

            KYC record.



5.5.8. In-Person Verification (IPV):



       a. The intermediary shall carry out IPV of the client and ensure that the

            details of the authorised official undertaking the IPV and the date and

            time stamp are recorded at the time of IPV.



       b. In case the physical IPV is not feasible, the intermediary shall

            undertake VIPV of the client, while ensuring the following:



             i. the client consent is recorded in an auditable and alteration proof

                 manner;

                  ii. the VIPV infrastructure has features of random action initiation for

                      client response to establish that the interactions are not pre-

                      recorded;



                 iii. the uninterrupted video recording contains the live GPS co-

                      ordinates (geo-tagging) of the client and the date and time stamp

                      through use of tamper proof technology;



                 iv. the VIPV infrastructure prevents connection from spoofed IP

                      addresses, using VPNs or proxy servers;



                  v. the IP address of the client, as captured, emanates from India or

                      from any of the FATF compliant country and matches with the

                      country specified by the client in the KYC form and officially valid

                      document or deemed officially valid document;



                 vi. the photo of the client is clearly captured in the VIPV process and

                      matches with the photo submitted by the client in the form and

                      officially valid document or deemed officially valid document;



                vii. there is end to end encryption of data between customer device

                      and the hosting point of application/ digital platform at the

                      intermediary;



                viii. the authorised official of the intermediary is present during the

                      VIPV process;



                 ix. the VIPV infrastructure uses components which verify face

                      liveness and detect spoofs, if any; such liveliness check does not

                      result in exclusion of person with special needs; and



                  x. the VIPV process is subject to concurrent audit, to ensure the

                      integrity of process and its acceptability of the outcome.



             c. The intermediary may incorporate additional safety and security

                  features in the VIPV process, as per its risk management policy.



5.6. Reliance of third party KYC:



     5.6.1. The intermediary may rely on the KYC undertaken by another SEBI

             registered intermediary, as per record obtained from the KRA. The KYC

             record shared by KRA with intermediary shall have each attribute wise

             tagging for whether it is “validated” or not.

          5.6.2. The intermediary may also rely on the KYC undertaken by an entity

                  regulated by any of the other Financial Sector Regulators10, as per record

                  obtained from the CKYCRR.



          5.6.3. The intermediary shall have the ultimate responsibility for the KYC of its

                  clients, including undertaking enhanced due diligence appropriate to the

                  risk profile of the clients.



    5.7. Upon completion of the KYC of individual PROI client, the intermediary shall

          provide the KYC information to KRA within 3 working days from the date of

          completion of KYC process.



    5.8. The intermediary shall ensure that the infrastructure being used for the KYC

          process is in compliance with the Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience

          Framework issued by SEBI.



    5.9. All documents submitted by an individual PROI client to the intermediary

          should be in English. In case the document is in any other language, then the

          client shall get the document translated to English and attested by a certifying

          authority, before submission to the intermediary.



  5.10.The aforementioned process shall also be applicable for re-KYC of the client in

         a FATF compliant country.



6. In cases where an individual foreign national seeks registration as a Foreign

    Portfolio Investor (FPI), the provisions of Master Circular for Foreign Portfolio

    Investors, Designated Depository Participants and Eligible Foreign Investors ref.

    no. SEBI/HO/AFD/AFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/70 dated May 30, 2024 or

    amendments thereof, shall be applicable.



7. The provisions of this circular shall come into effect, for on-boarding of every

    individual PROI client except client in a FATF non-compliant country, thirty (30)

    days from the date of issue of this circular i.e. from December 03, 2026.



8. Upon this circular coming into effect, the following shall also be effected:



    8.1. the provisions of the KYC Master Circular shall stand superseded, to such

          extent;



10 Financial Sector Regulator includes the Reserve Bank of India, Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India,

Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority and International Financial Services Centres Authority;

    8.2. the provisions of the circular ref. no. CIR/MIRSD/16/2011 dated August 22,

         2011, regarding, “Simplification and Rationalization of Trading Account

         Opening Process”, shall stand superseded, to such extent;



    8.3. the provisions of the circular ref. no. HO/38/30/12(1)2025-MIRSD-SEC-FATF

          dated December 10, 2025, regarding, “Relaxation on geo tagging requirement

          in India for NRIs while undertaking re KYC”, shall stand superseded;



    8.4. for clients residing in FATF non-compliant countries, the extant KYC process

          shall continue to be applicable; and



    8.5. for KYC undertaken by intermediaries prior to the date of this circular coming

          into effect, shall continue to be governed by the extant KYC provisions.



9. This circular is being issued in exercise of powers conferred under Section 11(1)

    of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, to protect the interests of

    investors in securities and to promote the development of, and to regulate the

    securities market.



10. This circular is available on the SEBI website at www.sebi.gov.in, under the

    category, ‘Legal → Circulars’.



                                                                                             Yours faithfully,



                                                                                         Divya Hamirbasia

                                                                               Deputy General Manager
```

```text
In continuation to the notice no. 20201001-2, dated 01st Oct 2020, Settlement Cycle for non-settlement

related payments between Custodians and Trading Members has been revised.



Revised Process for Non-Settlement Related Payments



• Custodians shall provide the non-settlement related payment file in the prescribed format

    (Annexure I) on T+1 (settlement) day by 4:00 PM.



• Based on the details provided by the Custodians, the Clearing Corporation shall debit the

    Custodian's clearing bank account and credit the corresponding amount to the Clearing

    Member's (linked to the Trading Member) clearing bank account on the same day.



• A report containing details of such payments shall be made available to Trading Members. The

    report format is provided in Annexure II.
```

```text
In line with the migration of the settlement cycle from T+2 to T+1, the process for non-settlement related payments is revised as detailed

below:



1. Custodians shall upload a file with the details as provided in Annexure I by 4:00 PM on the settlement day.

2. NCL shall initiate the respective debit of amount from the Custodian clearing bank account and credit the amount into the Clearing



     Member’s (linked to the Trading Member) clearing bank account on the same day.

3. NCL shall generate and download a report to the Trading Members containing the details of the non-settlement related payments



     from the Custodians. The report format is provided in Annexure II.



The payments made under the aforementioned payment facility shall not be commingled with the settlement obligations of the

Custodians/Members and will not be guaranteed by NCL. The payments to Trading Members shall be made subject to realization from

Custodians. NCL shall not have any responsibility whatsoever in respect of these payments or any disputes related thereto.



The revised process shall be operational with effect from 16th November 2026(i.e. T+1 settlement cycle for trade date 13th November

2026).
```

```text
National Stock Exchange of India Limited

Circular



Department: INVESTIGATION DEPARTMENT      Date: November 02, 2026

Circular Ref. No: 111/2026



All Market Participants,



Sub: Revision in formats for registration of Non-Neat Frontend (NNF) software documents and other important

updates.



This is with reference to Exchange consolidated circular number NSE/INVG/73992 dated April 30, 2026, wherein

operational guidelines were specified for Trading members/Empanelled Vendors/ Application Service Providers

(ASPs) and Algo Providers seeking registration of their Non-Neat Front End (NNF) software. The Exchange, vide

circular no. NSE/INVG/74233 dated May 15, 2026, had revised the documents/formats required for registration of

NNF registration.



The Current circular modifies/adds to specified sections of the earlier circulars as mentioned above, specifically to

sections 2, 12, 13 & 15 of Exchange circular number 73992 and 74233 dated April 30, 2026, and May 15, 2026, to

the extent of documents and formats required for NNF software registration.



Accordingly, market participants are requested to note the following:



     1. Minimum participation period for Mock/Simulation Trading:



          As per clause 5.1.2.2.2, Chapter 2 of SEBI Master circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing corporations

          dated December 30, 2024, Trading members are required to participate in mock / simulated trading

          environment provided by the Exchange. Such participation shall now be for a minimum period of one hour

          and the auditor shall verify whether the Trading Members have participated for such minimum period of 1

          hour and specify the time duration of participation in the auditor certificate submitted for registration of NNF

          new / modified software.



     2. Registration for Electronic Gold Receipts (EGR):



          As per Exchange Circular No. NSE/INVG/74233 dated May 15, 2026, members can apply for registration of

          NNF products in the EGR segment. This provision has now been extended to include ‘Algorithmic Trading’

          (AT) and ‘Client Direct API’ products.



     3. Minimum Net Worth Criteria:



          A minimum net worth threshold of INR 1 crore shall now apply to CTCL vendors and Application service

          provider (ASPs). In view of this requirement, all such vendors shall furnish a ‘Net worth certificate’ in the

          specified format. While the prospective vendors shall submit the ‘Net worth certificate’ with their

National Stock Exchange of India Limited



           empanelment application, the existing empanelled vendors shall furnish it by November 15, 2026. The

           format of the ‘Net worth certificate’ has been provided in Annexure 14.



      4. Vendor confirmation letter - CSCRF:



           In accordance with SEBI circular SEBI/HO/ ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113 dated 20 August 2024,

           on the Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF), and Exchange circular no. NSE/INVG/76131

           dated September 02, 2026, all Trading Members shall submit a ‘Vendor confirmation letter - CSCRF’ at the

           time of NNF product registration with the Exchange. This letter shall confirm that the minimum software /

           hardware requirements including the baseline requirements and security patch levels have been met as per

           the specifications provided by the empanelled vendor. The format of the ‘Vendor confirmation letter - CSCRF’

           has been provided in Annexure 15.



      5. Update to Algo Provider Empanelment Undertaking:
```

## [other-laws] 2026-11-26 | Public Sector Banks (PSBs) grow stronger with prudent banking practices and strong underwriting capabilities

- **section:** other-laws
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-26
- **kind:** PIB press release
- **exact title:** Public Sector Banks (PSBs) grow stronger with prudent banking practices and strong underwriting capabilities
- **reference number:** PRID 2342160
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2342160
- **local text file name:** PIB-2342160.txt
- **note:** Issuing ministry as shown on PIB: Ministry of Finance

```text
Ministry of Finance

 Public Sector Banks (PSBs) grow stronger with prudent banking practices and strong underwriting capabilities

PSB asset quality at all-time high with historically low stressed assets

PSBs’ gross advances reach ₹127 lakh crore with 18.8% y-o-y growth

Retail, agriculture and MSME advances grow at 17.0%, 19.5% and 20.4%, respectively

Total deposits grow to ₹165.2 lakh crore at 12.9% y-o-y

Net NPA ratio at 0.33%; Gross NPAs fall to ₹44,100 crore

 Posted On:
 26 NOV 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

 The Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue to grow rapidly with high asset quality, ably supported by reform enabled prudent credit underwriting and effective risk management policies. The systemic reforms instituted in PSBs are showing fruitful results in the form of high quality rapidly paced credit growth across sectors, especially productive credit growth. Credit delivery to MSMEs and corporates by PSBs has also shown remarkable improvement with both growing at fast pace along with Agriculture and Retail. At the same time, the asset quality continues to improve to all-time best, supported by low slippages and strong recoveries in impaired assets. The institutionalisation of reforms has created a strong system of governance led banking in PSBs, supporting economic upcycle.

PSBs’ advances are growing rapidly at 15.1% in last 5-years and reached ₹127 lakh crore as on 30.9.2026. However, at the same time PSBs are also showing signs of strong prudence in credit underwriting through rapidly declining slippages. As against advances of ₹67.7 lakh crore as on 31.3.2021, the slippages were as high as ₹1.44 lakh crore at a rate of 2.35% in FY2021-22. It has now come down to just ₹38,780 crore against advances of ₹127 lakh crore in H1FY2026-27, recording slippage ratio of just 0.62%, a remarkable sign of growth with prudence. 

The credit growth is not only prudent in terms of asset quality, but also is well diversified and focused across sectors. PSBs are extending credit to productive and consumptive sectors simultaneously with high credit growth in Retail, Agriculture, MSME and corporate sectors evenly balanced. While credit to retail and agriculture continues at strong rate over past more than 5-years, credit to MSME and corporates have also picked up to outpace other sectors marginally.

Looking at bank-wise performance in terms of credit growth, almost all banks are evenly extending credit with Bank of Maharashtra outpacing others, while large banks such as, State Bank of India, Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and Punjab National Bank are also growing rapidly.

Even with high credit growth, continued improvement in slippages ratio is observed across banks with only Punjab & Sind Bank recording marginal decline in slippage ratio, though already having low slippage ratio of 0.57%. Amongst large banks, State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank and Canara Bank continues to have low slippages. All PSBs now have slippage ratio of less than 1%.

The lower slippages have helped banks in maintaining low NPA levels, though aided by sufficient provisioning and strong recovery also. As a result of combined efforts in prudent underwriting and efficient collections, PSBs are maintaining significantly low net NPAs of 0.33%, amounting Rs. 44,100 crore only, in advances of more than Rs. 127 lakh crore. PSBs continue to have significantly low stress in the form of SMAs also, with aggregate advances of only ₹18,800 crore falling in SMA 1 and 2 amongst advances above ₹5 crore. PSBs continue to improve in SMA levels also with ratio of SMA 1 & 2 advances of above ₹5 crore to total standard advances being only 0.14% as on 30.9.2026, as against 0.24% as on 30.9.2025.

Prudent credit underwriting and efficient risk management practices are paving way for a stronger and robust banking sector having capability to support credit needs of the economy for long term.

***

KT/KMN/SS

 (Release ID: 2342160)
 Visitor Counter : 764
```

```text
Ministry of Finance

 High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat initiates stakeholder consultations

 Posted On:
 18 NOV 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

 The High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat constituted by the Government of India, in its first two sittings discussed the key areas for examination under its Terms of Reference. It also identified stakeholder groups for consultation, including banks, non-banking financial companies, development financial institutions, regulators, industry associations, fintech organisations and others.

To ensure a structured consultative process, the Committee has circulated questionnaires to stakeholder groups, inviting their views and suggestions on key areas of banking sector reforms.

Going forward, the Committee will hold consultation meetings with key stakeholders to gather further inputs for its recommendations on Banking for Viksit Bharat 2047.

These consultations will help the Committee frame recommendations to strengthen the Indian banking sector and make it competitive, resilient, inclusive and future-ready.
```

## [other-laws] 2026-11-18 | Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue strong financial performance in first half of FY2026-27

- **section:** other-laws
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-18
- **kind:** PIB press release
- **exact title:** Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue strong financial performance in first half of FY2026-27
- **reference number:** PRID 2337946
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2337946
- **local text file name:** PIB-2337946.txt
- **note:** Issuing ministry as shown on PIB: Ministry of Finance

```text
Ministry of Finance

 Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue strong financial performance in first half of FY2026-27

PSBs’ profitability soars to highest ever with aggregate net profit of Rs. 1,09,540 crore, growing by 16.9% y-o-y

Total PSBs business crosses Rs. 300 lakh crore; with y-o-y growth at 15.5%

Gross advances of PSBs grew to ₹127 lakh crore, registering a robust growth of 18.8% evenly panned across retail, agriculture and MSME segments

PSBs record historic low stressed assets, with gross NPA ratio declining to 1.69% and net NPA ratio to 0.33% as on 30.09.2026

Systemic reforms, improved governance and Government’s commitment of healthy PSBs manifest through improved financial performance of PSBs in profitability, business growth, asset quality and capital position

 Posted On:
 18 NOV 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

 The sustained improvement in financial health across different financial parameters, including, inter alia, capital adequacy, business growth, low slippages, healthy asset quality and outstandingly improved profitability, establishes the complete turnaround in overall functioning of Public Sector Banks (PSBs). It shows that PSBs are not only making profit but also meeting the requirements of credit supply need with improved underwriting capabilities, aided by technology and higher governance standards.

PSBs’ aggregate net profit reached ₹1.10 lakh crore with 16.9% y-o-y growth and aggregate operating profit reached ₹1.81 lakh crore with 13.9% y-o-y growth. Return on assets of PSBs continue to improve, reaching 1.11% with y-o-y improvement of 3bps. The continued improvement in profitability in both net and operating profit for the fifth consecutive year shows fruitful outcome of enablement of deeply engaged reforms drive and establishment of better governance standards by the Government.

Aggregate business of PSBs grew by 15.5% y-o-y to ₹301.6 lakh crore as on 30.9.2026, crossing the ₹300 lakh crore business mark for the first time. While aggregate deposits grew by 13.1% y-o-y to reach ₹275 lakh crore, the aggregate advances grew at 18.8% y-o-y to reach ₹136.4 lakh crore. The robust credit growth having evenly panned out across different segments, i.e. Retail, Agriculture, MSME, shows PSBs’ continued support to grassroot economic development, inculcation of entrepreneurship and deepening financial inclusion. Credit growth for retail, agriculture and MSME loans was recorded at 17%, 19.5%, 20.4%, respectively.

PSBs’ asset quality remains in continual improvement, recording another long-time low, with Gross NPA ratio declining to 1.69% and Net NPA ratio declining to 0.33%. Low levels of NPAs are aided by better underwriting standards visible through low slippages of 0.62% and continually focused collections efforts visible through improved recoveries and upgradations of 21.1%. All PSBs are now having provisioning coverage ratio of above 90%, reflecting prudent banking practices and resilient financial performance.

Capital buffers of PSBs remain well above regulatory minimum benchmark through higher retained earnings and strong capital raising, showing availability of adequate cushion to support credit growth while also having capability to absorb systemic shocks. CRAR of PSBs was at 16.89% as on 30.9.2026, improved by 93bps y-o-y. The improvement was also aided by decline in RWA density by 94bps y-o-y to 47.9%.

Cost to income ratio of PSBs also improved by 191 bps y-o-y to 47.38% for H1FY2026-27, aided by decline in cost per asset to 1.60% by 14bps y-o-y. The improved operational efficiency shows gains of investment in technologies and digital transformation, a reflection of efficient cost management.

Performance of PSBs is true reflection of outcomes of institutionalisation of reforms by the Government in PSBs, primarily aimed at better governance standards, improved operational efficiency, prudency in banking practices, enhanced risk management and continual adaptability of technology. The steps taken by the Government in improving operational standards of PSBs is now being reflected in the financial performance, aimed supporting India’s growth aspirations of Viksit Bharat 2047.

***

KT/KMN

 (Release ID: 2337946)
 Visitor Counter : 2502
```

## [other-laws] 2026-11-11 | Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units

- **section:** other-laws
- **date (YYYY-MM-DD):** 2026-11-11
- **kind:** PIB press release
- **exact title:** Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units
- **reference number:** PRID 2334977
- **official URL (detail page):** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2334977
- **local text file name:** PIB-2334977.txt
- **note:** Issuing ministry as shown on PIB: Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units

```text
Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units 

Provides credit guarantee for loans extended under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana 

Approval for corpus of Rs.5,000 crore facilitating PMMY loans amounting to Rs.12.6 lakh crore

 Posted On:
 11 NOV 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi

 The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved thecontinuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) for a period of five years upto 31.03.2031. The scheme provides credit guarantee coverage to the Lending Institutions through National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) against default risk. 

As on September 2026, more than 60.36 crore loans amounting to Rs.43.34 lakhs crore have been sanctioned by lending institutions since launch of PM Mudra Scheme. CGFMU which was launched in January 2016 has acted as a major catalyst in enabling the growth of PMMY loans in the country.

Salient features of the Scheme:

 The purpose of the fund is to provide guarantee to Lending Institutions (LIs) for the following credit facilities:

 Loans extended to eligible micro enterprises under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) upto Rs.20 lakh;

 Overdraft of upto Rs.10,000 provided by banks under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts; and

 Loans granted to Self Help Group (SHG) where portfolio is between Rs.10 lakh to Rs.20 lakh.

 Guarantee coverage: Linked to the disbursement amount in case of working capital limits and outstanding amount for term loan accounts to reflect the actual risk exposure of LIs.

 Guarantee Fee: Decrease in guarantee fee from @1% p.a. to @ 0.75% p.a. No change for SHG; continue to pay guarantee fee of 0.25% for the first year and 0.50% in subsequent years.

 Duration of the Scheme: The Scheme would be applicable to all loans extended under PMMY during the XVIth Finance Commission Cycle i.e. FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.

Impact:

 Collateral free loans under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana has created a whole new generation of entrepreneurs who previously could not avail loans from formal banking system. 

 The extension of CGFMU scheme will enable loans of Rs.12.6 lakh crore over next 5 years

 The scheme will act as a catalyst to young aspiring entrepreneurs to set up and grow their business.

****

MJPS

 (Release ID: 2334977)
 Visitor Counter : 1085
```

```text
Cabinet approves Continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme 

To promote entrepreneurship among Women, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes

Targets to cover minimum 2.5 lakh beneficiaries

Approval for Credit Guarantee Corpus of Rs.4,111 crore

 Posted On:
 11 NOV 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi

 The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved thecontinuation of Stand-Up India Scheme for a period of 5 years upto 31.03.2031. The scheme aims to promote entrepreneurship among Women, Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) and aims to provide financial assistance to additional 2.5 lakh entrepreneurs in a span of five years. Since its launch in April 2016, the scheme has facilitated loans to more than 2.75 lakh Women/SC/ST entrepreneurs.

Salient features of the scheme:

 Eligible borrowers: Women, SC and ST entrepreneurs for setting up new/green field enterprises

 Quantum of Support: The loan can be in the form of either Composite (Working Capital and Term Loan) or Term loan for amounts above Rs.10.00 lakh and upto Rs.1.00 crore (upto 85% of the project cost). 

 Eligible Sectors: Manufacturing, Services, Trading and Agri allied activities.

 Credit Guarantee coverage: 85% of the loan amount 

 Guarantee Fee: Standard guarantee fee of 0.50 %

Impact:

 Credit access for women, SC and ST entrepreneurs, enabling enterprise creation and strengthening entrepreneurship across underserved communities, thereby supporting inclusive economic growth.
```

```text
             AI Security Auditing Guidelines



1. Preamble



Artificial Intelligence has evolved from a specialised technology into an important component of

digital services, business processes, public administration and critical infrastructure. AI systems

are increasingly being used in banking & financial services, healthcare, telecommunications,

education, transportation, manufacturing, law enforcement, defence, citizen-service delivery and

other sectors to generate predictions, recommendations, decisions and content, and in certain

cases to autonomously initiate actions in physical or digital environments.



While AI offers significant opportunities for innovation, efficiency and improved service delivery,

its adoption also introduces risks that are not fully addressed through conventional information

technology and cybersecurity assurance mechanisms. Such risks include manipulation of training

data and models, adversarial attacks, unauthorised model access, leakage of sensitive

information, algorithmic bias, lack of explainability, model and data drift, insecure third-party

dependencies, misuse of generative and agentic AI, deepfakes, hallucinated outputs and

inadequate human oversight. These risks may affect the confidentiality, integrity, availability,

safety, fairness, reliability and accountability of AI-enabled systems.



The Artificial Intelligence Security Auditing Guidelines have been developed by Sub-group 03 of

the Working Group on “Indian Standards for Cybersecurity Auditing” constituted by the Indian

Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In). The Guidelines establish a common, risk-

based and lifecycle-oriented framework for assessing the governance, security, privacy, fairness,

transparency, resilience and auditability of AI systems. They are intended to facilitate consistent

security auditing practices across sectors while supporting responsible innovation, indigenous

capability development and alignment with applicable Indian legal, regulatory and policy

requirements and internationally recognised AI governance and cybersecurity standards.



The Guidelines recognise that AI governance cannot be addressed solely through ethical

principles or conventional cybersecurity controls. Effective assurance requires organisational

accountability, technical testing, data and model governance, continuous monitoring, human

oversight, incident response and third-party assurance. Accordingly, the framework provides

auditable requirements proportionate to the nature, scale, autonomy and potential impact of each

AI system.



CERT-In has also taken initiatives to strengthen coordinated cybersecurity monitoring, threat

assessment, technical analysis through the establishment of a dedicated AI cyber defence War

Room bringing together relevant technical capabilities for coordinated assessment and response.

The framework further draws upon the operational experience and institutional capabilities

developed through such initiatives, providing a practical foundation for strengthening the

implementation of risk-based AI security auditing and continuous assurance practices.



             Page 3 of 107

                      AI Security Auditing Guidelines



2. Executive Summary



The Artificial Intelligence Security Auditing Guidelines provide a structured framework for

conducting security and governance audits of AI systems developed, procured, deployed or

operated by organisations in India, as well as AI systems processing Indian data or providing AI-

enabled services to Indian users.



The framework adopts a risk-based approach under which AI systems are classified into four risk

tiers—Low, Moderate, High and Critical based on factors such as impact severity, autonomy of

decision-making, data sensitivity, scale and exposure, transparency, Explainable AI (XAI),

incident response readiness, reversibility and recoverability, operational/sector criticality,

adversarial exposure and complexity/auditability. The assigned risk tier determines the depth,

frequency and independence of the audit, the extent of documentation required, the level of

human oversight and the applicable monitoring, reporting and assurance requirements.



The Guidelines establish nine core audit domains:



   i. AI Governance and Accountability



  ii. Data Lifecycle, Quality and Privacy



  iii. Model Risk Management



 iv. AI Ethics, Bias and Fairness



  v. Explainability and Transparency



 vi. Security, Adversarial Resilience and Incident Reporting



 vii. Continuous Monitoring, Drift Management and Validation



viii. Human Oversight and Decision Accountability



 ix. Third-Party and AI Supply-Chain Assurance



These domains collectively cover the entire AI lifecycle, including design, procurement, data

collection, model development, training, validation, deployment, operation, retraining, monitoring

and decommissioning. The framework supplements these domains with dedicated requirements

for advanced AI architectures, including Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG),

Agentic AI, Multimodal AI, Multi-Agent AI and Autonomous/Cyber-Physical AI. These

requirements address prompt injection, sensitive-information disclosure, excessive agency, data

and model poisoning, supply-chain risks, vector and embedding weaknesses, unsafe tool use,

persistent-memory risks, inter-agent communication, multimodal attacks, misinformation and

improper output handling.



The Guidelines also prescribe a structured audit methodology covering engagement initiation,

risk assessment, scoping, audit planning, evidence collection, technical testing, finding



                                                                                                                    Page 4 of 107

                                                                                                                                 AI Security Auditing Guidelines



classification, reporting, remediation and follow-up verification. Audit findings are classified as

Critical, High, Moderate or Low/Observation, with corresponding containment, remediation,

escalation and reporting requirements. A five-level maturity model enables organisations to

assess their current AI governance capability and plan progressive improvement from ad hoc

practices to measured and continuously optimised governance.



AI-assisted audit procedures may support evidence analysis, control mapping, technical testing

and report preparation. Their use is subject to approved scope, confidentiality controls, tool

validation, traceable evidence and competent human review. AI-generated outputs shall not

replace sufficient and appropriate evidence or the auditor’s independent judgement.



The framework is aligned with recognised standards and frameworks, including CERT-In’s

Blueprint for Reducing Exposure and Defending against AI-Assisted Vulnerabilities Exploitation

in Digital Infrastructure, India AI Governance Guidelines by MeitY, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC

23894, ISO/IEC 27001, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS and OWASP guidance for machine learning

and large language model applications. The framework also provides a structured mechanism for

identifying, assessing and mapping applicable CERT-In requirements, sector-specific

cybersecurity obligations, contractual security requirements and other external requirements into

the audit criteria and Statement of Applicability.



The Guidelines are intended for use by government organisations, public sector entities, critical

infrastructure operators, regulated entities, private organisations, AI developers, AI service

providers, internal and external auditors, CERT-In empanelled cybersecurity auditing

organisations, risk and compliance functions and other stakeholders involved in the development,

procurement, deployment or oversight of AI systems.



2.1 What This Framework Provides



This document delivers a comprehensive, actionable and internationally aligned auditing

framework structured across the following pillars:

2.2 Guiding Principles



The framework is anchored on seven foundational principles for secure, ethical and auditable AI

 vii. Resilience and Continuous Assurance

    Guidelines. Consistent definitions are essential to ensure uniform interpretation by auditors,

    auditees, AI system owners, security teams and other relevant stakeholders across all audit

    domains and compliance contexts.

4. Purpose & Scope



    This section defines the objectives, boundaries and applicability of the AI Security Auditing

    Guidelines. It establishes what the framework aims to achieve, who it applies to, which AI systems

    and data categories fall within scope.



   4.1 Purpose



    The purpose of these Guidelines is to establish a consistent, risk-based and auditable mechanism

    for evaluating the security, governance and responsible operation of AI systems throughout their

    lifecycle.

    The framework aims to:



      Ensure secure, ethical and auditable AI adoption: Define consistent audit requirements

      applicable to AI systems regardless of whether they are developed internally, procured from

      third parties, consumed through APIs or cloud services, or derived from open-source or

      foundation models.



      Enable risk-based assurance: Determine the depth, frequency and technical intensity of an

      audit based on the AI system’s potential impact, autonomy, data sensitivity, scale, criticality,

      adversarial exposure and explainability.



      Assess AI-specific security risks: Provide procedures for assessing threats including data

      and model poisoning, adversarial manipulation, model extraction, model inversion, prompt

      injection, unsafe tool use, supply-chain compromise, insecure AI APIs and unauthorised model

      modification.



      Verify AI lifecycle controls: Assess governance and security controls covering data

      preparation, model development, validation, deployment, operation, monitoring, retraining,

      change management and decommissioning.



      Improve audit consistency and reproducibility: Establish common expectations for audit

      scoping, evidence collection, technical testing, sampling, working papers, finding classification,

      reporting and remediation verification.



      Support interoperability with recognised standards: Facilitate alignment with relevant AI

      management, cybersecurity, risk-management and technical-assurance standards and

      frameworks.



   4.2 Strategic Objectives



    The framework is designed around the following technical and assurance objectives:
```
